Oriental Sentinel Services · developer study guide

Rebuilding OSSI the senior way

Guards clock in with a selfie and GPS, supervisors approve leave and overtime, accounting turns attendance into payslips. This guide walks through every feature of ossi_official_site: why it is built that way, the real code (read straight from the repository), the questions you'd ask, and something to try.

Reading order

Chapters 00 to 04 are the foundation every feature leans on: read them first. After that, each feature chapter stands alone. Every code folder below is the file as it exists in the repo today; open it, then open the same file in your editor and follow along. 00

Architecture

Every feature follows one path. A route checks a gate, a thin Livewire component validates and re-checks the gate, an Action applies the business rule inside a transaction and writes the audit entry. Reads go through a Query that fetches in bulk and hands plain data to a pure calculator.

flowchart LR
  B[Browser] -->|wire:click| R[Route + can: gate]
  R --> C[Livewire component
validate + authorize]
  C -->|write| A[Action
DB transaction]
  A --> M[(Models / MySQL)]
  A --> L[AuditLogger]
  C -->|read| Q[Query
bulk fetch]
  Q --> M
  Q --> P[Pure calculator]
FolderHoldsHouse rule (enforced by an arch test)
app/ActionsOne class per write: approve, punch, generatefinal, one public handle()
app/QueriesScreen read modelsfinal, handle(), no query per row
app/ServicesCalculators, photo store, geocoder, audit loggerCalculators use no facades or models
app/DataValues passed between layersfinal readonly
app/EnumsRoles, gates, statusesBacked enums, stored as short strings
app/LivewirePage componentsNo DB facade: queries live elsewhere
Question you'd askAnswer
Why Actions instead of putting logic in the component?The same rule is reused by the seeder, a console command and tests, and a component re-renders constantly. An Action is a plain class you can call and test without a browser.
Why do Actions throw ValidationException?Livewire catches it and shows the message under the matching field, so components need no try/catch. "Already clocked in" lands under punch.
What is "pure" about the calculators?They take every input as arguments and return a value. No database, no clock, no config. That is why the payroll formula can be unit-tested with hand-written rates.
01

Fortify & HR-only registration

Yes, Fortify is the right tool here. It is headless: it owns the login, reset, verification and two-factor routes and their security details, while we write the views and one hook, CreateNewUser. That hook is where "only employees HR has registered may create an account" is enforced.

Fortify gives usThrottled login, session regeneration, signed verification links, reset tokens, TOTP two-factor with recovery codes.
We addBlade views, the HR-only claim rule, a block on resigned staff, queued emails, a friendlier logout message.
Every attempt is loggedSuccess or failure, with the reason, in the audit log. The person registering only ever sees one generic message.
sequenceDiagram
  participant HR
  participant DB as employee_profiles
  participant E as Employee
  participant F as Fortify /register
  participant C as ClaimEmployeeAccount
  HR->>DB: Add employee (number + email), user_id NULL
  E->>F: employee number, email, password
  F->>C: CreateNewUser (rate limit by IP)
  C->>DB: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
  alt number exists, unclaimed, email matches, still employed
    C->>DB: create user + Employee role, link profile
    C-->>E: signed in, verification email queued
  else any check fails
    C-->>E: one generic error
    Note over C: audit registration.failed + reason
  end

Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Actions\Auth;

use App\Actions\Payroll\EnrollCashBond;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\RegistrationFailure;
use App\Enums\Role;
use App\Models\EmployeeProfile;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\UpdateNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use App\Support\EmployeeNumber;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Notification;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Registration is not "anyone can sign up". HR adds the employee first
 * (employee number + email); registering CLAIMS that record:
 *
 *   1. the employee number exists,
 *   2. nobody has claimed it yet,
 *   3. the email matches the one HR recorded,
 *   4. the employee is still active,
 *   5. no other account already uses the email.
 *
 * Every attempt, successful or not, is written to the audit log. A failure
 * always shows the SAME message, so the form can't be used to discover which
 * employee numbers exist.
 */
final class ClaimEmployeeAccount
{
    public const FAILURE_MESSAGE = 'We could not match these details to an employee record from HR. Check your employee number and the email you gave HR, or contact HR.';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
        private readonly EnrollCashBond $enrollCashBond,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @throws ValidationException
     */
    public function handle(string $employeeNumber, string $email, string $password): User
    {
        $employeeNumber = EmployeeNumber::normalize($employeeNumber);
        $email = Str::lower(trim($email));

        /** @var array{0: User|RegistrationFailure, 1: EmployeeProfile|null} $result */
        $result = DB::transaction(function () use ($employeeNumber, $email, $password): array {
            // Locked so two people racing to claim the same number can't both win.
            $profile = EmployeeProfile::query()
                ->where('employee_number', $employeeNumber)
                ->lockForUpdate()
                ->first();

            $failure = $this->check($profile, $email);

            if ($failure !== null || $profile === null) {
                return [$failure ?? RegistrationFailure::UnknownEmployeeNumber, $profile];
            }

            $user = User::create([
                'name' => $profile->name,
                // A test account keeps the number's capitals, as HR's record shows it.
                'email' => $profile->is_test_account ? $profile->email : $email,
                'password' => $password,
            ]);
            $user->roles()->create(['role' => Role::Employee]);

            // A role the Super Admin set in advance (Roles & Access → Not registered yet).
            $pendingRole = $profile->pending_role;
            if ($pendingRole !== null) {
                $user->roles()->create(['role' => $pendingRole]);
                $user->forceFill(['operations_region' => $pendingRole === Role::SatelliteOperations ? $profile->pending_region : null])->save();
                $profile->forceFill(['pending_role' => null, 'pending_region' => null]);
            }

            // A test account's address has no mailbox (HR chose it): confirmed now, no link sent.
            if ($profile->is_test_account) {
                $user->forceFill(['email_verified_at' => now()])->save();
            }

            $profile->user()->associate($user);
            $profile->save();

            // Guards pay a cash bond from their first payslip (₱100 a cut-off), refunded in final pay.
            if ($profile->hasDeployment()) {
                $this->enrollCashBond->handle($user, $user);
            }

            $this->audit->record(
                AuditArea::Auth,
                'registration.succeeded',
                "{$profile->name} registered an account",
                $profile,
                ['employee_number' => $employeeNumber, 'email' => $email, 'role' => $pendingRole?->value],
                causer: $user,
            );

            // HR knows onboarding is done: they can now be deployed, rostered and paid.
            Notification::send(User::query()->notifiable([Role::Hr])->whereKeyNot($user->id)->get(), new UpdateNotice(
                "{$profile->name} registered",
                "Employee no. {$profile->employee_number} created their account".($pendingRole !== null ? " and has the {$pendingRole->label()} role" : '').'.',
                route('employees.show', $profile), 'user-plus',
            ));

            return [$user, $profile];
        });

        [$outcome, $profile] = $result;

        if ($outcome instanceof RegistrationFailure) {
            // Outside the transaction on purpose: the failure must be recorded even though nothing else is saved.
            $this->audit->record(
                AuditArea::Auth,
                'registration.failed',
                'Registration refused',
                $profile,
                ['employee_number' => $employeeNumber, 'email' => $email, 'reason' => $outcome->value],
            );

            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['employee_number' => self::FAILURE_MESSAGE]);
        }

        return $outcome;
    }

    private function check(?EmployeeProfile $profile, string $email): ?RegistrationFailure
    {
        return match (true) {
            $profile === null => RegistrationFailure::UnknownEmployeeNumber,
            $profile->isClaimed() => RegistrationFailure::AlreadyClaimed,
            ! hash_equals(Str::lower($profile->email), $email) => RegistrationFailure::EmailMismatch,
            ! $profile->employment_status->isActive() => RegistrationFailure::NotActive,
            User::query()->whereRaw('lower(email) = ?', [$email])->exists() => RegistrationFailure::EmailTaken,
            default => null,
        };
    }
}
app/Actions/Fortify/CreateNewUser.php50 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Actions\Fortify;

use App\Actions\Auth\ClaimEmployeeAccount;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\RateLimiter;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use Laravel\Fortify\Contracts\CreatesNewUsers;

/**
 * Fortify's registration hook. It only handles HTTP concerns (input shape,
 * rate limiting by IP); the business rule lives in ClaimEmployeeAccount.
 */
class CreateNewUser implements CreatesNewUsers
{
    use PasswordValidationRules;

    public function __construct(private readonly ClaimEmployeeAccount $claimEmployeeAccount) {}

    /**
     * @param  array<string, string>  $input
     *
     * @throws ValidationException
     */
    public function create(array $input): User
    {
        $throttleKey = 'register|'.request()->ip();
        $maxAttempts = (int) config('security.registration.max_attempts');

        if (RateLimiter::tooManyAttempts($throttleKey, $maxAttempts)) {
            $minutes = (int) ceil(RateLimiter::availableIn($throttleKey) / 60);

            throw ValidationException::withMessages([
                'employee_number' => "Too many registration attempts. Please try again in {$minutes} minute(s).",
            ]);
        }

        Validator::make($input, [
            'employee_number' => ['required', 'string', 'max:50'],
            'email' => ['required', 'string', 'email', 'max:255'],
            'password' => $this->passwordRules(),
        ])->validate();

        RateLimiter::hit($throttleKey, (int) config('security.registration.decay_seconds'));

        return $this->claimEmployeeAccount->handle($input['employee_number'], $input['email'], $input['password']);
    }
}
app/Providers/FortifyServiceProvider.php91 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Providers;

use App\Actions\Fortify\CreateNewUser;
use App\Actions\Fortify\ResetUserPassword;
use App\Actions\Fortify\UpdateUserPassword;
use App\Actions\Fortify\UpdateUserProfileInformation;
use App\Http\Responses\LogoutResponse;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Cache\RateLimiting\Limit;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\RateLimiter;
use Illuminate\Support\ServiceProvider;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use Laravel\Fortify\Contracts\LogoutResponse as LogoutResponseContract;
use Laravel\Fortify\Fortify;

/**
 * Fortify is headless: it owns the auth ROUTES and logic (login throttling,
 * session regeneration, password reset tokens, email verification, 2FA),
 * and we only supply views and a few hooks.
 */
class FortifyServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function register(): void
    {
        $this->app->singleton(LogoutResponseContract::class, LogoutResponse::class);
    }

    public function boot(): void
    {
        $this->registerViews();

        Fortify::createUsersUsing(CreateNewUser::class);
        Fortify::updateUserProfileInformationUsing(UpdateUserProfileInformation::class);
        Fortify::updateUserPasswordsUsing(UpdateUserPassword::class);
        Fortify::resetUserPasswordsUsing(ResetUserPassword::class);

        Fortify::authenticateUsing($this->authenticate(...));

        RateLimiter::for('login', function (Request $request) {
            $email = Str::transliterate(Str::lower($request->string(Fortify::username())->toString()));

            return [
                // One account: 5 tries a minute (guessing one person's password).
                Limit::perMinute(5)->by($email.'|'.$request->ip()),
                // One IP: 20 tries a minute across all emails (one password, many accounts).
                Limit::perMinute(20)->by('ip|'.$request->ip()),
            ];
        });

        RateLimiter::for('two-factor', fn (Request $request) => Limit::perMinute(5)->by((string) $request->session()->get('login.id')));
    }

    /**
     * Same check as Fortify's default, plus one rule: people HR has marked
     * resigned or terminated can't sign in, even with the right password.
     */
    private function authenticate(Request $request): ?User
    {
        $user = User::query()
            ->with('employeeProfile')
            // In any case: a test account keeps its number's capitals (260627PAM-0950@test.invalid).
            ->whereRaw('lower(email) = ?', [Str::lower($request->string('email')->toString())])
            ->first();

        if ($user === null || ! Hash::check($request->string('password')->toString(), $user->password)) {
            return null;
        }

        if ($user->employeeProfile !== null && ! $user->employeeProfile->employment_status->isActive()) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages([Fortify::username() => 'This account has been deactivated. Please contact HR.']);
        }

        return $user;
    }

    private function registerViews(): void
    {
        Fortify::loginView(fn () => view('auth.login'));
        Fortify::registerView(fn () => view('auth.register'));
        Fortify::requestPasswordResetLinkView(fn () => view('auth.forgot-password'));
        Fortify::resetPasswordView(fn (Request $request) => view('auth.reset-password', ['request' => $request]));
        Fortify::verifyEmailView(fn () => view('auth.verify-email'));
        Fortify::twoFactorChallengeView(fn () => view('auth.two-factor-challenge'));
        Fortify::confirmPasswordView(fn () => view('auth.confirm-password'));
    }
}
Question you'd askAnswer
Why the same error for every failure?"That number exists but the email is wrong" tells a stranger which numbers are real. HR still sees the exact reason in the audit log.
A pilot tester has no real email. What does HR do?Switch on Test account (no real email) when adding them (on Add only; an x-ui.switch, a real checkbox with role="switch" drawn as a sliding track). The record's email is made from the employee number at test.invalid, a domain reserved so it never delivers (e.g. 260627PAM-0950@test.invalid, capitals kept in the record and the account; sign-in matches the email in any case). They register with it, ClaimEmployeeAccount confirms the email at once (no link to click), and User::routeNotificationForMail() returns null so Laravel's mail channel sends nothing there; in-app notices still show. A "Test account" badge marks them on Employees, to clean up before going live. The trade-off: nobody proves they own that address, so it's only for testers.
Why is the failure logged after the transaction?The failure path throws, and a throw rolls back everything inside the transaction, including an audit row written there.
Why lock the profile row?Two people submitting the same employee number at the same moment could both pass the "unclaimed" check without it.
Why doesn't the form ask for a name?HR's record is the source of truth. The account takes the name HR typed.
Why a rate limiter in CreateNewUser?Fortify's register route has none, and this form checks an identifier, so it could be used to guess employee numbers.
Why queue the verification email?Gmail's SMTP handshake can take seconds. Queued, the request returns at once; composer dev runs the worker locally.
Try it
  1. Open /register, enter 999999-XXX-9999 with any email. Note the message.
  2. Sign in as the super admin and open Audit Log: find registration.failed with reason unknown_employee_number.
  3. Register with 250115-SEC-3001 / juan.delacruz@example.test: you land on "Confirm your email".
02

Roles & gates

Ten roles and a set of gates, both PHP enums. The company's leadership is two roles, President and Vice President, with the same access everywhere through Role::leadership() (there's no "Executive": the company doesn't use the word), so either one can approve. They and the Super Admin are accounts without an employee record (Role::withoutEmployeeRecord()): no employee number, payroll, attendance or headcount, created from the console rather than registered, and Roles & Access won't give these roles to someone on payroll. Their My Profile says so in a plain note ("This is a Super Admin account, not an employee: it has no employee number ... It can still open and manage every part of the system": not being an employee doesn't take any access away) instead of the "HR hasn't set up your employee record yet" warning meant for new staff. One match in Ability::roles() decides who opens what. The service provider turns each case into a Gate::define(), routes use Ability::X->middleware(), and every write calls $this->authorize() again. Where a role may look but not touch, viewing and changing are separate gates.

RoleIn one line
Super AdminEverything: settings, holidays, clients, roles, audit log.
PresidentLeads the company: monitors, posts announcements, approves office staff's leave, overtime and reimbursements, signs final pay.
Vice PresidentThe same access as the President, so either one can approve.
AdminDocuments, licenses, client and legal documents, training, holidays; views employees.
HROnboarding and records, guards' leave, complaints.
AccountingPayroll, daily rates, 13th month, Borrow Load approval; views employees.
Operation HQMonitors leave, approves overtime, runs the Duty Roster, assigns relievers.
Satellite OperationThe same for one region (roster included), plus Change deployment (client, post, shift).
DeveloperReads the audit log.
EmployeeSelf-service.
Monitor ≠ decidemonitor-requests opens the lists; review-field-leave, review-office-leave and review-overtime decide. A row you can't decide says who does.
Office leave → President or VPReviewLeaveRequest::requiredAbility() reads the requester's is_office_staff. No HR profile counts as office.
One regionSatellite has users.operations_region. visibleTo($viewer) scopes lists; canSeeProfile() guards single records and Actions.
Operations: guards onlyThe same rule also hides office staff from anyone without view-office-staff, which means Operation HQ (a Satellite sees only its region's guards anyway). Operations looks after guards, and office staff answer to the President or Vice President. So the Employees list and its filter, the Attendance Log, and a record opened by its link all follow one rule.

<?php

namespace App\Enums;

/**
 * Every gate in the system. Each route requires one, and every write
 * re-checks it (see App\Livewire\Concerns\AuthorizesAbility).
 *
 * Viewing and changing are separate gates where a role may look but not
 * touch (the President or Vice President monitors; Accounting views the employee list).
 *
 * AppServiceProvider defines one Gate per case from roles(), so this match
 * is the single source of truth for "who can open what".
 */
enum Ability: string
{
    case AccessEmployerArea = 'access-employer-area';
    case SuperviseAttendance = 'supervise-attendance';
    case MonitorRequests = 'monitor-requests';
    case ReviewFieldLeave = 'review-field-leave';
    case ReviewOfficeLeave = 'review-office-leave';
    case EndorseGuardLeave = 'endorse-guard-leave';
    case ReviewOvertime = 'review-overtime';
    case ReviewOfficeOvertime = 'review-office-overtime';
    case ViewPeople = 'view-people';
    case ManagePeople = 'manage-people';
    case ViewPayRates = 'view-pay-rates';
    case DeployGuards = 'deploy-guards';
    case ManagePayroll = 'manage-payroll';
    case ConfigureSystem = 'configure-system';
    case ConfigureHolidays = 'configure-holidays';
    case ViewSystemLogs = 'view-system-logs';
    case PublishContent = 'publish-content';
    case ManageLoadRequests = 'manage-load-requests';
    case ApprovePayrollAdjustments = 'approve-payroll-adjustments';
    case ManageRelievers = 'manage-relievers';
    case ManageRoster = 'manage-roster';
    case ManagePatrols = 'manage-patrols';
    case MonitorOfficeAway = 'monitor-office-away';
    case ManageDocuments = 'manage-documents';
    case ManageTraining = 'manage-training';
    case HandleComplaints = 'handle-complaints';
    case HandleHrComplaints = 'handle-hr-complaints';
    case ManagePolicies = 'manage-policies';
    case ViewOrganization = 'view-organization';
    case ViewOfficeStaff = 'view-office-staff';
    case HandleResignations = 'handle-resignations';
    case HandleHrResignations = 'handle-hr-resignations';
    case PrepareFinalPay = 'prepare-final-pay';
    case SignFinalPay = 'sign-final-pay';
    case GiveMerits = 'give-merits';
    case ManageMeritTypes = 'manage-merit-types';
    case IssueNoticesToExplain = 'issue-notices-to-explain';
    case ApproveReimbursements = 'approve-reimbursements';
    case ViewReimbursements = 'view-reimbursements';
    case FileDeploymentClaims = 'file-deployment-claims';
    case ManageGuardPhones = 'manage-guard-phones';
    case ManageClients = 'manage-clients';
    case ManageOffices = 'manage-offices';
    case SeeBirthdays = 'see-birthdays';
    case ViewPettyCash = 'view-petty-cash';
    case ManagePettyCash = 'manage-petty-cash';
    case ManageRadios = 'manage-radios';
    case ManageReferrals = 'manage-referrals';
    case IssueEquipment = 'issue-equipment';
    case ManageEquipmentItems = 'manage-equipment-items';

    /**
     * @return list<Role>
     */
    public function roles(): array
    {
        return match ($this) {
            // The dashboard. Each section on it has its own Ability (what's waiting for
            // you, the people by area, today's attendance), so each role sees its part.
            self::AccessEmployerArea => [Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin, ...Role::leadership(), Role::Hr, Role::Accounting, Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations],
            // The attendance log (read-only).
            self::SuperviseAttendance => [Role::Admin, Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin, ...Role::leadership(), Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations],
            // The leave and overtime lists. Deciding needs one of the review gates below.
            self::MonitorRequests => [Role::Admin, Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin, ...Role::leadership(), Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations],
            // Guards' (field staff) leave: HR has the final say, after Operations endorses it.
            self::ReviewFieldLeave => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Endorsing a guard's leave up the chain: the region's Satellite Operation, then Operation HQ.
            self::EndorseGuardLeave => [Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::OperationsHq],
            // Office staff's leave: the President or Vice President, not HR.
            self::ReviewOfficeLeave => [...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Guards' overtime.
            self::ReviewOvertime => [Role::Hr, Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin, Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations],
            // Office staff's overtime: the President or Vice President, like their leave. Only they (and
            // the Super Admin) see office staff's leave and overtime requests at all.
            self::ReviewOfficeOvertime => [...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The employee list and records, read-only. Editing needs ManagePeople.
            self::ViewPeople => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin, Role::Admin, Role::Accounting, ...Role::leadership(), Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations],
            self::ManagePeople => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The pay rate on an employee record (Accounting sets it on Daily Rates).
            self::ViewPayRates => [Role::Hr, Role::Accounting, Role::SuperAdmin, ...Role::leadership()],
            // A guard's client, post and shift (Satellite Operation: in their region only).
            self::DeployGuards => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin, Role::SatelliteOperations],
            self::ManagePayroll => [Role::Accounting, Role::SuperAdmin],
            self::ConfigureSystem => [Role::SuperAdmin],
            self::ConfigureHolidays => [Role::SuperAdmin, Role::Admin],
            self::ViewSystemLogs => [Role::Developer, Role::SuperAdmin],
            self::PublishContent => [Role::Admin, Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin, ...Role::leadership()],
            self::ManageLoadRequests => [Role::Admin, Role::Accounting, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The second person on large payroll adjustments; never the one who made it.
            self::ApprovePayrollAdjustments => [Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Absence notices and relievers (Satellite Operation: its region).
            self::ManageRelievers => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The Duty Roster and manual attendance (Satellite Operation: its region).
            self::ManageRoster => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Checkpoints, patrol rounds and guards away from the post (Satellite: its region).
            self::ManagePatrols => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Office staff out of the office: the President or Vice President, like their leave.
            // HR for the office staff it heads, Operation HQ for its Satellites (App\Support\Heads);
            // the President or VP see everyone's (and approve HR's).
            self::MonitorOfficeAway => [...Role::leadership(), Role::Hr, Role::OperationsHq, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Company documents, licenses and client / legal documents.
            self::ManageDocuments => [Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin],
            self::ManageTraining => [Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Complaints are confidential: HR (and Super Admin) only.
            self::HandleComplaints => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // ...except those filed by HR staff, which HR never sees: the President or Vice President's,
            // like HR's own leave and overtime.
            self::HandleHrComplaints => [...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Writing the Company Policy page; everyone reads it.
            self::ManagePolicies => [Role::Admin, Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The company's structure, from the President or Vice President down to the guards at each client.
            self::ViewOrganization => [...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Office staff in the dashboard's numbers, charts and DTR. Operations (HQ and
            // Satellite) look after guards only, so theirs counts guards: all, or their region's.
            self::ViewOfficeStaff => [Role::SuperAdmin, ...Role::leadership(), Role::Admin, Role::Hr, Role::Accounting],
            // Resignations: accepting the last day and the clearance checklist. HR's job...
            self::HandleResignations => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // ...except an HR member's own, which the President or Vice President handles (like their leave and complaints).
            self::HandleHrResignations => [...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Final pay: Accounting prepares the statement (and the cash bonds behind it)...
            self::PrepareFinalPay => [Role::Accounting, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // ...and Accounting and the President or Vice President sign it, they last (FinalPay::SIGNERS). Only they see the amounts. Super Admin can look, not sign.
            self::SignFinalPay => [Role::Accounting, ...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Merits and demerits: whoever supervises the person (MeritRecord::canGive): Operations
            // for guards (a Satellite in its region), HR for anyone, the President or Vice President for HR staff.
            self::GiveMerits => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::Hr, ...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The list of merit and demerit types and their points.
            self::ManageMeritTypes => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Notices to Explain (due process): issued and decided by whoever supervises the person
            // (NoticeToExplain::canIssue): Operations for guards, HR for office staff, the President or Vice President
            // for HR staff. HR and the President or Vice President also read them all (canView).
            self::IssueNoticesToExplain => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::Hr, ...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Office staff's reimbursements: the President or Vice President approves (like their leave)...
            self::ApproveReimbursements => [...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // ...and Accounting sees them all (it pays them on the next payslip).
            self::ViewReimbursements => [...Role::leadership(), Role::Accounting, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Roadmap 5: Operations files a guard's deployment cost (a Satellite: its region's guards).
            self::FileDeploymentClaims => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // A guard's company phone: told when they clock in on another one, and can make a
            // replacement phone theirs or forget the old one (a Satellite: its region's guards).
            self::ManageGuardPhones => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Clients (the sites guards are deployed to) and their location and geofence: Operation HQ or
            // Admin sets them up before HR onboards a guard there. Satellite Operation, below HQ, doesn't.
            self::ManageClients => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // OSSI's own offices (head office, branches) where office staff clock in: company
            // premises, which Admin looks after. Operation HQ stays with clients.
            self::ManageOffices => [Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Birthday reminders and "Birthdays this month": HR for everyone; Operations for guards
            // (a Satellite: its region's), as with other people matters of the guards they supervise.
            self::SeeBirthdays => [Role::Hr, Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Petty cash: every fund and its expenses, read-only (the President or Vice President monitors)...
            self::ViewPettyCash => [Role::Accounting, ...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin],
            // ...Accounting sets up the funds and releases replenishments. A fund's custodian keeps its
            // expenses without this (PettyCashFund::custodianOf).
            self::ManagePettyCash => [Role::Accounting, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The NTC radio masterlist: Admin keeps company property and licenses, Operation HQ the
            // radios at the posts.
            self::ManageRadios => [Role::Admin, Role::OperationsHq, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Referrals: HR links them to the hire (or says not hired), and sets the bonus and days.
            self::ManageReferrals => [Role::Hr, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // Uniforms, radios and gear (the owner's choice, 2026-10-23): Operations issues to the
            // guards it deploys (a Satellite: its region's), Admin to office staff
            // (EquipmentIssue::canIssueTo says which person).
            self::IssueEquipment => [Role::OperationsHq, Role::SatelliteOperations, Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin],
            // The item list and prices: Admin keeps the stock list.
            self::ManageEquipmentItems => [Role::Admin, Role::SuperAdmin],
        };
    }

    /**
     * Route middleware string, e.g. "can:manage-payroll".
     */
    public function middleware(): string
    {
        return 'can:'.$this->value;
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Enums;

/**
 * The roles. Stored as strings in `user_roles.role`; a user may hold several.
 *
 * Presentation (label, colour, description) lives here too, so a new role is a
 * one-file change. Access itself is decided by Ability, never by checking a
 * role name in a view or component.
 */
enum Role: string
{
    case SuperAdmin = 'super-admin';
    // The company's leadership (was one "Executive" role until 2026-10-20). Same access for both:
    // either one approves, so a request doesn't wait while one is away. See leadership().
    case President = 'president';
    case VicePresident = 'vice-president';
    case Admin = 'admin';
    case Hr = 'hr';
    case Accounting = 'accounting';
    case OperationsHq = 'operations-hq';
    case SatelliteOperations = 'satellite-operations';
    case Developer = 'developer';
    case Employee = 'employee';

    public function label(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::SuperAdmin => 'Super Admin',
            self::President => 'President',
            self::VicePresident => 'Vice President',
            self::Admin => 'Admin',
            self::Hr => 'HR',
            self::Accounting => 'Accounting',
            self::OperationsHq => 'Operation HQ',
            self::SatelliteOperations => 'Satellite Operation',
            self::Developer => 'Developer',
            self::Employee => 'Employee',
        };
    }

    /**
     * A tone name for <x-ui.badge>. Tailwind classes stay in Blade, because
     * Tailwind only scans the views for class names.
     */
    public function tone(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::SuperAdmin => 'purple',
            self::President, self::VicePresident => 'orange',
            self::Admin => 'blue',
            self::Hr => 'emerald',
            self::Accounting => 'indigo',
            self::OperationsHq => 'sky',
            self::SatelliteOperations => 'teal',
            self::Developer => 'amber',
            self::Employee => 'gray',
        };
    }

    public function description(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::SuperAdmin => 'Full system control: every feature, system settings, holidays, clients, roles and the audit log.',
            self::President => 'Leads the company: monitors everything, approves office staff\'s leave, overtime and reimbursements, signs final pay. Paid outside this payroll.',
            self::VicePresident => 'The same access as the President, so either one can approve. Paid outside this payroll.',
            self::Admin => 'Sets up clients; company documents, licenses, client and legal documents, guard training, holidays and the employee list.',
            self::Hr => 'Onboards employees, keeps their records, approves guards\' leave, and handles complaints.',
            self::Accounting => 'Runs payroll, daily rates and 13th month pay, approves borrowed load, and views the employee list.',
            self::OperationsHq => 'Head of operations: sets up clients, monitors leave, approves overtime, and finds relievers for absent guards.',
            self::SatelliteOperations => 'One region: monitors it, assigns detachments and posts, changes shifts, finds relievers, approves overtime.',
            self::Developer => 'Reads the audit log for support and debugging. No HR or payroll access.',
            self::Employee => 'Clocks in and out, files leave and overtime, and views their own payslips.',
        };
    }

    /**
     * Whether holding this role shows every employee. Satellite Operation
     * sees only its own region (set on Roles & Access); Developer and
     * Employee see no one else's records at all.
     */
    public function seesWholeCompany(): bool
    {
        return ! in_array($this, [self::SatelliteOperations, self::Developer, self::Employee], true);
    }

    /**
     * Roles paid outside this payroll (the owner/director level): no payslip,
     * no attendance, no DTR row, no daily rate needed, even with an HR record.
     *
     * @return list<self>
     */
    public static function paidOutsidePayroll(): array
    {
        return self::withoutEmployeeRecord();
    }

    /**
     * Accounts that aren't employees here: no HR record, no employee number, no payroll,
     * attendance or headcount (company decision, 2026-10-21). The Super Admin is a system
     * account; the President and Vice President are paid outside this payroll. Someone who
     * is also on payroll keeps a separate, ordinary account for that.
     *
     * @return list<self>
     */
    public static function withoutEmployeeRecord(): array
    {
        return [self::SuperAdmin, ...self::leadership()];
    }

    /**
     * The President and the Vice President: the same access everywhere (they were one
     * "Executive" role). Use this wherever either may act, e.g. `[...Role::leadership(), Role::SuperAdmin]`.
     *
     * @return list<self>
     */
    public static function leadership(): array
    {
        return [self::President, self::VicePresident];
    }

    /** "the President or Vice President": how the screens name who decides. */
    public const LEADERSHIP_LABEL = 'the President or Vice President';
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Leave;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\RequestStatus;
use App\Models\LeaveRequest;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\RequestDecided;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use App\Support\Heads;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;
use InvalidArgumentException;

/**
 * Who decides depends on who's asking: HR decides guards' leave (final),
 * once the region's Satellite Operation and Operation HQ have endorsed it
 * (EndorseLeaveRequest); an office staffer's head decides theirs (Heads: HR for Admin and
 * others; Operation HQ for a Satellite; the President or VP for HR, Operation HQ, Accounting).
 */
final class ReviewLeaveRequest
{
    public function __construct(private readonly AuditLogger $audit) {}

    /**
     * Why this reviewer can't decide it, or null when they can. The list shows the same text
     * in place of the Review button. A guard's: HR, once Operations has endorsed it. An office
     * staffer's: their head (Heads). No HR profile (e.g. a Super Admin's own account) counts
     * as office staff.
     */
    public static function blockedReason(LeaveRequest $leaveRequest, User $reviewer): ?string
    {
        $leaveRequest->loadMissing('user.employeeProfile');
        $office = $leaveRequest->user->isOfficeStaff();

        return match (true) {
            $leaveRequest->user_id === $reviewer->id => 'You cannot review your own request.',
            $office && ! Heads::isHeadOf($reviewer, $leaveRequest->user) => 'Their head decides it: '.Heads::label($leaveRequest->user).'.',
            ! $office && ! $reviewer->can(Ability::ReviewFieldLeave->value) => 'Guards\' leave is approved by HR.',
            // A guard's leave reaches HR only once Operation HQ has endorsed it.
            ! $office && $leaveRequest->stage !== null && $leaveRequest->stage->endorses() => "Waiting for {$leaveRequest->stage->label()} to endorse it.",
            ! $reviewer->canSeeEmployee($leaveRequest->user) => 'This employee is outside your region.',
            default => null,
        };
    }

    /**
     * Why it can't be approved yet (rejecting is still possible): the proof it
     * needs isn't attached. The review box shows the same text.
     */
    public static function approvalBlockedReason(LeaveRequest $leaveRequest): ?string
    {
        $leaveRequest->loadMissing('documents');

        return $leaveRequest->missingDocument()
            ? 'Waiting for the document: '.lcfirst((string) $leaveRequest->documentNeeded()).'. They attach it on My Leave.'
            : null;
    }

    public function handle(LeaveRequest $leaveRequest, User $reviewer, RequestStatus $decision, ?string $note): LeaveRequest
    {
        if (! in_array($decision, [RequestStatus::Approved, RequestStatus::Rejected], true)) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException('A review either approves or rejects.');
        }

        // Separation of duties (nobody approves their own leave), who decides what, and the region.
        if (($reason = self::blockedReason($leaveRequest, $reviewer)) !== null) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['review' => $reason]);
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($leaveRequest, $reviewer, $decision, $note) {
            // Locked: two supervisors clicking at once can't both decide.
            $locked = LeaveRequest::query()->with('user')->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($leaveRequest->id);

            if ($locked->status !== RequestStatus::Pending) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['review' => 'This leave request has already been reviewed.']);
            }

            // Re-checked on the locked row: an endorsement may have just moved it (or not yet).
            if (($reason = self::blockedReason($locked, $reviewer)) !== null) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['review' => $reason]);
            }

            // Proof first (a medical certificate, a birth certificate…): no approving without it.
            if ($decision === RequestStatus::Approved && ($reason = self::approvalBlockedReason($locked)) !== null) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['review' => $reason]);
            }

            $locked->forceFill([
                'status' => $decision,
                'stage' => null,
                'reviewed_by' => $reviewer->id,
                'reviewed_at' => now(),
                'review_note' => $note,
            ])->save();

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Leave, 'leave.'.$decision->value, ucfirst($decision->value)." leave of {$locked->user->name} ({$locked->dateRangeLabel()})", $locked, [
                'old' => ['status' => RequestStatus::Pending->value],
                'new' => ['status' => $decision->value, 'review_note' => $note],
            ], causer: $reviewer);

            // The person who asked hears the answer.
            $locked->user->notify(new RequestDecided($locked->setRelation('reviewer', $reviewer)));

            return $locked;
        });
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Roles;

use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\Region;
use App\Enums\Role;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Models\UserRole;
use App\Notifications\UpdateNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Replaces a user's roles. Two guard rails stop the system locking itself out:
 * you can't remove your own Super Admin role, and the last Super Admin stays.
 *
 * A Satellite Operation must cover a region; without that role the region is
 * cleared, so a stale one can't limit anybody later.
 */
final class SyncUserRoles
{
    public function __construct(private readonly AuditLogger $audit) {}

    /**
     * @param  list<Role>  $roles
     */
    public function handle(User $target, array $roles, User $actor, ?Region $region = null): void
    {
        $new = array_values(array_unique(array_map(fn (Role $role) => $role->value, $roles)));
        $old = array_map(fn (Role $role) => $role->value, $target->roleList());

        sort($new);
        sort($old);

        $region = in_array(Role::SatelliteOperations->value, $new, true) ? $region : null;

        if (in_array(Role::SatelliteOperations->value, $new, true) && $region === null) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['region' => 'Choose the region this Satellite Operation covers.']);
        }

        $oldRegion = $target->operations_region;

        if ($new === $old && $oldRegion === $region) {
            return;
        }

        // Super Admin, President and Vice President are accounts without an HR record: an
        // employee on payroll who also needs one of them gets a second, separate account.
        $noRecord = array_map(fn (Role $role) => $role->value, Role::withoutEmployeeRecord());
        $adding = array_intersect(array_diff($new, $old), $noRecord);

        if ($adding !== [] && $target->employeeProfile()->exists()) {
            $names = implode(', ', array_map(fn (string $value) => Role::from($value)->label(), $adding));
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['roles' => "{$names} can't go to someone with an employee record: those accounts are outside payroll. Create a separate account for that role (php artisan app:create-super-admin)."]);
        }

        $losesSuperAdmin = in_array(Role::SuperAdmin->value, $old, true) && ! in_array(Role::SuperAdmin->value, $new, true);

        if ($losesSuperAdmin && $target->is($actor)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['roles' => 'You cannot remove your own Super Admin role.']);
        }

        DB::transaction(function () use ($target, $new, $old, $region, $oldRegion, $losesSuperAdmin, $actor) {
            if ($losesSuperAdmin) {
                $superAdmins = UserRole::query()->where('role', Role::SuperAdmin)->lockForUpdate()->count();

                if ($superAdmins <= 1) {
                    throw ValidationException::withMessages(['roles' => 'At least one Super Admin must remain.']);
                }
            }

            $target->roles()->whereNotIn('role', $new)->delete();

            foreach (array_diff($new, $old) as $role) {
                $target->roles()->create(['role' => $role]);
            }

            $target->forceFill(['operations_region' => $region])->save();
            $target->unsetRelation('roles');

            $properties = ['old' => ['roles' => $old], 'new' => ['roles' => $new]];

            if ($oldRegion !== $region) {
                $properties['old']['region'] = $oldRegion?->value;
                $properties['new']['region'] = $region?->value;
            }

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Roles, 'roles.changed', "Changed roles of {$target->name}", $target, $properties, causer: $actor);

            // New menus appear (or go) on their next click: tell them why.
            $jobRoles = array_values(array_filter($new, fn (string $role) => $role !== Role::Employee->value));
            UpdateNotice::tell($target, $actor, 'Your access changed',
                ($jobRoles === [] ? 'You have the self-service pages only.' : 'Your role: '.implode(', ', array_map(fn (string $role) => Role::from($role)->label(), $jobRoles)).($region !== null ? " ({$region->label()})" : '').'. Its pages are in your menu.'),
                route('home'), 'shield', email: true);
        });
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Support;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\ComplaintStatus;
use App\Enums\EquipmentStatus;
use App\Enums\LoadRequestStatus;
use App\Enums\PayrollRunStatus;
use App\Enums\ReferralStatus;
use App\Enums\ReplenishmentStatus;
use App\Enums\ResignationStatus;
use App\Livewire\Admin\Equipment as EquipmentDesk;
use App\Livewire\Equipment\MyEquipment;
use App\Models\AbsenceNotice;
use App\Models\AwayLog;
use App\Models\CompanyDocument;
use App\Models\Complaint;
use App\Models\EmployeeProfile;
use App\Models\EquipmentIssue;
use App\Models\FinalPay;
use App\Models\LeaveRequest;
use App\Models\LoadRequest;
use App\Models\NoticeToExplain;
use App\Models\OvertimeRequest;
use App\Models\PayrollConcern;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\PettyCashFund;
use App\Models\PettyCashReplenishment;
use App\Models\Radio;
use App\Models\Referral;
use App\Models\Reimbursement;
use App\Models\Resignation;
use App\Models\TrainingRequest;
use App\Models\User;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;

/**
 * The sidebar, as data. Each item names the Ability that opens its page, so
 * the menu can never show a link the route would refuse, and adding a page
 * is one line here instead of another hand-written <a> in the layout.
 *
 * @phpstan-type NavItem array{label: string, route: string, icon: string, active: string, badge: int, tone: string}
 * @phpstan-type NavSection array{title: string, items: list<NavItem>}
 */
final class Navigation
{
    /**
     * @return list<NavSection>
     */
    public static function for(User $user): array
    {
        $can = fn (Ability $ability): bool => $user->can($ability->value);
        $user->loadMissing('employeeProfile');
        $onPayroll = ! $user->isPaidOutsidePayroll();

        $sections = [
            ['title' => 'Overview', 'items' => array_values(array_filter([
                $can(Ability::AccessEmployerArea) ? self::item('Dashboard', 'dashboard', 'grid') : null,
                $can(Ability::ViewOrganization) ? self::item('Organization', 'organization', 'building') : null,
            ]))],
            ['title' => 'Management', 'items' => array_values(array_filter([
                $can(Ability::ManagePayroll) ? self::item('Payroll', 'payroll', 'banknotes', badge: PayrollRun::query()->where('status', PayrollRunStatus::Processing)->count()) : null,
                // Office staff's reimbursements; the badge (what to approve) is the President or Vice President's.
                $can(Ability::ViewReimbursements) ? self::item('Reimbursements', 'reimbursement-requests', 'banknotes', badge: $can(Ability::ApproveReimbursements) ? Reimbursement::query()->pending()->where('user_id', '!=', $user->id)->count() : 0) : null,
                // Employees' "Report a problem" on a payslip, until answered.
                $can(Ability::ManagePayroll) ? self::item('Payroll Concerns', 'payroll-concerns', 'flag', badge: PayrollConcern::query()->open()->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::ManagePayroll) ? self::item('13th Month Pay', 'thirteenth-month', 'gift') : null,
                $can(Ability::ManagePayroll) ? self::item('Daily Rates', 'daily-rates', 'banknotes', badge: EmployeeProfile::query()->paidHere()->withoutRate()->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::ViewPeople) ? self::item('Employees', 'employees', 'users', active: 'employees*') : null,
                $can(Ability::SuperviseAttendance) ? self::item('Attendance Log', 'attendance-log', 'map-pin') : null,
                // Badges count what's waiting for YOUR decision (office staff's go to the President or Vice President).
                $can(Ability::MonitorRequests) ? self::item('Leave Requests', 'leave-requests', 'clipboard', badge: LeaveRequest::query()->awaitingActionBy($user)->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::MonitorRequests) ? self::item('Overtime Requests', 'overtime-requests', 'clock-plus', badge: OvertimeRequest::query()->awaitingReviewBy($user)->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::ManagePayroll) ? self::item('Late Deduction', 'late-deductions', 'clock-alert') : null,
                $can(Ability::ManagePayroll) ? self::item('Tax & Contributions', 'tax-settings', 'scroll') : null,
                // The sites guards are deployed to: set up by Operation HQ before HR onboards guards there.
                $can(Ability::ManageClients) ? self::item('Clients', 'clients', 'building') : null,
                // OSSI's own offices, where office staff clock in.
                $can(Ability::ManageOffices) ? self::item('OSSI Offices', 'offices', 'building') : null,
                $can(Ability::ManageRoster) ? self::item('Duty Roster', 'roster', 'calendar') : null,
                $can(Ability::ManagePatrols) ? self::item('Patrols', 'patrols', 'shield', badge: AwayLog::query()->open()->whereHas('user', fn ($query) => $query->visibleTo($user)->whereHas('employeeProfile', fn ($profile) => $profile->where('is_office_staff', false)))->count()) : null,
                // Badge: office staff away right now, among those this viewer heads (all for the President or VP).
                $can(Ability::MonitorOfficeAway) ? self::item('Office Away', 'office-away', 'map-pin', badge: AwayLog::query()->open()->whereHas('user', fn ($query) => Heads::seesAllOfficeStaff($user) ? $query->officeStaff() : Heads::constrainOfficeStaffHeadedBy($query, $user))->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::ManageRelievers) ? self::item('Relievers', 'relievers', 'arrows-right-left', badge: AbsenceNotice::query()->needsReliever()->visibleTo($user)->count()) : null,
                // What guards paid for a deployment, claimed by Operations (roadmap 5).
                $can(Ability::FileDeploymentClaims) ? self::item('Deployment Costs', 'deployment-claims', 'banknotes') : null,
                Complaint::handlesAny($user) ? self::item('Complaints', 'complaint-cases', 'flag', badge: Complaint::query()->handledBy($user)->where('status', ComplaintStatus::Open)->count()) : null,
                Resignation::handlesAny($user) ? self::item('Resignations', 'resignations', 'logout', badge: Resignation::query()->handledBy($user)->where('status', ResignationStatus::Pending)->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::SignFinalPay) ? self::item('Final Pay', 'final-pay', 'banknotes', badge: FinalPay::waitingFor($user)) : null,
                $can(Ability::PrepareFinalPay) ? self::item('Cash Bonds', 'cash-bonds', 'lock') : null,
                // Every fund; the badge (replenishments to release) is Accounting's.
                $can(Ability::ViewPettyCash) ? self::item('Petty Cash', 'petty-cash', 'wallet', badge: $can(Ability::ManagePettyCash) ? PettyCashReplenishment::query()->where('status', ReplenishmentStatus::Pending)->where('requested_by', '!=', $user->id)->count() : 0) : null,
                $can(Ability::ManageDocuments) ? self::item('Documents', 'documents', 'folder', badge: CompanyDocument::query()->current()->whereNotNull('expires_on')->whereDate('expires_on', '<=', today()->addDays(CompanyDocument::DUE_SOON_DAYS)->toDateString())->count()) : null,
                // Badge: guards' training requests to answer.
                $can(Ability::ManageTraining) ? self::item('Training', 'trainings', 'academic-cap', badge: TrainingRequest::query()->pending()->count()) : null,
                // Badge: radios whose NTC permit expires within 30 days, or has.
                $can(Ability::ManageRadios) ? self::item('Radios', 'radios', 'radio', badge: Radio::query()->permitDueBy(CarbonImmutable::today()->addDays(Radio::DUE_SOON_DAYS))->count()) : null,
                // Issuers (Operations, Admin): badge = requests waiting + reports to decide. A head who
                // doesn't issue (HR, the President or VP) sees it only while a report waits for them.
                ($equipmentBadge = EquipmentDesk::canOpen($user) ? EquipmentIssue::query()->handledBy($user)->where('status', EquipmentStatus::Requested)->count() + EquipmentDesk::incidentsToDecide($user) : 0) > 0 || $can(Ability::IssueEquipment)
                    ? self::item('Equipment', 'equipment', 'package', badge: $equipmentBadge)
                    : null,
                // Badge: referrals waiting for HR to say hired or not.
                $can(Ability::ManageReferrals) ? self::item('Referrals', 'referral-cases', 'user-plus', badge: Referral::query()->where('status', ReferralStatus::Submitted)->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::GiveMerits) ? self::item('Merits & Demerits', 'merits', 'scale') : null,
                // Badge: the ones you issued that are ready to decide (explained, or the days passed).
                $can(Ability::IssueNoticesToExplain) ? self::item('Notices to Explain', 'notices-to-explain', 'scroll', badge: NoticeToExplain::query()->where('issued_by', $user->id)->get(['id', 'status', 'explain_by'])->filter(fn (NoticeToExplain $notice) => $notice->readyToDecide())->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::ManageLoadRequests) ? self::item('Load Requests', 'load-requests', 'phone', badge: LoadRequest::query()->where('status', LoadRequestStatus::Pending)->count()) : null,
                $can(Ability::PublishContent) ? self::item('Announcements', 'announcements', 'megaphone') : null,
            ]))],
            ['title' => 'System', 'items' => array_values(array_filter([
                $can(Ability::ConfigureHolidays) ? self::item('Holidays', 'holidays', 'calendar') : null,
                $can(Ability::ConfigureSystem) ? self::item('Shifts', 'shifts', 'sun-moon') : null,
                $can(Ability::ConfigureSystem) ? self::item('Roles & Access', 'roles', 'shield') : null,
                $can(Ability::ViewSystemLogs) ? self::item('Audit Log', 'audit-log', 'scroll') : null,
            ]))],
            // Paid outside this payroll (the President or Vice President): no attendance, leave, pay or load of their own here.
            ['title' => 'Personal', 'items' => array_values(array_filter([
                $onPayroll ? self::item('My Attendance', 'attendance', 'clock') : null,
                // Guards at a post tell Operations when they can't report; office staff use My Leave.
                $onPayroll && $user->employeeProfile?->hasDeployment() === true ? self::item('Report Absence', 'absence-notice', 'arrows-right-left') : null,
                $onPayroll ? self::item('My Leave', 'leave', 'calendar') : null,
                $onPayroll ? self::item('My Overtime', 'overtime', 'clock-plus') : null,
                $onPayroll ? self::item('My Payslips', 'payslips', 'banknotes') : null,
                // Loans, cash advances and the cash bond: what's left and what each payslip took.
                $onPayroll ? self::item('My Loans', 'loans', 'clipboard') : null,
                // Guards: ask for a refresher, license-renewal training, first aid.
                $onPayroll && $user->employeeProfile?->hasDeployment() === true ? self::item('My Training', 'my-training', 'academic-cap') : null,
                $onPayroll ? self::item('Borrow Load', 'load', 'phone') : null,
                // Office staff: money spent for the company. A guard: once Operations claimed a deployment cost for them.
                $onPayroll && Reimbursement::canSeeOwn($user) ? self::item('My Reimbursements', 'reimbursements', 'banknotes') : null,
                // A fund's custodian who doesn't already have Management → Petty Cash.
                ! $can(Ability::ViewPettyCash) && PettyCashFund::custodianOf($user) !== null ? self::item('Petty Cash', 'petty-cash', 'wallet') : null,
                $onPayroll && Referral::canRefer($user) ? self::item('Refer a Friend', 'referrals', 'user-plus') : null,
                // Badge: items to confirm receiving, and damage or loss reports to explain.
                $onPayroll ? self::item('My Equipment', 'my-equipment', 'package', badge: MyEquipment::waitingFor($user)) : null,
                $onPayroll ? self::item('My Complaints', 'complaints', 'flag') : null,
                // Only while one is in progress; filing starts from My Profile (not a daily menu item).
                $onPayroll && $user->resignations()->open()->exists() ? self::item('My Resignation', 'resignation', 'logout') : null,
                // Only for someone who has one; badge: to mark received, or still to explain.
                ($myNotices = NoticeToExplain::query()->where('user_id', $user->id)->get(['id', 'status', 'explain_by', 'acknowledged_at', 'decision_acknowledged_at']))->isNotEmpty()
                    ? self::item('My Notices', 'my-notices', 'scroll', badge: $myNotices->filter(fn (NoticeToExplain $notice) => $notice->canStillExplain() || ($notice->isDecided() ? $notice->decision_acknowledged_at === null : $notice->acknowledged_at === null))->count())
                    : null,
                // Publishers already have Management → Announcements (with all of them).
                $can(Ability::PublishContent) ? null : self::item('Announcements', 'news', 'megaphone'),
                self::item('Company Policy', 'company-policy', 'book-open'),
                self::item('Help & FAQs', 'help', 'question'),
            ]))],
        ];

        return array_values(array_filter($sections, fn (array $section) => $section['items'] !== []));
    }

    /**
     * @return NavItem
     */
    private static function item(string $label, string $route, string $icon, int $badge = 0, ?string $active = null): array
    {
        return [
            'label' => $label,
            'route' => $route,
            'icon' => $icon,
            'active' => $active ?? $route,
            'badge' => $badge,
            'tone' => 'amber',
        ];
    }
}
Question you'd askAnswer
The route already has can:. Why check again in the method?The old app had a bug: a page opened while you held a role kept its buttons working after the role was removed. The in-method check also survives if the component is ever mounted on another route.
A Satellite who is also HR: one region or all?All. isRegionallyLimited() is true only when none of the user's roles sees the whole company.
What does a Satellite with no region see?Nobody. The scope becomes 1 = 0, and Roles & Access refuses to save the role without a region.
HR added someone who hasn't registered. Can they get a role now?Yes. Roles belong to accounts, so Roles & Access lists them under Not registered yet. Set role saves it on the record (pending_role, SetPendingRole), and ClaimEmployeeAccount gives it to their account the moment they register.
Why not spatie/laravel-permission?The old app's permission rows were never checked. Enums say the real rules honestly, need no package, and PHPStan can check every use.
Can a Super Admin lock everyone out?No. SyncUserRoles refuses to remove your own Super Admin role and refuses to remove the last one.
Try it
  1. As president@example.test (or vp@example.test): Leave Requests. Guards' rows say "approved by HR"; HR, Operation HQ and Accounting staff's rows have Review; other office staff's say "View only".
  2. As satellite@example.test: Employees lists only guards in that account's region (the demo sets Region IV-A). As super admin, change it on Roles & Access → Region covered, and the list follows.
03

Privacy notice & sessions

Five middleware run on every web request, including every Livewire click, because Livewire's update endpoint sits in the same web group. Order matters: the idle check comes first, so a timed-out session is signed out, not sent to the privacy notice.

MiddlewareJob
EnforceIdleTimeoutSign out after 15 idle minutes. The browser countdown is only the friendly half.
EnsureAccountIsActiveEnd sessions of people HR marked resigned or terminated.
RequirePrivacyAcknowledgementHold users on the notice until they acknowledge its current version (RA 10173 sec. 16(a)).
PreventAuthenticatedPageCachingno-store, so the Back button after logout shows nothing.
AddSecurityHeadersNo framing, no MIME sniffing, camera and GPS for this site only, HSTS in production.

<?php

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

/**
 * Signs a user out after config('security.idle_timeout.minutes') without a request.
 *
 * resources/js/idle-timeout.js is only the UX (countdown, "Stay signed in").
 * THIS is the enforcement: JavaScript can be disabled or the tab closed, but
 * every request, including Livewire's, passes through here.
 */
final class EnforceIdleTimeout
{
    public const SESSION_KEY = 'last_activity_at';

    /**
     * Set by SessionKeepAliveController: a heartbeat may read the clock but
     * only resets it when the browser reports real input.
     */
    public const HEARTBEAT = 'idle_timeout.heartbeat';

    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response
    {
        if (! config('security.idle_timeout.enabled') || ! Auth::check()) {
            return $next($request);
        }

        $lastActivity = $request->session()->get(self::SESSION_KEY);

        if (is_int($lastActivity) && time() - $lastActivity >= $this->timeoutSeconds()) {
            return $this->signOut($request);
        }

        $response = $next($request);

        // $request->user(), not Auth::check(): the request itself may have logged the user out.
        // Joining the live-notification channel isn't activity: an unattended tab re-joins on its own
        // whenever its WebSocket reconnects.
        if ($request->user() !== null && ! $request->attributes->get(self::HEARTBEAT, false) && ! $request->is('broadcasting/auth')) {
            $request->session()->put(self::SESSION_KEY, time());
        }

        return $response;
    }

    private function signOut(Request $request): Response
    {
        Auth::guard('web')->logout();
        $request->session()->invalidate();
        $request->session()->regenerateToken();

        // After invalidate(), which empties the session: order matters.
        $request->session()->flash('status', $this->message());

        // Livewire treats 419 as "session expired"; idle-timeout.js turns it into a redirect.
        if ($request->hasHeader('X-Livewire') || $request->expectsJson()) {
            return response()->json(['message' => $this->message()], 419);
        }

        return redirect()->route('login');
    }

    private function message(): string
    {
        $minutes = intdiv($this->timeoutSeconds(), 60);

        return "You were signed out after {$minutes} minutes of inactivity.";
    }

    private function timeoutSeconds(): int
    {
        return max(1, (int) config('security.idle_timeout.minutes')) * 60;
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use App\Models\User;
use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

/**
 * Holds a signed-in user on the privacy notice until they acknowledge its
 * CURRENT version (RA 10173 sec. 16(a)). In the `web` group, so Livewire
 * requests can't skip it by never loading a new page.
 */
final class RequirePrivacyAcknowledgement
{
    /**
     * Routes a user must still reach, or the gate becomes a trap.
     */
    private const ALLOWED = [
        'privacy-notice',
        'privacy-notice.acknowledge',
        'logout',
        'session.keep-alive',
        'verification.notice',
        'verification.verify',
        'verification.send',
    ];

    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        if (! $user instanceof User || $user->hasAcknowledgedPrivacyNotice()) {
            return $next($request);
        }

        if (in_array($request->route()?->getName(), self::ALLOWED, true)) {
            return $next($request);
        }

        if ($request->hasHeader('X-Livewire') || $request->expectsJson()) {
            return response()->json(['message' => 'Please acknowledge the privacy notice first.'], 403);
        }

        // guest() remembers the URL, so they land where they were going afterwards.
        return redirect()->guest(route('privacy-notice'));
    }
}

/**
 * Browser half of the idle timeout. App\Http\Middleware\EnforceIdleTimeout is
 * the enforcement; this file is UX and clock syncing:
 *
 *  - shows a countdown before the deadline instead of dropping the user mid-form;
 *  - shares "last activity" across tabs via localStorage;
 *  - pings the server only after REAL input, so an abandoned tab never keeps a
 *    session alive.
 */
const STORAGE_KEY = 'ossi:last-activity';
const ACTIVITY_EVENTS = ['pointerdown', 'keydown', 'wheel', 'touchstart', 'scroll'];

export default function idleTimeout({ timeoutSeconds, warningSeconds, keepAliveUrl, loginUrl }) {
    return {
        warningVisible: false,
        secondsLeft: warningSeconds,
        lastActivity: Date.now(),
        activitySincePing: false,
        signingOut: false,
        tickHandle: null,
        pingHandle: null,

        init() {
            this.restore();
            this.markActive();

            const onActivity = () => this.markActive();
            ACTIVITY_EVENTS.forEach((event) => window.addEventListener(event, onActivity, { passive: true, capture: true }));

            window.addEventListener('storage', (event) => {
                const stamp = Number(event.newValue);
                if (event.key === STORAGE_KEY && Number.isFinite(stamp) && stamp > this.lastActivity) {
                    this.lastActivity = stamp;
                    this.warningVisible = false;
                }
            });

            // A Livewire round trip already resets the server clock.
            window.Livewire?.hook?.('request', () => {
                this.lastActivity = Date.now();
                this.activitySincePing = false;
                this.publish();
            });

            // 419 = the server already ended the session: go to login instead of Livewire's "page expired" dialog.
            window.Livewire?.interceptRequest?.(({ onError }) => {
                onError(({ response, preventDefault }) => {
                    if (response?.status === 419) {
                        preventDefault();
                        window.location.href = loginUrl;
                    }
                });
            });

            this.tickHandle = setInterval(() => this.tick(), 1000);
            this.pingHandle = setInterval(() => this.ping(), Math.max(60, Math.floor(timeoutSeconds / 3)) * 1000);
        },

        destroy() {
            clearInterval(this.tickHandle);
            clearInterval(this.pingHandle);
        },

        get countdownLabel() {
            const minutes = Math.floor(this.secondsLeft / 60);
            const seconds = this.secondsLeft % 60;

            return minutes > 0 ? `${minutes}:${String(seconds).padStart(2, '0')}` : `${seconds}s`;
        },

        markActive() {
            if (this.warningVisible) return; // Only the button dismisses the warning.

            this.lastActivity = Date.now();
            this.activitySincePing = true;
            this.publish();
        },

        publish() {
            try {
                localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, String(this.lastActivity));
            } catch {
                // Private mode: the timer still works, just not across tabs.
            }
        },

        restore() {
            try {
                const stamp = Number(localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY));
                if (Number.isFinite(stamp) && stamp > 0) this.lastActivity = stamp;
            } catch {
                // Ignore.
            }
        },

        tick() {
            const remaining = timeoutSeconds - Math.floor((Date.now() - this.lastActivity) / 1000);

            if (remaining <= 0) {
                this.signOut();
                return;
            }

            this.warningVisible = remaining <= warningSeconds;
            this.secondsLeft = remaining;
        },

        ping() {
            if (!this.activitySincePing || this.warningVisible || this.signingOut) return;

            this.activitySincePing = false;
            this.keepAlive();
        },

        staySignedIn() {
            this.warningVisible = false;
            this.lastActivity = Date.now();
            this.activitySincePing = false;
            this.publish();
            this.keepAlive();
        },

        keepAlive() {
            fetch(keepAliveUrl, {
                method: 'POST',
                credentials: 'same-origin',
                headers: {
                    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                    Accept: 'application/json',
                    'X-CSRF-TOKEN': document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]')?.content ?? '',
                },
                body: JSON.stringify({ active: true }),
            }).catch(() => {});
        },

        signOut() {
            if (this.signingOut) return;

            this.signingOut = true;
            this.destroy();
            this.$refs.logoutForm.submit();
        },
    };
}
Question you'd askAnswer
Why both a JS timer and middleware?JavaScript can be disabled or the tab closed; the session cookie outlives both. The middleware enforces, the script warns and syncs tabs.
Can an open tab keep a session alive forever?No. The keep-alive ping only resets the clock when it reports real input (active: true), and the script only sends that after a key press, click or scroll.
Why store the notice version, not a yes/no?When the notice changes, bump PRIVACY_NOTICE_VERSION and everyone is asked again.
Why "acknowledge" and never "consent"?The legal basis is the employment contract and the law. Consent given to keep a job isn't freely given, and calling it consent would invite withdrawing it. The reasoning is in config/privacy.php.
04

Audit log

One append-only table. Every approve, generate, role change and record edit writes an entry inside the same transaction as the change, so the two are saved together or not at all. The model throws on update and delete: an audit trail that can be edited proves nothing.

app/Services/AuditLogger.php85 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Services;

use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\ActivityLog;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;

/**
 * Writes one audit entry. Called from inside the same DB transaction as the
 * change it describes, so a change and its audit entry are saved together or
 * not at all. Deliberately NOT queued: an audit row lost in a failed job is
 * worse than a slightly slower request.
 */
final class AuditLogger
{
    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $properties
     */
    public function record(
        AuditArea $area,
        string $event,
        string $description,
        ?Model $subject = null,
        array $properties = [],
        ?User $causer = null,
    ): ActivityLog {
        $causer ??= auth()->user();

        $entry = new ActivityLog;
        $entry->forceFill([
            'log_name' => $area,
            'event' => $event,
            'description' => $description,
            'subject_type' => $subject?->getMorphClass(),
            'subject_id' => $subject?->getKey(),
            'causer_id' => $causer instanceof User ? $causer->id : null,
            'properties' => $properties === [] ? null : $properties,
            'ip_address' => app()->runningInConsole() ? null : request()->ip(),
        ])->save();

        return $entry;
    }

    /**
     * Before/after values of the keys that changed. Sensitive keys are listed
     * as changed without their values, so the audit log doesn't become a
     * second copy of the government IDs it is meant to protect.
     *
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $before
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $after
     * @param  list<string>  $masked
     * @return array{old: array<string, mixed>, new: array<string, mixed>}
     */
    public static function diff(array $before, array $after, array $masked = []): array
    {
        $old = [];
        $new = [];

        foreach ($after as $key => $value) {
            $previous = $before[$key] ?? null;

            if (self::normalize($previous) === self::normalize($value)) {
                continue;
            }

            $isMasked = in_array($key, $masked, true);
            $old[$key] = $isMasked ? '(hidden)' : self::normalize($previous);
            $new[$key] = $isMasked ? '(changed)' : self::normalize($value);
        }

        return ['old' => $old, 'new' => $new];
    }

    private static function normalize(mixed $value): mixed
    {
        return match (true) {
            $value instanceof \BackedEnum => $value->value,
            $value instanceof \DateTimeInterface => $value->format('Y-m-d'),
            // An empty list is no value, like an empty string (a new "other IDs" isn't a change).
            default => $value === '' || $value === [] ? null : $value,
        };
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\MorphTo;
use LogicException;

/**
 * One audit entry. Append-only: an audit trail that can be edited proves nothing.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property AuditArea $log_name
 * @property string $event
 * @property string $description
 * @property string|null $subject_type
 * @property int|null $subject_id
 * @property int|null $causer_id
 * @property array<string, mixed>|null $properties
 * @property string|null $ip_address
 * @property CarbonImmutable $created_at
 * @property-read User|null $causer
 * @property-read Model|null $subject
 */
class ActivityLog extends Model
{
    protected $table = 'activity_log';

    public const UPDATED_AT = null;

    protected static function booted(): void
    {
        static::updating(fn () => throw new LogicException('Audit entries cannot be changed.'));
        static::deleting(fn () => throw new LogicException('Audit entries cannot be deleted.'));
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'log_name' => AuditArea::class,
            'properties' => 'array',
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function causer(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'causer_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return MorphTo<Model, $this>
     */
    public function subject(): MorphTo
    {
        return $this->morphTo();
    }
}
Question you'd askAnswer
Why not queue audit writes?A failed job would lose the record of who approved a payslip. A few milliseconds in the request is the cheaper risk.
Why mask some fields in the diff?Otherwise the audit log becomes a second, unencrypted copy of every SSS and TIN number. It records "(changed)" instead.

People: employees, shifts, holidays

The employee profile is HR's record, and it exists before the login account does (user_id is nullable). That is the hinge of the registration rule. Government IDs and medical notes use Laravel's encrypted cast, and the profile carries explicit is_office_staff and is_night_shift flags for payroll.
