<?php

namespace App\Services\Payroll;

use App\Data\AdjustmentLine;
use App\Data\LateBracket;
use App\Data\LoanLine;
use App\Data\MonthToDate;
use App\Data\PayslipBreakdown;
use App\Data\PayslipInput;
use App\Data\RateSchedule;
use App\Data\StatutoryRules;
use App\Enums\HolidayType;

/**
 * The one payslip formula, shared by the payroll screen and the employee's
 * own payslip page so they can never disagree. Pure: no queries, no config.
 *
 *   minute rate   = daily rate / (8 × 60)
 *   basic         = daily rate × days worked
 *   night diff    = round(basic × 0.10)                 night-shift employees only
 *   overtime      = round(OT minutes × minute rate × 1.25)
 *   holiday       = Σ holiday days worked × daily rate × premium
 *   taxable gross = basic + night diff + overtime + holiday + correction adjustments
 *   gross         = taxable gross + allowance/refund adjustments (not taxed)
 *   deductions    = SSS + PhilHealth + Pag-IBIG + tax + carried over + late + deduction adjustments + loan installments
 *   net           = gross − deductions, never below ₱0
 *
 * Deductions are taken in exactly that order and stop when the pay runs out.
 * The rest is a shortfall: carried to the next payslip, except an unpaid loan
 * installment, which just stays in the loan's balance.
 *
 * @phpstan-import-type Contributions from PayslipBreakdown
 */
final class PayslipCalculator
{
    public function __construct(private readonly StatutoryContributions $formulas = new StatutoryContributions) {}

    /**
     * What the attendance itself is worth: basic, holiday premium, overtime and night
     * differential, less the late deduction DUE (before the pay runs out). No
     * contributions, loans or adjustments. calculate() is built on it, and
     * DetectPriorPeriodCorrections compares it against a frozen payslip, so a
     * recomputed cut-off can never drift from how payslips are computed.
     *
     * @return array{daily_rate: float, basic: float, holiday: float, overtime: float, night: float, late: float, total: float}
     */
    public function attendancePay(PayslipInput $input, RateSchedule $rates): array
    {
        // The employee's own rate from HR when set; the schedule's default for their type otherwise.
        $dailyRate = $input->dailyRate ?? $rates->dailyRate($input->isOfficeStaff);
        $minuteRate = $dailyRate / ($rates->standardHoursPerDay * 60);

        $basic = $dailyRate * $input->daysWorked;
        // Labor Code Art. 86: 10% of the regular rate for each hour worked 10 PM–6 AM.
        $night = round($input->nightMinutes * $minuteRate * $rates->nightDifferentialRate);
        $overtime = round($input->overtimeMinutes * $minuteRate * $rates->overtimeMultiplier);
        $holiday = $this->holidayPremium($input->holidayDaysWorked, $dailyRate, $rates);
        $late = $this->lateDeduction($input->lateMinutes, $input->lateBrackets, $minuteRate);

        return [
            'daily_rate' => $dailyRate,
            'basic' => $basic,
            'holiday' => $holiday,
            'overtime' => $overtime,
            'night' => $night,
            'late' => $late,
            'total' => round(round($basic, 2) + $holiday + $overtime + $night - $late, 2),
        ];
    }

    public function calculate(PayslipInput $input, RateSchedule $rates): PayslipBreakdown
    {
        $office = $input->isOfficeStaff;
        $pay = $this->attendancePay($input, $rates);
        $dailyRate = $pay['daily_rate'];
        $basicPay = $pay['basic'];
        $nightDifferential = $pay['night'];
        $overtimePay = $pay['overtime'];
        $holidayPay = $pay['holiday'];

        // Approved adjustments that ADD to pay. Corrections replace pay that was
        // earned, so they are taxed like it; allowances and refunds are not.
        $earningAdjustments = array_values(array_filter($input->adjustments, fn (AdjustmentLine $line) => $line->amount > 0));
        $taxableAdjustments = array_sum(array_map(fn (AdjustmentLine $line) => $line->isTaxable ? $line->amount : 0.0, $earningAdjustments));
        $otherAdjustments = array_sum(array_map(fn (AdjustmentLine $line) => $line->isTaxable ? 0.0 : $line->amount, $earningAdjustments));

        $taxableGross = $basicPay + $nightDifferential + $overtimePay + $holidayPay + $taxableAdjustments;

        // What is DUE, before checking the pay can cover it.
        $contributions = [];

        if ($rates->statutory !== null) {
            // 2026+: computed from the government rules. No attendance = no payslip = nothing due.
            [$due, $contributions] = $input->daysWorked > 0
                ? $this->statutoryDue($rates->statutory, $input->monthToDate ?? MonthToDate::wholeMonth(), $basicPay, $taxableGross, $rates->isMinimumWageEarner($office, $dailyRate))
                : [['sss' => 0.0, 'philhealth' => 0.0, 'pagibig' => 0.0, 'withholding_tax' => 0.0], []];
        } else {
            // Older schedules: the fixed amounts of the original spec.
            $due = [
                'sss' => $rates->sss($office),
                'philhealth' => $rates->philhealth($office),
                'pagibig' => $rates->pagibig($office),
                // 0% for field staff: minimum wage earners are exempt (RA 9504).
                'withholding_tax' => round($taxableGross * $rates->withholdingRate($office), 2),
            ];
        }
        $lateDue = $pay['late'];

        // Net pay never goes below ₱0. Deductions are taken in this order until
        // the pay runs out; whatever is left is listed as a shortfall.
        $remaining = round($taxableGross + $otherAdjustments, 2);
        $shortfalls = [];
        $take = function (float $amount, string $label, bool $carries) use (&$remaining, &$shortfalls): float {
            $taken = round(min($amount, max(0.0, $remaining)), 2);
            $remaining = round($remaining - $taken, 2);

            if ($amount - $taken >= 0.01) {
                $shortfalls[] = ['label' => $label, 'amount' => round($amount - $taken, 2), 'carries' => $carries];
            }

            return $taken;
        };

        // 1. Statutory contributions and tax: owed to the government first.
        $sss = $take($due['sss'], 'SSS', true);
        $philhealth = $take($due['philhealth'], 'PhilHealth', true);
        $pagibig = $take($due['pagibig'], 'Pag-IBIG', true);
        $withholdingTax = $take($due['withholding_tax'], 'Withholding tax', true);

        // 2. What earlier payslips couldn't cover.
        $carryoverLines = [];
        foreach ($input->carryovers as $carryover) {
            $carryoverLines[] = ['carryover_id' => $carryover->carryoverId, 'label' => $carryover->label, 'amount' => $take($carryover->amount, $carryover->label, true)];
        }

        // 3. Late deduction, 4. deduction adjustments, then 5. loans. An unpaid
        // loan installment is NOT carried: it simply stays in the loan's balance.
        $lateDeduction = $take($lateDue, 'Late deduction', true);

        $adjustmentLines = array_map(fn (AdjustmentLine $line) => ['adjustment_id' => $line->adjustmentId, 'label' => $line->label, 'amount' => round($line->amount, 2)], $earningAdjustments);
        foreach ($input->adjustments as $line) {
            if ($line->amount < 0) {
                $adjustmentLines[] = ['adjustment_id' => $line->adjustmentId, 'label' => $line->label, 'amount' => -$take(-$line->amount, $line->label, true)];
            }
        }

        $loanLines = array_map(fn (LoanLine $loan) => [...$loan->toArray(), 'amount' => $take($loan->amount, $loan->label, false)], $input->loans);

        return new PayslipBreakdown(
            rateSchedule: $rates->effectiveFrom,
            isOfficeStaff: $office,
            daysWorked: $input->daysWorked,
            lateMinutes: $input->lateMinutes,
            overtimeMinutes: $input->overtimeMinutes,
            dailyRate: $dailyRate,
            basicPay: $basicPay,
            holidayPay: $holidayPay,
            overtimePay: $overtimePay,
            nightDifferential: $nightDifferential,
            nightMinutes: $input->nightMinutes,
            sss: $sss,
            philhealth: $philhealth,
            pagibig: $pagibig,
            withholdingTax: $withholdingTax,
            lateDeduction: $lateDeduction,
            loanLines: $loanLines,
            carryoverLines: $carryoverLines,
            shortfallLines: $shortfalls,
            adjustmentLines: $adjustmentLines,
            contributions: $contributions,
        );
    }

    /**
     * SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG are MONTHLY; payroll runs twice a month.
     *
     *   1st cutoff   half of the monthly amount, estimated as if the month
     *                continues like this cutoff (base × 2)
     *   last cutoff  monthly amount on the ACTUAL month (earlier cutoffs +
     *                this one) minus what the earlier cutoffs were due
     *
     * Bases: SSS uses all taxable compensation; PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG use
     * basic pay. Tax (unless a minimum wage earner) is the BIR semi-monthly
     * table on taxable pay after the employee's three contributions.
     *
     * @return array{0: array{sss: float, philhealth: float, pagibig: float, withholding_tax: float}, 1: Contributions}
     */
    private function statutoryDue(StatutoryRules $rules, MonthToDate $month, float $basicPay, float $taxableGross, bool $minimumWageEarner): array
    {
        $final = $month->isFinalCutoff;
        $scale = $final ? 1.0 : 2.0;
        $part = fn (float $monthly, float $already): float => $final ? round(max(0.0, $monthly - $already), 2) : round($monthly / 2, 2);

        $sssMonthly = $this->formulas->sss($rules, $final ? $month->sss['base'] + $taxableGross : $taxableGross * $scale);
        $philhealthMonthly = $this->formulas->philhealth($rules, $final ? $month->philhealth['base'] + $basicPay : $basicPay * $scale);
        $pagibigMonthly = $this->formulas->pagibig($rules, $final ? $month->pagibig['base'] + $basicPay : $basicPay * $scale);

        // basis = the monthly amount the formula was applied to; monthly = the monthly
        // employee contribution. Saved so any payslip can show its working later.
        $sssBasis = $final ? $month->sss['base'] + $taxableGross : $taxableGross * $scale;
        $philhealthBasis = $final ? $month->philhealth['base'] + $basicPay : $basicPay * $scale;

        $shares = [
            'sss' => ['base' => round($taxableGross, 2), 'basis' => round($sssBasis, 2), 'monthly' => $sssMonthly['employee'], 'employee' => $part($sssMonthly['employee'], $month->sss['employee']), 'employer' => $part($sssMonthly['employer'], $month->sss['employer']), 'ec' => $part($sssMonthly['ec'], $month->sss['ec'])],
            'philhealth' => ['base' => round($basicPay, 2), 'basis' => $philhealthMonthly['base'], 'monthly' => $philhealthMonthly['employee'], 'employee' => $part($philhealthMonthly['employee'], $month->philhealth['employee']), 'employer' => $part($philhealthMonthly['employer'], $month->philhealth['employer']), 'ec' => 0.0],
            'pagibig' => ['base' => round($basicPay, 2), 'basis' => $pagibigMonthly['base'], 'monthly' => $pagibigMonthly['employee'], 'employee' => $part($pagibigMonthly['employee'], $month->pagibig['employee']), 'employer' => $part($pagibigMonthly['employer'], $month->pagibig['employer']), 'ec' => 0.0],
        ];

        $employeeContributions = $shares['sss']['employee'] + $shares['philhealth']['employee'] + $shares['pagibig']['employee'];
        $taxable = round(max(0.0, $taxableGross - $employeeContributions), 2);
        $tax = $minimumWageEarner ? 0.0 : $this->formulas->withholdingSemiMonthly($rules, $taxable);

        return [
            ['sss' => $shares['sss']['employee'], 'philhealth' => $shares['philhealth']['employee'], 'pagibig' => $shares['pagibig']['employee'], 'withholding_tax' => $tax],
            [
                'final_cutoff' => $final,
                'minimum_wage_earner' => $minimumWageEarner,
                'msc' => $sssMonthly['msc'],
                'taxable' => $taxable,
                'tax_bracket' => $minimumWageEarner ? null : $this->formulas->bracketFor($rules, $taxable),
                ...$shares,
            ],
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Only the PREMIUM: basic pay already covers the day, so a worked regular
     * holiday totals 200% and a special day 130%. Unworked holidays earn nothing.
     *
     * @param  array<string, int>  $daysByType
     */
    private function holidayPremium(array $daysByType, float $dailyRate, RateSchedule $rates): float
    {
        $premium = 0.0;

        foreach (HolidayType::cases() as $type) {
            $premium += ($daysByType[$type->value] ?? 0) * $dailyRate * $rates->holidayPremium($type);
        }

        return round($premium, 2);
    }

    /**
     * Brackets win when configured: the fixed amount of the matching bracket,
     * or 0 when none matches. With no brackets at all, fall back to per-minute.
     *
     * @param  list<LateBracket>  $brackets
     */
    private function lateDeduction(int $lateMinutes, array $brackets, float $minuteRate): float
    {
        if ($lateMinutes <= 0) {
            return 0.0;
        }

        if ($brackets === []) {
            return round($lateMinutes * $minuteRate);
        }

        foreach ($brackets as $bracket) {
            if ($bracket->covers($lateMinutes)) {
                return $bracket->amount;
            }
        }

        return 0.0;
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Queries\Payroll;

use App\Data\PayslipBreakdown;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\PayslipRecord;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Services\Payroll\PayslipCalculator;
use App\Services\Payroll\RateScheduleResolver;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;

/**
 * The payslip of each employee for a run: the FROZEN record once generated,
 * otherwise a live estimate from the calculator.
 *
 * Both the payroll screen and "My payslips" call this, which is how the spec's
 * "an employee's payslip page and the payroll screen show identical numbers"
 * is guaranteed rather than hoped for.
 */
final class ResolvePayslips
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly PayslipInputsQuery $inputs,
        private readonly PayslipCalculator $calculator,
        private readonly RateScheduleResolver $rates,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  Collection<int, User>  $users  with employeeProfile loaded
     * @return array<int, PayslipBreakdown> keyed by user id
     */
    public function handle(PayrollRun $run, Collection $users): array
    {
        $records = PayslipRecord::query()
            ->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)
            ->whereIn('user_id', $users->pluck('id')->all())
            ->get()
            ->keyBy('user_id');

        $pending = $users->reject(fn (User $user) => $records->has($user->id));
        $inputs = $this->inputs->handle($run, $pending);
        $rates = $this->rates->forDate($run->start_date);

        $payslips = [];

        foreach ($users as $user) {
            /** @var PayslipRecord|null $record */
            $record = $records->get($user->id);

            $payslips[$user->id] = $record !== null
                ? PayslipBreakdown::fromRecord($record)
                : $this->calculator->calculate($inputs[$user->id], $rates);
        }

        return $payslips;
    }

    public function forUser(PayrollRun $run, User $user): PayslipBreakdown
    {
        $user->loadMissing('employeeProfile');

        return $this->handle($run, collect([$user]))[$user->id];
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Queries\Payroll;

use App\Data\AdjustmentLine;
use App\Data\CarryoverLine;
use App\Data\LateBracket;
use App\Data\LoanLine;
use App\Data\MonthToDate;
use App\Data\PayslipInput;
use App\Data\ResolvedRate;
use App\Enums\HolidayType;
use App\Enums\RateSource;
use App\Models\EmployeeDeduction;
use App\Models\Holiday;
use App\Models\LateDeductionRule;
use App\Models\OvertimeRequest;
use App\Models\PayrollAdjustment;
use App\Models\PayrollCarryover;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\TimeLog;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Queries\People\EffectiveRatesQuery;
use App\Services\Attendance\AttendanceCalculator;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;

/**
 * Gathers calculator inputs for many employees in seven queries total,
 * whatever the headcount (no query per employee).
 */
final class PayslipInputsQuery
{
    /**
     * @param  Collection<int, User>  $users  with employeeProfile loaded
     * @return array<int, PayslipInput> keyed by user id
     */
    public function handle(PayrollRun $run, Collection $users): array
    {
        $ids = $users->pluck('id')->all();

        if ($ids === []) {
            return [];
        }

        $logsByUser = TimeLog::query()
            ->whereIn('user_id', $ids)
            ->between($run->start_date, $run->end_date)
            ->with('shift')
            ->get(['user_id', 'shift_id', 'log_date', 'clock_in_at', 'clock_out_at', 'late_minutes', 'overtime_minutes'])
            ->groupBy('user_id');

        $approvedByUser = OvertimeRequest::query()
            ->approved()
            ->whereIn('user_id', $ids)
            ->whereDate('date', '>=', $run->start_date->toDateString())
            ->whereDate('date', '<=', $run->end_date->toDateString())
            ->get(['user_id', 'date', 'approved_minutes'])
            ->groupBy('user_id')
            ->map(fn (Collection $rows) => $rows->mapWithKeys(fn (OvertimeRequest $row) => [$row->date->toDateString() => (int) $row->approved_minutes]));

        /** @var Collection<string, HolidayType> $holidayTypes */
        $holidayTypes = Holiday::query()
            ->between($run->start_date, $run->end_date)
            ->get(['date', 'type'])
            ->mapWithKeys(fn (Holiday $holiday) => [$holiday->date->toDateString() => $holiday->type]);

        // Not one still waiting for the employee's authorization (Art. 113).
        $loansByUser = EmployeeDeduction::query()
            ->takenFromPay()
            ->whereIn('user_id', $ids)
            ->orderBy('id')
            ->get()
            ->groupBy('user_id');

        // Shortfalls of earlier payslips, owed on this one.
        $carryoversByUser = PayrollCarryover::query()
            ->owedBefore($run)
            ->whereIn('user_id', $ids)
            ->orderBy('id')
            ->get()
            ->groupBy('user_id');

        // Only APPROVED adjustments reach a payslip; pending ones wait for a second person.
        $adjustmentsByUser = PayrollAdjustment::query()
            ->approved()
            ->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)
            ->whereIn('user_id', $ids)
            ->orderBy('id')
            ->get()
            ->groupBy('user_id');

        $brackets = array_values(LateDeductionRule::query()
            ->orderBy('min_minutes')
            ->get()
            ->map(fn (LateDeductionRule $rule) => new LateBracket($rule->min_minutes, $rule->max_minutes, (float) $rule->deduction_amount))
            ->all());

        $monthToDate = $this->monthToDate($run, $users);

        // Personal rate, else the position's rate, in force when the period starts.
        // The schedule default stays null here: the calculator applies it itself.
        $ratesByProfile = array_map(
            fn (ResolvedRate $rate) => $rate->source === RateSource::Default ? null : $rate->rate,
            app(EffectiveRatesQuery::class)->handle($users->map(fn (User $user) => $user->employeeProfile)->filter()->values()->all(), $run->start_date),
        );

        $inputs = [];

        foreach ($users as $user) {
            /** @var Collection<int, TimeLog> $logs */
            $logs = $logsByUser->get($user->id, collect());
            /** @var Collection<string, int> $approved */
            $approved = $approvedByUser->get($user->id, collect());
            /** @var Collection<int, EmployeeDeduction> $loans */
            $loans = $loansByUser->get($user->id, collect());
            /** @var Collection<int, PayrollCarryover> $carryovers */
            $carryovers = $carryoversByUser->get($user->id, collect());
            /** @var Collection<int, PayrollAdjustment> $adjustments */
            $adjustments = $adjustmentsByUser->get($user->id, collect());

            $inputs[$user->id] = new PayslipInput(
                isOfficeStaff: (bool) $user->employeeProfile?->is_office_staff,
                nightMinutes: $this->nightMinutes($logs),
                daysWorked: $logs->count(),
                lateMinutes: (int) $logs->sum('late_minutes'),
                overtimeMinutes: $this->payableOvertime($logs, $approved),
                holidayDaysWorked: $this->holidayDaysWorked($logs, $holidayTypes),
                loans: $this->loanLines($loans),
                lateBrackets: $brackets,
                carryovers: array_values($carryovers->map(fn (PayrollCarryover $carryover) => new CarryoverLine($carryover->id, $carryover->label, (float) $carryover->amount))->all()),
                adjustments: array_values($adjustments->map(fn (PayrollAdjustment $adjustment) => new AdjustmentLine($adjustment->id, $adjustment->lineLabel(), (float) $adjustment->amount, $adjustment->category->isTaxable()))->all()),
                monthToDate: $monthToDate[$user->id],
                dailyRate: $ratesByProfile[$user->employeeProfile->id ?? 0] ?? null,
            );
        }

        return $inputs;
    }

    /**
     * Night minutes over the period, from each day's actual clock-in and
     * clock-out within its shift. A day still open (no clock-out) earns none yet.
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, TimeLog>  $logs
     */
    private function nightMinutes(Collection $logs): int
    {
        $calculator = app(AttendanceCalculator::class);

        return (int) $logs->sum(fn (TimeLog $log) => $log->clock_in_at !== null && $log->clock_out_at !== null
            ? $calculator->nightMinutes($log->clock_in_at, $log->clock_out_at, $log->shift, $log->log_date)
            : 0);
    }

    /**
     * Contributions are monthly. A run that ends on the month's last day is
     * its FINAL cutoff: it needs what the month's earlier runs were due, so
     * it can deduct "monthly − already due". Earlier runs are read through
     * ResolvePayslips: the frozen payslip when generated, else its estimate.
     * (Resolved lazily: ResolvePayslips itself depends on this class.)
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, User>  $users
     * @return array<int, MonthToDate> keyed by user id
     */
    private function monthToDate(PayrollRun $run, Collection $users): array
    {
        $isFinal = $run->end_date->isSameDay($run->end_date->endOfMonth());
        $empty = $users->mapWithKeys(fn (User $user) => [$user->id => new MonthToDate(isFinalCutoff: $isFinal)])->all();

        if (! $isFinal) {
            return $empty;
        }

        $earlierRuns = PayrollRun::query()
            ->whereKeyNot($run->id)
            ->whereDate('start_date', '<', $run->start_date->toDateString())
            ->whereDate('end_date', '>=', $run->end_date->startOfMonth()->toDateString())
            ->whereDate('end_date', '<=', $run->end_date->toDateString())
            ->get();

        if ($earlierRuns->isEmpty()) {
            return $empty;
        }

        $resolver = app(ResolvePayslips::class);
        $months = $empty;

        foreach ($earlierRuns as $earlierRun) {
            foreach ($resolver->handle($earlierRun, $users) as $userId => $payslip) {
                $earlier = $payslip->contributions;

                // No payslip there (no attendance), or one from before the formulas.
                if ($earlier === [] || (! $payslip->isGenerated && $payslip->daysWorked === 0)) {
                    continue;
                }

                $sofar = $months[$userId];
                $months[$userId] = new MonthToDate(
                    isFinalCutoff: true,
                    sss: self::add($sofar->sss, $earlier['sss']),
                    philhealth: self::add($sofar->philhealth, $earlier['philhealth']),
                    pagibig: self::add($sofar->pagibig, $earlier['pagibig']),
                );
            }
        }

        return $months;
    }

    /**
     * @param  array{base: float, employee: float, employer: float, ec: float}  $a
     * @param  array{base: float, employee: float, employer: float, ec: float}  $b
     * @return array{base: float, employee: float, employer: float, ec: float}
     */
    private static function add(array $a, array $b): array
    {
        return [
            'base' => $a['base'] + $b['base'],
            'employee' => $a['employee'] + $b['employee'],
            'employer' => $a['employer'] + $b['employer'],
            'ec' => $a['ec'] + $b['ec'],
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Per day, the smaller of logged and approved overtime. No approved request = 0.
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, TimeLog>  $logs
     * @param  Collection<string, int>  $approvedByDate
     */
    private function payableOvertime(Collection $logs, Collection $approvedByDate): int
    {
        return (int) $logs->sum(fn (TimeLog $log) => min($log->overtime_minutes, $approvedByDate->get($log->log_date->toDateString(), 0)));
    }

    /**
     * Only holidays the employee actually has a time log on: the premium is
     * for WORKING the holiday.
     *
     * @param  Collection<int, TimeLog>  $logs
     * @param  Collection<string, HolidayType>  $holidayTypes
     * @return array<string, int>
     */
    private function holidayDaysWorked(Collection $logs, Collection $holidayTypes): array
    {
        $tally = [];

        foreach ($logs as $log) {
            $type = $holidayTypes->get($log->log_date->toDateString());

            if ($type !== null) {
                $tally[$type->value] = ($tally[$type->value] ?? 0) + 1;
            }
        }

        return $tally;
    }

    /**
     * @param  Collection<int, EmployeeDeduction>  $deductions
     * @return list<LoanLine>
     */
    private function loanLines(Collection $deductions): array
    {
        return array_values($deductions
            ->filter(fn (EmployeeDeduction $deduction) => $deduction->amountDue() > 0)
            ->map(fn (EmployeeDeduction $deduction) => new LoanLine(
                deductionId: $deduction->id,
                label: $deduction->label,
                type: $deduction->type->value,
                amount: round($deduction->amountDue(), 2),
                remainingBalance: $deduction->remaining_balance !== null ? (float) $deduction->remaining_balance : null,
            ))
            ->all());
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Data\PayslipBreakdown;
use App\Data\RateSchedule;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\EmployeeDeduction;
use App\Models\PaidLeavePayment;
use App\Models\PayrollAdjustment;
use App\Models\PayrollCarryover;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\PayslipRecord;
use App\Models\PriorPeriodCorrection;
use App\Models\TimeLog;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Queries\Payroll\PayslipInputsQuery;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use App\Services\Payroll\PayslipCalculator;
use App\Services\Payroll\RateScheduleResolver;
use Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Freezes one employee's payslip for a run: every line is saved to
 * payslip_records, and from then on the SAVED figures are shown, even if
 * rates or attendance change later. Loan balances drop by what was deducted.
 *
 * Net pay never goes below ₱0 (PayslipCalculator). What the pay couldn't
 * cover is saved as payroll_carryovers and deducted first on the next payslip.
 */
final class GeneratePayslip
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly PayslipInputsQuery $inputs,
        private readonly PayslipCalculator $calculator,
        private readonly RateScheduleResolver $rates,
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
        private readonly DetectPriorPeriodCorrections $corrections,
        private readonly PayApprovedReimbursements $reimbursements,
        private readonly DetectPaidLeave $paidLeave,
        private readonly PayDueReferralBonuses $referralBonuses,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  bool  $correctionsChecked  the caller already ran DetectPriorPeriodCorrections for the run (Generate all)
     */
    public function handle(PayrollRun $run, User $employee, User $actor, bool $correctionsChecked = false): PayslipRecord
    {
        // Pay that changed on an earlier cut-off is decided before this payslip is frozen.
        if (! $correctionsChecked) {
            $this->corrections->handle($run, $employee->newCollection([$employee]));
            $this->paidLeave->handle($run, $employee->newCollection([$employee]));
        }

        try {
            return DB::transaction(function () use ($run, $employee, $actor) {
                // Locking the run serializes generation with "advance to approved".
                $lockedRun = PayrollRun::query()->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($run->id);

                if (! $lockedRun->status->canGeneratePayslips()) {
                    throw $this->reject('Payslips can only be generated while the run is processing.');
                }

                if (PayslipRecord::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $lockedRun->id)->where('user_id', $employee->id)->exists()) {
                    throw $this->reject("{$employee->name}'s payslip has already been generated for this run.");
                }

                if (PayrollAdjustment::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $lockedRun->id)->where('user_id', $employee->id)->pending()->exists()) {
                    throw $this->reject("{$employee->name} has an adjustment awaiting approval. Approve or reject it first.");
                }

                $correction = PriorPeriodCorrection::query()->with('fromRun')->where('payroll_run_id', $lockedRun->id)->where('user_id', $employee->id)->suggested()->first();
                if ($correction !== null) {
                    throw $this->reject("{$employee->name}'s pay for {$correction->fromRun->periodLabel()} changed after it was paid (".($correction->amount >= 0 ? '+' : '−').'₱'.number_format(abs((float) $correction->amount), 2).'). Accept or dismiss it under "Corrections from earlier cut-offs" first.');
                }

                if (PaidLeavePayment::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $lockedRun->id)->where('user_id', $employee->id)->suggested()->exists()) {
                    throw $this->reject("{$employee->name} has paid leave in this cut-off. Accept or dismiss it under \"Paid leave this cut-off\" first.");
                }

                if (($earlier = $this->blockingEarlierRun($lockedRun, $employee)) !== null) {
                    throw $this->reject("Generate {$employee->name}'s {$earlier->periodLabel()} payslip first: this one balances the month's SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG against it.");
                }

                $employee->loadMissing('employeeProfile');

                // Approved reimbursements become lines on this payslip before it's computed.
                $this->reimbursements->handle($lockedRun, $employee, $actor);
                // So do referral bonuses that fell due by the end of this cut-off.
                $this->referralBonuses->handle($lockedRun, $employee, $actor);

                $input = $this->inputs->handle($lockedRun, collect([$employee]))[$employee->id];

                // No attendance is fine when the law pays their leave (e.g. paternity leave the whole cut-off).
                $paidLeave = PaidLeavePayment::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $lockedRun->id)->where('user_id', $employee->id)->where('status', PaidLeavePayment::ACCEPTED)->exists();

                if ($input->daysWorked === 0 && ! $paidLeave) {
                    throw $this->reject("{$employee->name} has no attendance in this period, so there is nothing to pay.");
                }

                $schedule = $this->rates->forDate($lockedRun->start_date);

                if (! self::hasRate($input->dailyRate, $schedule, $input->isOfficeStaff)) {
                    throw $this->reject("{$employee->name} has no daily rate yet. Accounting sets it on Daily Rates (a personal rate, or the rate for their position).");
                }

                $breakdown = $this->calculator->calculate($input, $schedule);

                $record = new PayslipRecord;
                $record->forceFill([
                    ...$breakdown->toRecordAttributes(),
                    'payroll_run_id' => $lockedRun->id,
                    'user_id' => $employee->id,
                    'generated_at' => now(),
                    'generated_by' => $actor->id,
                ])->save();

                // Balances drop by what was ACTUALLY deducted: when the pay ran
                // out, an installment may be partly or not at all taken.
                foreach ($breakdown->loanLines as $line) {
                    if (isset($line['deduction_id']) && $line['amount'] > 0) {
                        $this->consumeInstallment($line['deduction_id'], $line['amount']);
                    }
                }

                $this->settleCarryovers($lockedRun, $employee, $breakdown);

                $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, 'payslip.generated', "Generated payslip of {$employee->name} for {$lockedRun->periodLabel()}", $record, [
                    'new' => [
                        'gross_pay' => $record->gross_pay,
                        'total_deductions' => $record->total_deductions,
                        'net_pay' => $record->net_pay,
                        'rate_schedule' => $record->rate_schedule,
                        'carried_in' => $record->carryover_deductions,
                        'carried_forward' => $breakdown->shortfall() > 0 ? number_format($breakdown->shortfall(), 2, '.', '') : null,
                    ],
                ], causer: $actor);

                return $record;
            });
        } catch (UniqueConstraintViolationException) {
            // A second request raced past the exists() check; the unique index stopped it.
            throw $this->reject("{$employee->name}'s payslip has already been generated for this run.");
        }
    }

    /**
     * Reduces the remaining balance by what this payslip took, never below 0.
     * A fully paid loan switches itself off.
     */
    private function consumeInstallment(int $deductionId, float $amount): void
    {
        $deduction = EmployeeDeduction::query()->lockForUpdate()->find($deductionId);

        if ($deduction === null || $deduction->remaining_balance === null) {
            return;
        }

        $remaining = max(0.0, round((float) $deduction->remaining_balance - $amount, 2));

        $deduction->forceFill([
            'remaining_balance' => number_format($remaining, 2, '.', ''),
            'is_active' => $remaining > 0,
        ])->save();
    }

    /**
     * The month's LAST cutoff deducts "monthly contribution − what earlier
     * cutoffs were due", so an earlier cutoff the employee worked must be
     * frozen first; otherwise it could later deduct something different from
     * the estimate this payslip subtracted. Returns that earlier run, if any.
     */
    /**
     * A rate of their own, or a company default above ₱0. From 2026 the
     * default is ₱0: nobody is paid on a made-up rate.
     */
    public static function hasRate(?float $dailyRate, RateSchedule $schedule, bool $isOfficeStaff): bool
    {
        return ($dailyRate ?? $schedule->dailyRate($isOfficeStaff)) > 0;
    }

    public function blockingEarlierRun(PayrollRun $run, User $employee): ?PayrollRun
    {
        if (! $run->end_date->isSameDay($run->end_date->endOfMonth()) || ! $this->rates->forDate($run->start_date)->usesStatutoryFormulas()) {
            return null;
        }

        return PayrollRun::query()
            ->whereKeyNot($run->id)
            ->whereDate('start_date', '<', $run->start_date->toDateString())
            ->whereDate('end_date', '>=', $run->end_date->startOfMonth()->toDateString())
            ->whereDate('end_date', '<=', $run->end_date->toDateString())
            ->orderBy('start_date')
            ->get()
            ->first(fn (PayrollRun $earlier) => $this->rates->forDate($earlier->start_date)->usesStatutoryFormulas()
                && TimeLog::query()->where('user_id', $employee->id)->between($earlier->start_date, $earlier->end_date)->exists()
                && ! PayslipRecord::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $earlier->id)->where('user_id', $employee->id)->exists());
    }

    /**
     * Every carry-over this payslip brought in is settled here, even if only
     * partly covered: its unpaid remainder is in the shortfall list, and so
     * becomes a NEW carry-over from this run. One rule, no partial rows.
     */
    private function settleCarryovers(PayrollRun $run, User $employee, PayslipBreakdown $breakdown): void
    {
        $broughtIn = array_column($breakdown->carryoverLines, 'carryover_id');

        if ($broughtIn !== []) {
            PayrollCarryover::query()
                ->whereIn('id', $broughtIn)
                ->whereNull('settled_in_payroll_run_id')
                ->lockForUpdate()
                ->get()
                ->each(fn (PayrollCarryover $carryover) => $carryover->forceFill(['settled_in_payroll_run_id' => $run->id])->save());
        }

        foreach ($breakdown->shortfallLines as $shortfall) {
            if (! $shortfall['carries']) {
                continue; // a loan installment: it stays in the loan's balance
            }

            // A carried line already names its first period; don't stack "(from …)" twice.
            $label = str_contains($shortfall['label'], '(from ') ? $shortfall['label'] : "{$shortfall['label']} (from {$run->periodLabel()})";

            $carryover = new PayrollCarryover;
            $carryover->forceFill([
                'user_id' => $employee->id,
                'from_payroll_run_id' => $run->id,
                'label' => $label,
                'amount' => number_format($shortfall['amount'], 2, '.', ''),
            ])->save();
        }
    }

    private function reject(string $message): ValidationException
    {
        return ValidationException::withMessages(['payslip' => $message]);
    }
}

<?php

/**
 * Pay rates and statutory amounts, keyed by the date each set took effect.
 *
 * A payroll run uses the schedule in force on its START DATE, never today's,
 * so reopening an old run reproduces the figures it was computed with. See
 * App\Services\Payroll\RateScheduleResolver.
 *
 * To change a rate: ADD a new entry keyed by the date it takes effect.
 * Never edit or delete a past entry — older entries are what keep historical
 * payslips reproducible.
 */
return [

    'schedules' => [

        '1970-01-01' => [
            'daily_rate' => ['field' => 610, 'office' => 900],
            'sss' => ['field' => 581, 'office' => 900],
            'philhealth' => ['field' => 225, 'office' => 400],
            'pagibig' => ['field' => 100, 'office' => 100],

            // Office staff only. Field staff are minimum wage earners, exempt under RA 9504.
            'withholding_rate' => ['field' => 0.0, 'office' => 0.02],
        ],

        /*
         * From 2026: contributions and tax are COMPUTED from the government
         * rules instead of fixed amounts (verified 2026-10-09; have Accounting
         * check them against the circulars before the first live payroll):
         *
         *   SSS        RA 11199: 15% of the Monthly Salary Credit (5% employee,
         *              10% employer), MSC ₱5,000–₱35,000 in ₱500 steps, + EC.
         *   PhilHealth RA 11223: 5% of monthly basic salary, split 2.5% / 2.5%,
         *              floor ₱10,000, ceiling ₱100,000.
         *   Pag-IBIG   RA 9679 / HDMF Circular 460: 2% each (employee 1% at
         *              ₱1,500 or less), Maximum Fund Salary ₱10,000.
         *   Tax        RR 11-2018 semi-monthly table, rates effective 2023.
         *
         * These are MONTHLY contributions: the 1st–15th payslip deducts half,
         * the month's last payslip deducts the rest based on the actual month.
         */
        '2026-01-01' => [
            // No made-up default: a newly onboarded employee has NO rate (₱0,
            // shown as "Not set") until Accounting sets their position's rate or a
            // personal one on Daily Rates. Payroll refuses to generate a payslip
            // without a rate. The 1970 schedule keeps ₱610/₱900 for old payslips.
            'daily_rate' => ['field' => 0, 'office' => 0],

            'statutory' => [
                'sss' => [
                    'employee_rate' => 0.05,
                    'employer_rate' => 0.10,
                    'msc_min' => 5000,
                    'msc_max' => 35000,
                    'msc_step' => 500,
                    // Employees' Compensation (employer only): ₱10 below MSC ₱15,000, ₱30 from it.
                    'ec_low' => 10,
                    'ec_high' => 30,
                    'ec_high_from_msc' => 15000,
                ],
                'philhealth' => [
                    'rate' => 0.05,
                    'floor' => 10000,
                    'ceiling' => 100000,
                ],
                'pagibig' => [
                    'employee_rate' => 0.02,
                    'employee_rate_low' => 0.01,
                    'low_threshold' => 1500,
                    'employer_rate' => 0.02,
                    'max_fund_salary' => 10000,
                ],
                // Semi-monthly withholding: over ₱X → base + rate × (taxable − X).
                'withholding_semi_monthly' => [
                    ['over' => 0, 'base' => 0, 'rate' => 0],
                    ['over' => 10417, 'base' => 0, 'rate' => 0.15],
                    ['over' => 16667, 'base' => 937.50, 'rate' => 0.20],
                    ['over' => 33333, 'base' => 4270.70, 'rate' => 0.25],
                    ['over' => 83333, 'base' => 16770.70, 'rate' => 0.30],
                    ['over' => 333333, 'base' => 91770.70, 'rate' => 0.35],
                ],
            ],
        ],

    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Minimum wage (NCR, non-agriculture), by the date each wage order took effect
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Decides who is a minimum wage earner (tax exempt) and warns Accounting
    | when a configured daily rate is below the law. Add a line per new wage
    | order; never edit a past one.
    |
    */

    'minimum_wages' => [
        '2025-07-17' => ['amount' => 695, 'wage_order' => 'NCR-26'],
        '2026-09-26' => ['amount' => 755, 'wage_order' => 'NCR-28'],
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Statutory multipliers (Labor Code)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Holiday premiums are paid ON TOP of basic pay, because basic pay already
    | covers every day with a time log: a worked regular holiday totals 200%,
    | a worked special non-working day 130%. An unworked holiday earns nothing.
    |
    */

    'holiday_premiums' => [
        'regular' => 1.00,
        'special_non_working' => 0.30,
    ],

    'night_differential_rate' => 0.10,

    'overtime_multiplier' => 1.25,

    'standard_hours_per_day' => 8,

    // Printed under every payslip. Corrections never rewrite a past payslip;
    // they are added as lines on the next payroll.
    /*
     * Payslip adjustments (corrections, allowances, refunds, penalties).
     *
     * Accounting has full control of payroll, so adjustments apply at once
     * (decided 2026-10-09). Every one is audited either way.
     *
     * Optional second-person check: set an amount (e.g. 5000) and adjustments
     * of that size or larger wait for someone with approve-payroll-adjustments
     * who isn't their creator. null = off.
     */
    'adjustments' => [
        'approval_threshold' => env('PAYROLL_ADJUSTMENT_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD') ?: null,
    ],

    /*
     * Corrections from earlier cut-offs: before payslips are generated, every
     * paid cut-off that ended within this many days is recomputed with today's
     * attendance, overtime, holidays and rates. A difference is suggested on the
     * open run for Accounting to accept or dismiss (DetectPriorPeriodCorrections).
     */
    'prior_period' => [
        'lookback_days' => 90,
    ],

    /*
     * "Report a problem" on a payslip: the optional photo or PDF is kept on this
     * PRIVATE disk (never a public URL), like load receipts.
     */
    'concerns' => [
        'disk' => env('PAYROLL_CONCERNS_DISK') ?: env('ATTENDANCE_PHOTO_DISK', 'local'),
    ],

    /*
     * Reimbursements and deployment claims: company policy, not law. Only the
     * STARTING values: Accounting sets them on the Reimbursements page (Limits),
     * saved as the "reimbursements" Setting and audited (Reimbursement::limits()).
     */
    'reimbursements' => [
        'file_within_days' => 60,
        'max_amount' => 20000,
        'deployment_max_amount' => 20000,
    ],

    'disclaimer' => 'Payroll figures are subject to change with prior notice. Any adjustment will be reflected in the next payroll.',

];
Question you'd askAnswer
Why look rates up by the run's start date?So reopening a past run gives the figures it was paid with. To change a rate, add a dated entry; never edit an old one.
Why is the holiday line only the premium?Basic pay already covers every day with a time log. Adding 200% on top would pay the day three times.
What stops a payslip being generated twice?A locked run row, an existence check, and the unique (payroll_run_id, user_id) index for the race that slips past both.
Why can't accounting edit figures any more?Every peso should be explainable from attendance and rates. Manual corrections deserve their own audited "adjustment" feature.
Why are money columns decimal, written as strings?A float can't store 0.10 exactly. Strings like "7787.00" go into the database unchanged.

Net pay never goes below ₱0

One day worked earns ₱610, but ₱906 of contributions are due. The calculator takes deductions in a fixed order and stops when the pay runs out: SSS → PhilHealth → Pag-IBIG → tax → carried over → late → loans. The rest is a shortfall, listed on the payslip. Contributions, tax, late and earlier carry-overs go to payroll_carryovers and come off the next payslip first. An unpaid loan installment is not carried, because the loan balance only drops by what was actually taken.

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;

/**
 * A deduction a payslip could not cover, owed on the next one. Written only
 * by GeneratePayslip: created from a payslip's shortfall, settled when a
 * later payslip brings it in.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property int $user_id
 * @property int $from_payroll_run_id
 * @property string $label
 * @property string $amount
 * @property int|null $settled_in_payroll_run_id
 * @property CarbonImmutable $created_at
 * @property CarbonImmutable $updated_at
 * @property-read PayrollRun $fromRun
 */
class PayrollCarryover extends Model
{
    /**
     * @var array<string, mixed>
     */
    protected $attributes = [
        'settled_in_payroll_run_id' => null,
    ];

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['amount' => 'decimal:2'];
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<PayrollRun, $this>
     */
    public function fromRun(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(PayrollRun::class, 'from_payroll_run_id');
    }

    /**
     * Still owed, and from a run that started before $run (so generating an
     * OLDER run later never pulls in a newer run's shortfall).
     *
     * @param  Builder<PayrollCarryover>  $query
     */
    public function scopeOwedBefore(Builder $query, PayrollRun $run): void
    {
        $query->whereNull('settled_in_payroll_run_id')
            ->whereHas('fromRun', fn (Builder $from) => $from->whereDate('start_date', '<', $run->start_date->toDateString()));
    }
}
QuestionAnswer
Why are carry-overs taken right after the contributions, before late and loans?They are mostly unpaid contributions from last time. Government remittances come first.
Why settle a carry-over even when it was only partly covered?One rule, no partial rows: the unpaid remainder is in this payslip's shortfall, so it becomes a new carry-over from this run.
Why owedBefore($run)?If Accounting generates an older run late, it must not pull in a shortfall from a newer one.
Why a new migration instead of editing the payroll one?Existing databases (yours, and production later) only need php artisan migrate. Editing an old migration would force a full reset.

Government contributions and tax (2026)

From the 2026 schedule, contributions and tax are computed from the rules, not fixed amounts: SSS 5% of the Monthly Salary Credit (₱5,000–₱35,000 in ₱500 steps), PhilHealth 2.5% of basic pay (floor ₱10,000), Pag-IBIG 2% up to ₱200 a month, and the BIR semi-monthly table on pay after those three. Anyone paid at or below the minimum wage (NCR ₱755 from Sept 26, 2026) pays no tax. The contributions are monthly: the 1st–15th payslip takes half the estimate, and the month's last payslip takes the actual monthly amount minus what the first took.

<?php

namespace App\Services\Payroll;

use App\Data\StatutoryRules;

/**
 * The government formulas, and nothing else. Pure: no queries, no config, so
 * each rule is unit tested with plain numbers (tests/Unit/StatutoryContributionsTest).
 *
 * Every amount here is MONTHLY except withholding, which uses the BIR
 * semi-monthly table because payroll runs twice a month.
 */
final class StatutoryContributions
{
    /**
     * SSS: the Monthly Salary Credit is the bracket the month's compensation
     * falls in (₱500 steps: ₱5,250–5,749.99 → ₱5,500), clamped to the min/max.
     *
     * @return array{msc: float, employee: float, employer: float, ec: float}
     */
    public function sss(StatutoryRules $rules, float $monthlyCompensation): array
    {
        $step = $rules->sssMscStep;
        $msc = $step * floor(($monthlyCompensation + $step / 2) / $step);
        $msc = min($rules->sssMscMax, max($rules->sssMscMin, $msc));

        return [
            'msc' => $msc,
            'employee' => round($msc * $rules->sssEmployeeRate, 2),
            'employer' => round($msc * $rules->sssEmployerRate, 2),
            // Employees' Compensation: employer only.
            'ec' => $msc >= $rules->sssEcHighFromMsc ? $rules->sssEcHigh : $rules->sssEcLow,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * PhilHealth: 5% of monthly basic salary between the floor and ceiling,
     * shared equally by employee and employer.
     *
     * @return array{base: float, employee: float, employer: float}
     */
    public function philhealth(StatutoryRules $rules, float $monthlyBasic): array
    {
        $base = min($rules->philhealthCeiling, max($rules->philhealthFloor, $monthlyBasic));
        $premium = round($base * $rules->philhealthRate, 2);
        $employee = round($premium / 2, 2);

        return ['base' => $base, 'employee' => $employee, 'employer' => round($premium - $employee, 2)];
    }

    /**
     * Pag-IBIG: on monthly compensation up to the Maximum Fund Salary;
     * 1% from the employee at ₱1,500 or less, 2% above. Employer 2%.
     *
     * @return array{base: float, employee: float, employer: float}
     */
    public function pagibig(StatutoryRules $rules, float $monthlyCompensation): array
    {
        $base = min($rules->pagibigMaxFundSalary, max(0.0, $monthlyCompensation));
        $employeeRate = $monthlyCompensation <= $rules->pagibigLowThreshold ? $rules->pagibigEmployeeRateLow : $rules->pagibigEmployeeRate;

        return [
            'base' => $base,
            'employee' => round($base * $employeeRate, 2),
            'employer' => round($base * $rules->pagibigEmployerRate, 2),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * BIR withholding on one semi-monthly cutoff's taxable compensation
     * (gross taxable pay minus the employee's SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG):
     * the bracket's fixed amount plus its rate on the excess.
     */
    public function withholdingSemiMonthly(StatutoryRules $rules, float $taxable): float
    {
        $bracket = $this->bracketFor($rules, $taxable);

        return $bracket === null ? 0.0 : round(max(0.0, $bracket['base'] + ($taxable - $bracket['over']) * $bracket['rate']), 2);
    }

    /**
     * The bracket the taxable amount falls in, for showing the working.
     *
     * @return array{over: float, base: float, rate: float}|null
     */
    public function bracketFor(StatutoryRules $rules, float $taxable): ?array
    {
        $found = null;

        foreach ($rules->withholdingSemiMonthly as $bracket) {
            if ($taxable > $bracket['over']) {
                $found = $bracket;
            }
        }

        return $found;
    }
}
QuestionAnswer
Why a new schedule instead of changing the old amounts?Rate schedules are dated. Runs before 2026 keep the spec's fixed amounts, so their figures still reproduce, and a test proves the old ₱7,787 example still holds.
Why can't the 16th–end payslip be generated before the 1st–15th?It balances the month against the first cutoff. If the first could still change afterwards, the month would no longer add up.
Why store the employer share on a payslip?The employer pays it too, and the monthly SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG remittances need both shares per employee. It's in the CSV export.
Why a red banner instead of raising the rate automatically?Pay rates are a business and legal decision. The system makes the problem impossible to miss, and HR or Accounting fixes the rate.

Rates and rules from Accounting, and the viewers

Each employee's daily rate has the date it takes effect. Accounting sets it on Daily Rates, because payroll is theirs: a company rate per position (Security Guard, Shift-in-Charge, Office Staff…), and a personal rate only for exceptions. Payroll pays the personal rate, else the position's (EffectiveRatesQuery). There's no made-up default from 2026: a new hire shows Not set (₱0), and their payslip can't be generated until Accounting sets a rate. HR sees it read-only on the employee record, and is told "Set by Accounting" in a tooltip. When HR adds someone, Accounting gets a Daily rate needed notice. Accounting maintains the rules on Tax & Contributions as dated versions, and a version can never start inside a period whose payslips are already generated. To check the numbers, use the run's Contributions & tax tab (everyone's shares at a glance) and each payslip's How this was computed panel.

The page's second tab, How it's computed (PH law), explains each deduction with its law (RA 11199 for SSS, RA 11223 for PhilHealth, RA 9679 and HDMF Circular 460 for Pag-IBIG, TRAIN / RR 11-2018 for tax, RA 9504 for minimum wage earners) and the values in force. Its calculator runs the real payroll calculator for a whole month: for example ₱1,200 × 26 days gives SSS ₱1,550, PhilHealth ₱780, Pag-IBIG ₱200 and tax ₱587.70 per cutoff. It also lists what isn't computed yet, such as 13th month pay.

Two safety rules: new hires are flagged on Daily Rates (and in Accounting's bell) until they have a rate; and Approve run stays locked, with the reason in a tooltip, until the period has ended, since attendance, leave and overtime can still change. Payslips can still be generated early to check.

<?php

namespace App\Actions\People;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\EmployeeProfile;
use App\Models\EmployeeRate;
use App\Models\PayslipRecord;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\UpdateNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Accounting sets an employee's daily rate from a date (HR only sees it). A raise is a new row; the
 * same date again replaces that row (a typo fix), unless a generated payslip
 * already used the period: then the change must start later.
 */
final class SetEmployeeRate
{
    public function __construct(private readonly AuditLogger $audit) {}

    public function handle(EmployeeProfile $profile, float $dailyRate, CarbonImmutable $effectiveFrom, ?string $note, User $actor): EmployeeRate
    {
        if (! $actor->can(Ability::ManagePayroll->value)) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        if ($dailyRate <= 0 || $dailyRate > 100000) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['rateAmount' => 'Enter a daily rate between ₱1 and ₱100,000.']);
        }

        // A payslip already frozen with this employee's rate must not be contradicted.
        $frozenFrom = $profile->user_id === null ? null : PayslipRecord::query()
            ->where('user_id', $profile->user_id)
            ->join('payroll_runs', 'payroll_runs.id', '=', 'payslip_records.payroll_run_id')
            ->whereDate('payroll_runs.end_date', '>=', $effectiveFrom->toDateString())
            ->max('payroll_runs.end_date');

        if ($frozenFrom !== null) {
            $after = CarbonImmutable::parse((string) $frozenFrom)->addDay();

            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['rateEffectiveFrom' => "A payslip up to {$after->subDay()->format('M j, Y')} is already generated with the old rate. Start the new rate on {$after->format('M j, Y')} or later."]);
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($profile, $dailyRate, $effectiveFrom, $note, $actor) {
            $rate = EmployeeRate::query()
                ->where('employee_profile_id', $profile->id)
                ->whereDate('effective_from', $effectiveFrom->toDateString())
                ->lockForUpdate()
                ->first() ?? new EmployeeRate;

            $previous = $rate->exists ? (float) $rate->daily_rate : null;

            $rate->forceFill([
                'employee_profile_id' => $profile->id,
                'daily_rate' => number_format($dailyRate, 2, '.', ''),
                'effective_from' => $effectiveFrom->toDateString(),
                'note' => filled($note) ? $note : null,
                'set_by' => $actor->id,
            ])->save();

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::People, 'rate.set', "Daily rate of {$profile->name}: ₱".number_format($dailyRate, 2)." from {$effectiveFrom->format('M j, Y')}", $rate, [
                'old' => ['daily_rate' => $previous],
                'new' => ['daily_rate' => $dailyRate, 'effective_from' => $effectiveFrom->toDateString()],
                'note' => $rate->note,
            ], causer: $actor);

            UpdateNotice::tellProfile($profile, $actor, 'Your daily rate: ₱'.number_format($dailyRate, 2),
                "From {$effectiveFrom->format('M j, Y')}. Your payslips use it from the cut-off that starts then.", route('payslips'), 'banknotes', email: true);

            return $rate;
        });
    }
}
app/Actions/Payroll/SaveStatutoryRuleSet.php75 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\StatutoryRuleSet;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Queries\Payroll\FrozenPayrollUntilQuery;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Accounting saves a version of the SSS / PhilHealth / Pag-IBIG / BIR rules
 * from a date. Payroll periods starting on or after it use the new rules;
 * generated payslips never change. The same date again replaces that version
 * (fixing a typo before it's used).
 */
final class SaveStatutoryRuleSet
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly FrozenPayrollUntilQuery $frozen,
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  array{sss: array<string, float>, philhealth: array<string, float>, pagibig: array<string, float>, withholding_semi_monthly: list<array{over: float, base: float, rate: float}>}  $rules  rates as fractions (0.05)
     */
    public function handle(array $rules, CarbonImmutable $effectiveFrom, ?string $note, User $actor): StatutoryRuleSet
    {
        if (! $actor->can(Ability::ManagePayroll->value)) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        if (($message = $this->frozen->tooEarly($effectiveFrom)) !== null) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['effectiveFrom' => $message]);
        }

        $brackets = $rules['withholding_semi_monthly'];
        usort($brackets, fn (array $a, array $b) => $a['over'] <=> $b['over']);

        if ($brackets === [] || $brackets[0]['over'] != 0.0) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['rules.withholding_semi_monthly' => 'The tax table must start with a bracket "over ₱0".']);
        }

        if ($rules['sss']['msc_min'] >= $rules['sss']['msc_max'] || $rules['philhealth']['floor'] >= $rules['philhealth']['ceiling']) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['rules.sss.msc_max' => 'Each maximum must be above its minimum.']);
        }

        $rules['withholding_semi_monthly'] = $brackets;

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($rules, $effectiveFrom, $note, $actor) {
            $version = StatutoryRuleSet::query()->whereDate('effective_from', $effectiveFrom->toDateString())->lockForUpdate()->first() ?? new StatutoryRuleSet;
            $previous = $version->exists ? $version->rules : null;

            $version->forceFill([
                'effective_from' => $effectiveFrom->toDateString(),
                'rules' => $rules,
                'note' => filled($note) ? $note : null,
                'created_by' => $actor->id,
            ])->save();

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Settings, 'statutory.saved', "Saved tax and contribution rules from {$effectiveFrom->format('M j, Y')}", $version, [
                'old' => $previous,
                'new' => $rules,
                'note' => $version->note,
            ], causer: $actor);

            return $version;
        });
    }
}
app/Queries/Payroll/FrozenPayrollUntilQuery.php35 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Queries\Payroll;

use App\Models\PayslipRecord;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;

/**
 * The last day covered by any generated payslip. Rules (tax, contributions,
 * minimum wage) may only change from the day after: a frozen payslip and its
 * "how this was computed" must keep telling the truth.
 */
final class FrozenPayrollUntilQuery
{
    public function handle(): ?CarbonImmutable
    {
        $last = PayslipRecord::query()
            ->join('payroll_runs', 'payroll_runs.id', '=', 'payslip_records.payroll_run_id')
            ->max('payroll_runs.end_date');

        return $last !== null ? CarbonImmutable::parse((string) $last)->startOfDay() : null;
    }

    /**
     * A ValidationException-ready message when $from is too early, else null.
     */
    public function tooEarly(CarbonImmutable $from): ?string
    {
        $until = $this->handle();

        return $until !== null && $from->lessThanOrEqualTo($until)
            ? "Payslips up to {$until->format('M j, Y')} are already generated with the current rules. Choose {$until->addDay()->format('M j, Y')} or later."
            : null;
    }
}

QuestionAnswer
Why does HR set rates, not Accounting?A rate is part of the employment terms HR keeps. Accounting applies it. Separating the two means nobody both sets a pay rate and pays it.
Why "effective from" instead of one rate field?A raise on Oct 16 must not change Oct 1–15. Each payroll looks up the rate in force when its period starts.
Why do rules live in the database now, with config as a fallback?Accounting changes them when a circular comes out, without waiting for a deploy. Config keeps the app working on a fresh install.

Adjustments: correct a payslip without editing it

Accounting never types over a calculated amount. A correction is its own line with a reason: correction, allowance, refund, penalty or other. Every peso still traces back to attendance, rates, a loan, or a named and dated adjustment. Accounting has full control of payroll, so adjustments apply at once. An optional second-person check (off by default) can hold large ones for a Super Admin, who can never be the creator.

Loans need authority first (Art. 113). A loan, cash advance, uniform, equipment or other deduction is only taken with a basis. Accounting picks one when adding it (DeductionAuthorizationBasis):

  • Ask the employee in the app, the default. Nothing is taken until they tick I authorize this on My Payslips, and their exact sentence is saved with the time, in English or Filipino. I don't agree takes nothing and tells Accounting.
  • A signed paper.
  • The law itself: SSS and Pag-IBIG salary loans.

PayslipInputsQuery reads EmployeeDeduction::takenFromPay(), so a deduction still waiting never reaches a payslip.

My Loans shows the employee each loan's balance, how it was authorized (in their words) and every payslip that took from it. It reads the payslips' own frozen loan lines (deduction_id), so the history can't disagree with what was paid.

Paid leave this cut-off. Leave the law pays is suggested on the run (DetectPaidLeave), never added silently:

  • Paternity, solo parent, VAWC, special leave for women: the days in the cut-off × the daily rate, capped by what the law gives across cut-offs. Accepting adds a taxable Paid leave adjustment, and Accounting can pay fewer days.
  • Maternity: the employer advances the SSS benefit, computed from the SSS salary credit, so Accounting enters it as a non-taxable allowance.

Someone with no attendance but accepted paid leave is still due a payslip (User::scopeDueAPayslip).

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\LeaveType;
use App\Models\LeaveRequest;
use App\Models\PaidLeavePayment;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\PayslipRecord;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Queries\People\EffectiveRatesQuery;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;

/**
 * Suggests the leave the law pays on a payroll run: each approved maternity,
 * paternity, solo parent, VAWC or special leave for women that overlaps the
 * cut-off, for Accounting to accept or dismiss (PaidLeaveSuggestions).
 *
 *   days    the leave's days inside this cut-off, capped by what the law gives
 *           (LeaveType::maxDays) less what earlier runs already suggested or paid
 *   amount  days × the daily rate on the cut-off's start; maternity has none (the
 *           SSS benefit is computed from the SSS salary credit: Accounting enters it)
 *
 * Run when a run starts processing, before "Generate all", and before one payslip.
 * Idempotent: one row per leave and run, never re-suggested once decided.
 */
final class DetectPaidLeave
{
    public function __construct(private readonly EffectiveRatesQuery $rates) {}

    /**
     * @param  Collection<int, User>|null  $employees  only these (one payslip); null: everyone
     * @return int how many are waiting for Accounting on this run
     */
    public function handle(PayrollRun $run, ?Collection $employees = null): int
    {
        $start = CarbonImmutable::parse($run->start_date);
        $end = CarbonImmutable::parse($run->end_date);
        $ids = $employees?->modelKeys();

        $leaves = LeaveRequest::query()->approved()
            ->whereIn('type', LeaveType::paidByLawValues())
            ->overlapping($start, $end)
            ->when($ids !== null, fn ($query) => $query->whereIn('user_id', $ids))
            ->with('user.employeeProfile')
            ->get();

        foreach ($leaves as $leave) {
            $profile = $leave->user->employeeProfile;

            // Already decided or suggested on this run, or the payslip is already frozen.
            if ($profile === null
                || PaidLeavePayment::query()->where('leave_request_id', $leave->id)->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)->exists()
                || PayslipRecord::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)->where('user_id', $leave->user_id)->exists()) {
                continue;
            }

            $from = $leave->start_date->max($start);
            $to = $leave->end_date->min($end);
            $days = (int) $from->diffInDays($to) + 1;

            // What the law gives, less what earlier runs already took (not dismissed).
            if (($max = $leave->type->maxDays()) !== null) {
                $used = (int) PaidLeavePayment::query()->where('leave_request_id', $leave->id)->where('status', '!=', PaidLeavePayment::DISMISSED)->sum('days');
                $days = min($days, $max - $used);
            }

            if ($days <= 0) {
                continue;
            }

            $rate = $leave->type->paidAsSssBenefit() ? null : ($this->rates->handle([$profile], $start)[$profile->id]->rate ?? 0.0);

            $payment = new PaidLeavePayment;
            $payment->forceFill([
                'payroll_run_id' => $run->id,
                'user_id' => $leave->user_id,
                'leave_request_id' => $leave->id,
                'days' => $days,
                'daily_rate' => $rate,
                'amount' => $rate !== null ? round($days * $rate, 2) : null,
            ])->save();
        }

        return PaidLeavePayment::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)
            ->when($ids !== null, fn ($query) => $query->whereIn('user_id', $ids))
            ->suggested()->count();
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\EmployeeDeduction;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\DeductionAuthorizationNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Notification;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * The employee answers a deduction Accounting asked them to authorize (Art. 113).
 * Authorized: their sentence is saved word for word with the time, and payslips
 * take it from now on. Declined: nothing is taken; Accounting is told either way.
 */
final class AnswerDeductionAuthorization
{
    public function __construct(private readonly AuditLogger $audit) {}

    public function handle(User $employee, EmployeeDeduction $deduction, bool $authorize, string $locale = 'en'): EmployeeDeduction
    {
        if ($deduction->user_id !== $employee->id) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($employee, $deduction, $authorize, $locale) {
            $locked = EmployeeDeduction::query()->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($deduction->id);

            if (! $locked->awaiting_authorization || $locked->declined_at !== null) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['deduction' => 'This one was already answered.']);
            }

            if ($authorize) {
                $locked->forceFill(['awaiting_authorization' => false, 'authorization' => $locked->authorizationText($locale), 'authorized_at' => now()])->save();
            } else {
                $locked->forceFill(['declined_at' => now()])->save();
            }

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, $authorize ? 'deduction.authorized' : 'deduction.declined', ($authorize ? "{$employee->name} authorized" : "{$employee->name} declined")." {$locked->type->label()} \"{$locked->label}\"", $locked, causer: $employee);

            Notification::send(
                User::query()->notifiable(Ability::ManagePayroll->roles())->whereKeyNot($employee->id)->get(),
                new DeductionAuthorizationNotice($locked->setRelation('user', $employee), $authorize ? DeductionAuthorizationNotice::AUTHORIZED : DeductionAuthorizationNotice::DECLINED),
            );

            return $locked;
        });
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AdjustmentCategory;
use App\Enums\AdjustmentStatus;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\PayrollAdjustment;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\PayslipRecord;
use App\Models\TimeLog;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\PayrollAdjustmentAwaitingApproval;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Notification;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * A correction on one payslip, as its own line with a reason: never an edit
 * of the calculated figures.
 *
 * They apply at once: Accounting has full control of payroll. Only if
 * payroll.adjustments.approval_threshold is set do adjustments of that size
 * wait for a second person (approve-payroll-adjustments), unless the creator
 * holds that gate already.
 */
final class AddPayrollAdjustment
{
    public function __construct(private readonly AuditLogger $audit) {}

    /**
     * @param  float  $amount  signed: positive adds to pay, negative is deducted
     * @param  bool  $forPaidLeave  from AcceptPaidLeave: leave the law pays makes them due a payslip
     *                              even with no attendance (e.g. paternity leave the whole cut-off)
     */
    public function handle(PayrollRun $run, User $employee, AdjustmentCategory $category, float $amount, string $reason, User $actor, bool $forPaidLeave = false): PayrollAdjustment
    {
        if (! $actor->can(Ability::ManagePayroll->value)) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        $amount = round($amount, 2);

        $errors = array_filter([
            'adjustmentAmount' => match (true) {
                $amount === 0.0 => 'Enter an amount.',
                $amount > 0 && ! $category->allowsAddition() => "A {$category->label()} can only be deducted.",
                $amount < 0 && ! $category->allowsDeduction() => "A {$category->label()} can only add to pay.",
                default => null,
            },
            'adjustmentReason' => mb_strlen(trim($reason)) < 5 ? 'Explain the adjustment (at least a few words).' : null,
        ]);

        if ($errors !== []) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages($errors);
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($run, $employee, $category, $amount, $reason, $actor, $forPaidLeave) {
            // Locked with generation: an adjustment can't slip in while the payslip is being frozen.
            $lockedRun = PayrollRun::query()->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($run->id);

            if (! $lockedRun->status->canGeneratePayslips()) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['adjustmentAmount' => 'Adjustments can only be added while the run is processing.']);
            }

            if (PayslipRecord::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $lockedRun->id)->where('user_id', $employee->id)->exists()) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['adjustmentAmount' => 'This payslip is already generated. Add the correction to the next payroll instead.']);
            }

            if (! $forPaidLeave && ! TimeLog::query()->where('user_id', $employee->id)->between($lockedRun->start_date, $lockedRun->end_date)->exists()) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['adjustmentAmount' => 'No attendance in this period, so there will be no payslip to adjust. Add it to a period they worked.']);
            }

            // Off by default (null): Accounting's adjustments apply at once.
            $threshold = config('payroll.adjustments.approval_threshold');
            $needsApproval = $threshold !== null
                && abs($amount) >= (float) $threshold
                && ! $actor->can(Ability::ApprovePayrollAdjustments->value);

            $adjustment = new PayrollAdjustment;
            $adjustment->forceFill([
                'payroll_run_id' => $lockedRun->id,
                'user_id' => $employee->id,
                'category' => $category,
                'amount' => number_format($amount, 2, '.', ''),
                'reason' => trim($reason),
                'status' => $needsApproval ? AdjustmentStatus::Pending : AdjustmentStatus::Approved,
                'created_by' => $actor->id,
                'reviewed_by' => $needsApproval ? null : $actor->id,
                'reviewed_at' => $needsApproval ? null : CarbonImmutable::now(),
            ])->save();

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, 'adjustment.added', ($amount > 0 ? 'Added ₱' : 'Deducted ₱').number_format(abs($amount), 2)." ({$category->label()}) on {$employee->name}'s payslip for {$lockedRun->periodLabel()}", $adjustment, [
                'amount' => $amount,
                'category' => $category->value,
                'reason' => $adjustment->reason,
                'status' => $adjustment->status->value,
            ], causer: $actor);

            if ($needsApproval) {
                $approvers = User::query()->notifiable(Ability::ApprovePayrollAdjustments->roles())->whereKeyNot($actor->id)->get();
                Notification::send($approvers, new PayrollAdjustmentAwaitingApproval($adjustment));
            }

            return $adjustment;
        });
    }
}
