<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AdjustmentStatus;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\PayrollAdjustment;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\UpdateNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * The second person's decision on a large adjustment. The creator can never
 * approve their own: that is the whole point of a second person.
 */
final class ReviewPayrollAdjustment
{
    public function __construct(private readonly AuditLogger $audit) {}

    public function handle(PayrollAdjustment $adjustment, bool $approve, ?string $note, User $actor): PayrollAdjustment
    {
        if (! $actor->can(Ability::ApprovePayrollAdjustments->value) || $adjustment->created_by === $actor->id) {
            throw new AuthorizationException('A different person must approve this adjustment.');
        }

        if (! $approve && blank($note)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['reviewNote' => 'Say why the adjustment is rejected.']);
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($adjustment, $approve, $note, $actor) {
            $locked = PayrollAdjustment::query()->with(['employee:id,name', 'creator'])->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($adjustment->id);

            if ($locked->status !== AdjustmentStatus::Pending) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['reviewNote' => "This adjustment is already {$locked->status->label()}."]);
            }

            $locked->forceFill([
                'status' => $approve ? AdjustmentStatus::Approved : AdjustmentStatus::Rejected,
                'reviewed_by' => $actor->id,
                'reviewed_at' => CarbonImmutable::now(),
                'review_note' => filled($note) ? $note : null,
            ])->save();

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, $approve ? 'adjustment.approved' : 'adjustment.rejected', ($approve ? 'Approved' : 'Rejected').' the ₱'.number_format(abs((float) $locked->amount), 2)." adjustment on {$locked->employee->name}'s payslip", $locked, [
                'old' => ['status' => AdjustmentStatus::Pending->value],
                'new' => ['status' => $locked->status->value],
                'note' => $locked->review_note,
            ], causer: $actor);

            // The one who asked for the second check hears the answer.
            UpdateNotice::tell($locked->creator, $actor, ($approve ? 'Adjustment approved: ' : 'Adjustment rejected: ').$locked->employee->name,
                '₱'.number_format(abs((float) $locked->amount), 2).($approve ? ' is on the payslip now.' : ". {$locked->review_note}"), route('payroll', ['run' => $locked->payroll_run_id]), 'banknotes');

            return $locked;
        });
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Enums;

/**
 * Why a payslip is adjusted. The category decides the direction and whether
 * the amount counts as taxable pay, so Accounting never has to know the tax
 * rule by heart.
 */
enum AdjustmentCategory: string
{
    case Correction = 'correction';
    case Allowance = 'allowance';
    case Refund = 'refund';
    case Penalty = 'penalty';
    case Reimbursement = 'reimbursement';
    // Leave the law pays (paternity, solo parent, VAWC, special leave for women): from PaidLeavePayment.
    case PaidLeave = 'paid_leave';
    // The bonus for referring someone who was hired and stayed (Referral, PayDueReferralBonuses).
    case ReferralBonus = 'referral_bonus';
    case Other = 'other';

    public function label(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::PaidLeave => 'Paid leave',
            self::ReferralBonus => 'Referral bonus',
            default => ucfirst($this->value),
        };
    }

    public function description(): string
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Correction => 'Fixes pay that was wrong (e.g. a missed clock-in). Counts as taxable pay.',
            self::Allowance => 'Extra non-taxable pay (e.g. transport, meal).',
            self::Refund => 'Pays back something deducted by mistake.',
            self::Penalty => 'A deduction the employee agreed to in writing (Labor Code Art. 113).',
            self::Reimbursement => 'Pays back company expenses an employee paid for (with the receipt). Not taxable: it isn\'t pay.',
            self::PaidLeave => 'Days of leave the law pays (paternity, solo parent, VAWC, special leave for women), at the daily rate. Taxable: it\'s pay.',
            self::ReferralBonus => 'The bonus for referring someone who was hired and stayed. Not taxed here: a bonus within the ₱90,000 a year of 13th month and other benefits (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e)).',
            self::Other => 'Anything else; explain it in the reason.',
        };
    }

    /**
     * Corrections replace pay the employee should have earned, so they are
     * taxed like it. Allowances and refunds are not pay for work.
     */
    public function isTaxable(): bool
    {
        return $this === self::Correction || $this === self::PaidLeave;
    }

    public function allowsAddition(): bool
    {
        return $this !== self::Penalty;
    }

    public function allowsDeduction(): bool
    {
        return in_array($this, [self::Correction, self::Penalty, self::Other], true);
    }
}
QuestionAnswer
Why not let Accounting edit the gross or net directly?An overwritten number proves nothing: correction, typo or fraud all look the same afterwards. And the real cause (a missed clock-in, a wrong rate) stays wrong for next payroll.
Why is a Correction taxable but an Allowance not?A correction replaces pay that was earned for work. An allowance or refund isn't pay for work. The category decides, so nobody has to remember the tax rule.
Why no approval step by default?Accounting owns payroll; an approval queue would slow every correction. The protection is the audit trail: every adjustment has a category, a reason, a name and a time, and the calculated figures are never overwritten. Companies that want a second person set PAYROLL_ADJUSTMENT_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD.
Why is the panel its own Livewire component?The Payroll page is already large. The panel owns its form and tells the page to re-read the payslip through an adjustments-changed event.

Corrections from earlier cut-offs: pay that changed after it was paid

A frozen payslip is never rewritten. But a guard's day can be recorded by hand after the cut-off, overtime or leave can be approved late, a rate can be back-dated. Before, that difference was simply never paid unless someone noticed. Now the open run recomputes everyone's paid cut-offs from the last 90 days and suggests each difference for Accounting to accept or dismiss.

flowchart LR
  A[Run starts processing
or Generate / Check again] --> D[DetectPriorPeriodCorrections]
  D -->|recompute attendancePay
vs the frozen payslip
minus what's decided| S{difference?}
  S -->|no| N[nothing]
  S -->|yes| L[Corrections from earlier cut-offs]
  L -->|Accept| ADJ[Correction adjustment
on this payslip, taxable]
  L -->|Dismiss + reason| X[settled, not paid]
  L -.->|undecided| H[payslip waits]
One formula, two usesPayslipCalculator::attendancePay() (basic, holiday, overtime, night, late due) is what calculate() is built on, and what detection compares against the frozen payslip. A recomputed cut-off can't drift from how payslips are computed.
Suggested, never appliedIt's money, so a person accepts it. Accepting goes through AddPayrollAdjustment: taxable as a Correction, audited, and held for a second person if large. The payslip line says which cut-off and what changed.
Never twice, never lostEach check subtracts what was already decided for that cut-off. A dismissed one stays dismissed; an accepted one whose adjustment is later removed or rejected becomes owed again.
A column named changes is a trapThe first draft stored the differences in a changes column. Inside the model, $this->changes is Eloquent's own list of changed attributes, so every reason read "recomputed pay differs". Renamed to differences. Avoid attribute names Eloquent already uses (changes, attributes, original, relations).
app/Actions/Payroll/DetectPriorPeriodCorrections.php165 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Data\PayslipInput;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\PayslipRecord;
use App\Models\PriorPeriodCorrection;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Queries\Payroll\PayslipInputsQuery;
use App\Services\Payroll\PayslipCalculator;
use App\Services\Payroll\RateScheduleResolver;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection as EloquentCollection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * Pay that changed after a payslip was frozen: a day recorded by hand after the
 * cut-off, overtime or leave approved late, a back-dated rate. Without this the
 * difference is simply never paid.
 *
 * For everyone who'll get a payslip on the open run, each of their payslips from
 * cut-offs that ended in the last `payroll.prior_period.lookback_days` is
 * recomputed with today's data (PayslipCalculator::attendancePay, the same rules
 * as the payslip) and compared with what was frozen. What's left after earlier
 * decisions (accepted or dismissed) is suggested on the open run, one per
 * person per cut-off, for Accounting to accept or dismiss. A suggestion that's no
 * longer right (the change was undone) is updated or removed.
 *
 * Only attendance pay is compared. Contributions aren't recomputed, and the
 * correction is taxed as a Correction adjustment on the new payslip.
 */
final class DetectPriorPeriodCorrections
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly PayslipInputsQuery $inputs,
        private readonly PayslipCalculator $calculator,
        private readonly RateScheduleResolver $rates,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  EloquentCollection<int, User>|null  $only  just these employees (one payslip); null = everyone in the run
     * @return int open suggestions on the run (for those checked)
     */
    public function handle(PayrollRun $run, ?EloquentCollection $only = null): int
    {
        if (! $run->status->canGeneratePayslips()) {
            return 0;
        }

        $employees = ($only ?? User::query()
            ->onPayroll()
            ->whereHas('timeLogs', fn ($query) => $query->between($run->start_date, $run->end_date))
            ->whereDoesntHave('payslipRecords', fn ($query) => $query->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id))
            ->get())
            ->loadMissing('employeeProfile')
            ->keyBy('id');

        if ($employees->isEmpty()) {
            return 0;
        }

        $since = CarbonImmutable::parse($run->start_date)->subDays((int) config('payroll.prior_period.lookback_days'))->toDateString();

        $earlier = PayslipRecord::query()
            ->whereIn('user_id', $employees->keys()->all())
            ->whereHas('payrollRun', fn ($query) => $query
                ->whereKeyNot($run->id)
                ->whereDate('end_date', '<', $run->start_date->toDateString())
                ->whereDate('end_date', '>=', $since))
            ->get();

        foreach (PayrollRun::query()->whereKey($earlier->pluck('payroll_run_id')->unique()->all())->orderBy('start_date')->get() as $fromRun) {
            $records = $earlier->where('payroll_run_id', $fromRun->id);
            $people = $employees->only($records->pluck('user_id')->all())->values();
            $inputs = $this->inputs->handle($fromRun, $people);
            $schedule = $this->rates->forDate($fromRun->start_date);

            foreach ($records as $record) {
                $now = $this->calculator->attendancePay($inputs[$record->user_id], $schedule);
                $this->reconcile($run, $fromRun, $record, $now, $this->changes($record, $inputs[$record->user_id], $now));
            }
        }

        return PriorPeriodCorrection::query()->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)->whereIn('user_id', $employees->keys()->all())->suggested()->count();
    }

    /**
     * @param  array{daily_rate: float, basic: float, holiday: float, overtime: float, night: float, late: float, total: float}  $now
     * @param  array<string, array{0: int|float, 1: int|float}>  $changes
     */
    private function reconcile(PayrollRun $run, PayrollRun $fromRun, PayslipRecord $record, array $now, array $changes): void
    {
        DB::transaction(function () use ($run, $fromRun, $record, $now, $changes) {
            $decided = (float) PriorPeriodCorrection::query()
                ->where('user_id', $record->user_id)
                ->where('from_payroll_run_id', $fromRun->id)
                ->settled()
                ->sum('amount');

            $open = PriorPeriodCorrection::query()
                ->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)
                ->where('user_id', $record->user_id)
                ->where('from_payroll_run_id', $fromRun->id)
                ->suggested()
                ->lockForUpdate()
                ->first();

            $owed = round($now['total'] - self::frozenTotal($record) - $decided, 2);

            if (abs($owed) < 0.01) {
                $open?->delete();

                return;
            }

            $correction = $open ?? new PriorPeriodCorrection;
            $correction->forceFill([
                'user_id' => $record->user_id,
                'payroll_run_id' => $run->id,
                'from_payroll_run_id' => $fromRun->id,
                'amount' => number_format($owed, 2, '.', ''),
                'differences' => $changes,
            ])->save();
        });
    }

    /**
     * The frozen payslip's attendance pay, measured the same way: the late deduction
     * DUE is what was taken plus any of it carried to the next payslip.
     */
    public static function frozenTotal(PayslipRecord $record): float
    {
        $lateCarried = array_sum(array_map(
            fn (array $line) => $line['label'] === 'Late deduction' ? (float) $line['amount'] : 0.0,
            $record->shortfall_lines ?? [],
        ));

        return round((float) $record->basic_pay + (float) $record->holiday_pay + (float) $record->overtime_pay + (float) $record->night_differential
            - (float) $record->late_deduction - $lateCarried, 2);
    }

    /**
     * What differs between the frozen payslip and today, for the reason line.
     *
     * @param  array{daily_rate: float, basic: float, holiday: float, overtime: float, night: float, late: float, total: float}  $now
     * @return array<string, array{0: int|float, 1: int|float}>
     */
    private function changes(PayslipRecord $record, PayslipInput $input, array $now): array
    {
        // Payslips from before night minutes were saved have 0 with a night differential: not a change.
        $nightUnknown = (int) $record->night_minutes === 0 && (float) $record->night_differential > 0;

        $pairs = [
            'days' => [$record->days_worked, $input->daysWorked],
            'overtime_minutes' => [$record->overtime_minutes, $input->overtimeMinutes],
            'night_minutes' => $nightUnknown ? [0, 0] : [(int) $record->night_minutes, $input->nightMinutes],
            'late_minutes' => [$record->late_minutes, $input->lateMinutes],
            'daily_rate' => [round((float) $record->daily_rate, 2), round($now['daily_rate'], 2)],
            'holiday_pay' => [round((float) $record->holiday_pay, 2), round($now['holiday'], 2)],
        ];

        return array_filter($pairs, fn (array $pair) => $pair[0] != $pair[1]);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AdjustmentCategory;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\PriorPeriodCorrection;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Accounting accepts a correction from an earlier cut-off: it becomes a
 * Correction adjustment on this run's payslip (taxable, like the pay it
 * replaces), through AddPayrollAdjustment, so the same rules hold, including
 * the optional second approval for large amounts.
 */
final class AcceptPriorPeriodCorrection
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly AddPayrollAdjustment $addAdjustment,
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
    ) {}

    public function handle(PriorPeriodCorrection $correction, User $actor): PriorPeriodCorrection
    {
        if (! $actor->can(Ability::ManagePayroll->value)) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($correction, $actor) {
            $locked = PriorPeriodCorrection::query()->with(['run', 'fromRun', 'user'])->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($correction->id);

            if ($locked->status !== PriorPeriodCorrection::SUGGESTED) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['correction' => 'This correction was already decided.']);
            }

            $adjustment = $this->addAdjustment->handle($locked->run, $locked->user, AdjustmentCategory::Correction, (float) $locked->amount, $locked->adjustmentReason(), $actor);

            $locked->forceFill([
                'status' => PriorPeriodCorrection::ACCEPTED,
                'payroll_adjustment_id' => $adjustment->id,
                'decided_by' => $actor->id,
                'decided_at' => CarbonImmutable::now(),
            ])->save();

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, 'correction.accepted', "Accepted a correction from {$locked->fromRun->periodLabel()} on {$locked->user->name}'s payslip for {$locked->run->periodLabel()}", $locked, [
                'amount' => (float) $locked->amount,
                'differences' => $locked->differences,
            ], causer: $actor);

            return $locked;
        });
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use App\Enums\AdjustmentStatus;
use App\Enums\AwayReason;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;

/**
 * Pay that changed after a payslip was frozen, suggested on the open run for
 * Accounting to accept (→ a Correction adjustment) or dismiss. See
 * App\Actions\Payroll\DetectPriorPeriodCorrections.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property int $user_id
 * @property int $payroll_run_id
 * @property int $from_payroll_run_id
 * @property string $amount
 * @property array<string, array{0: int|float, 1: int|float}> $differences
 * @property string $status
 * @property int|null $payroll_adjustment_id
 * @property int|null $decided_by
 * @property CarbonImmutable|null $decided_at
 * @property string|null $dismiss_reason
 * @property-read User $user
 * @property-read PayrollRun $run
 * @property-read PayrollRun $fromRun
 * @property-read PayrollAdjustment|null $adjustment
 */
class PriorPeriodCorrection extends Model
{
    public const SUGGESTED = 'suggested';

    public const ACCEPTED = 'accepted';

    public const DISMISSED = 'dismissed';

    /**
     * @var array<string, mixed>
     */
    protected $attributes = [
        'status' => self::SUGGESTED,
    ];

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'amount' => 'decimal:2',
            'differences' => 'array',
            'decided_at' => 'datetime',
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function user(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class);
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<PayrollRun, $this>
     */
    public function run(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(PayrollRun::class, 'payroll_run_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<PayrollRun, $this>
     */
    public function fromRun(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(PayrollRun::class, 'from_payroll_run_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<PayrollAdjustment, $this>
     */
    public function adjustment(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(PayrollAdjustment::class, 'payroll_adjustment_id');
    }

    /**
     * @param  Builder<PriorPeriodCorrection>  $query
     */
    public function scopeSuggested(Builder $query): void
    {
        $query->where('status', self::SUGGESTED);
    }

    /**
     * Already decided, so the next check doesn't suggest it again: dismissed, or
     * accepted with its adjustment still there (removing or rejecting that
     * adjustment makes the difference owed again).
     *
     * @param  Builder<PriorPeriodCorrection>  $query
     */
    public function scopeSettled(Builder $query): void
    {
        $query->where(fn (Builder $settled) => $settled
            ->where('status', self::DISMISSED)
            ->orWhere(fn (Builder $accepted) => $accepted->where('status', self::ACCEPTED)
                ->whereHas('adjustment', fn (Builder $adjustment) => $adjustment->where('status', '!=', AdjustmentStatus::Rejected->value))));
    }

    /**
     * What changed, in words: "1 more day worked, 2 hrs more overtime".
     */
    public function summary(): string
    {
        $parts = [];

        foreach ($this->differences as $what => [$before, $after]) {
            $parts[] = self::describe($what, $before, $after);
        }

        return $parts === [] ? 'recomputed pay differs' : implode(', ', $parts);
    }

    /**
     * The payslip line: "Prior period Oct 1–15, 2026: 1 more day worked".
     */
    public function adjustmentReason(): string
    {
        return "Prior period {$this->fromRun->periodLabel()}: {$this->summary()}";
    }

    private static function describe(string $what, int|float $before, int|float $after): string
    {
        $diff = $after - $before;
        // "2 hrs", "1 hr 30 min": the same wording as time away.
        $minutes = fn (int|float $value): string => AwayReason::durationLabel((int) abs($value));

        return match ($what) {
            'days' => abs($diff).' '.($diff > 0 ? 'more' : 'fewer').' '.str('day')->plural((int) abs($diff)).' worked',
            'overtime_minutes' => $minutes($diff).($diff > 0 ? ' more' : ' less').' overtime',
            'night_minutes' => $minutes($diff).($diff > 0 ? ' more' : ' less').' night work',
            'late_minutes' => $minutes($diff).($diff > 0 ? ' more' : ' less').' late',
            'daily_rate' => 'daily rate ₱'.number_format((float) $before, 2).' → ₱'.number_format((float) $after, 2),
            'holiday_pay' => 'holiday pay ₱'.number_format((float) $before, 2).' → ₱'.number_format((float) $after, 2),
            default => $what.' changed',
        };
    }
}

  2. As accounting@example.test: Payroll → the processing run → Check again. Accept it, then open that employee's payslip: Correction: Prior period …: 1 more day worked.

Report a problem: what only the employee can see

The corrections above catch what the system knows changed. A day never recorded at all, overtime a supervisor allowed but nobody filed, a deduction nobody recognises: only the employee notices. Under each payslip on My Payslips: Something wrong on this payslip? Report a problem. They pick what's wrong (each choice has its own example), write it with the dates, and can attach a photo or PDF. Accounting is told at once and answers on Payroll Concerns.

AnswerWhat happens
Pay itAn amount on a payslip still being processed (they worked that run, payslip not generated yet), as a Correction adjustment through AddPayrollAdjustment: taxable, audited, held for a second person if large. The reply is the reason on the payslip.
ExplainResolved, nothing changes: "Oct 10 was your day off on the roster."
Not validWith the reason.
Not ComplaintsComplaints go to HR and are confidential workplace matters. Pay goes to Accounting, who can fix it, and the answer sits under the payslip it's about.
Always a replyEvery answer carries words the employee reads (bell, email, and under the payslip), so nobody is left wondering whether it was seen.
The photo stays privateChecked by its first bytes (PrivateUploadStore), saved under a random name on the private disk, and streamed only to the employee and Accounting.

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\PayrollConcernCategory;
use App\Models\PayrollConcern;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\PayrollConcernNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use App\Services\Files\PrivateUploadStore;
use Illuminate\Http\UploadedFile;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Notification;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * An employee reports a problem on one of their payslips (roadmap item 14):
 * what's wrong, in their words, and optionally a photo or PDF (a DTR, a
 * supervisor's note). Accounting is told at once, by bell and email.
 *
 * One open report per kind of problem per payslip, so a double tap doesn't
 * file it twice.
 */
final class FilePayrollConcern
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly PrivateUploadStore $uploads,
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
    ) {}

    public function handle(User $employee, PayrollRun $run, PayrollConcernCategory $category, string $details, ?UploadedFile $attachment = null): PayrollConcern
    {
        $employee->loadMissing('employeeProfile');

        if ($employee->employeeProfile === null || $employee->isPaidOutsidePayroll() || ! PayrollRun::query()->visibleToEmployees()->whereKey($run->id)->exists()) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['details' => 'Problems can be reported on your own payslips only.']);
        }

        if (mb_strlen(trim($details)) < 10) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['details' => 'Say what\'s wrong, with the dates (a sentence or two).']);
        }

        if (PayrollConcern::query()->open()->where('user_id', $employee->id)->where('payroll_run_id', $run->id)->where('category', $category)->exists()) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['details' => 'You already reported this on this payslip. Accounting will answer it.']);
        }

        $disk = (string) config('payroll.concerns.disk');
        $stored = $attachment !== null ? $this->uploads->store($attachment, $disk, 'payroll-concerns/'.$employee->id, 'concern', ['png', 'jpg', 'pdf'], 'attachment') : null;

        try {
            return DB::transaction(function () use ($employee, $run, $category, $details, $stored) {
                $concern = new PayrollConcern;
                $concern->forceFill([
                    'user_id' => $employee->id,
                    'payroll_run_id' => $run->id,
                    'category' => $category,
                    'details' => trim($details),
                    'attachment_path' => $stored['path'] ?? null,
                    'attachment_name' => $stored['name'] ?? null,
                    'attachment_mime' => $stored['mime'] ?? null,
                ])->save();

                $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, 'concern.filed', "{$employee->name} reported a problem on the {$run->periodLabel()} payslip: {$category->label()}", $concern, causer: $employee);

                Notification::send(User::query()->notifiable(Ability::ManagePayroll->roles())->whereKeyNot($employee->id)->get(), new PayrollConcernNotice($concern, PayrollConcernNotice::FILED));

                return $concern;
            });
        } catch (\Throwable $e) {
            // Nothing saved: don't leave the file behind.
            $this->uploads->delete($disk, $stored['path'] ?? null);

            throw $e;
        }
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AdjustmentCategory;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\PayrollConcernStatus;
use App\Enums\PayrollRunStatus;
use App\Models\PayrollConcern;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\PayrollConcernNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Accounting answers a reported payslip problem, always with a reply the
 * employee reads:
 *
 *   PAY       resolved, and the amount goes on a payslip still open in a
 *             processing run, as a Correction adjustment (AddPayrollAdjustment:
 *             taxable, audited, the optional second approval)
 *   EXPLAIN   resolved, nothing to change (the payslip was right)
 *   DECLINE   not valid
 *
 * The employee is told either way.
 */
final class AnswerPayrollConcern
{
    public const PAY = 'pay';

    public const EXPLAIN = 'explain';

    public const DECLINE = 'decline';

    public function __construct(
        private readonly AddPayrollAdjustment $addAdjustment,
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  float|null  $amount  signed, for PAY: + adds to pay, − takes off
     */
    public function handle(PayrollConcern $concern, User $actor, string $outcome, string $response, ?PayrollRun $payOn = null, ?float $amount = null): PayrollConcern
    {
        if (! $actor->can(Ability::ManagePayroll->value)) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        if (! in_array($outcome, [self::PAY, self::EXPLAIN, self::DECLINE], true)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['outcome' => 'Choose how it\'s answered.']);
        }

        if (mb_strlen(trim($response)) < 5) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['response' => 'Write the reply the employee will read (a few words).']);
        }

        if ($outcome === self::PAY && ($payOn === null || $amount === null)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['payRunId' => 'Choose the payslip it goes on, and the amount.']);
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($concern, $actor, $outcome, $response, $payOn, $amount) {
            $locked = PayrollConcern::query()->with(['user', 'run'])->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($concern->id);

            if ($locked->status !== PayrollConcernStatus::Open) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['response' => 'This concern was already answered.']);
            }

            // PAY always has a run and an amount here (checked above).
            $adjustment = $outcome === self::PAY
                ? $this->addAdjustment->handle($payOn, $locked->user, AdjustmentCategory::Correction, $amount, "Payroll concern ({$locked->run->periodLabel()}): ".trim($response), $actor)
                : null;

            $locked->forceFill([
                'status' => $outcome === self::DECLINE ? PayrollConcernStatus::Declined : PayrollConcernStatus::Resolved,
                'response' => trim($response),
                'payroll_adjustment_id' => $adjustment?->id,
                'resolved_by' => $actor->id,
                'resolved_at' => CarbonImmutable::now(),
            ])->save();

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, 'concern.answered', "Answered {$locked->user->name}'s payroll concern ({$locked->run->periodLabel()}): {$locked->status->label()}", $locked, [
                'outcome' => $outcome,
                'amount' => $amount,
                'response' => $locked->response,
            ], causer: $actor);

            $locked->user->notify(new PayrollConcernNotice($locked, PayrollConcernNotice::ANSWERED));

            return $locked;
        });
    }

    /**
     * Where a fix can be paid: runs still processing in which this person has
     * attendance and no generated payslip yet (AddPayrollAdjustment's own rules).
     *
     * @return Collection<int, PayrollRun>
     */
    public static function payableRuns(User $employee): Collection
    {
        return PayrollRun::query()
            ->where('status', PayrollRunStatus::Processing)
            ->whereDoesntHave('payslipRecords', fn ($query) => $query->where('user_id', $employee->id))
            ->orderBy('start_date')
            ->get()
            ->filter(fn (PayrollRun $run) => $employee->timeLogs()->between($run->start_date, $run->end_date)->exists())
            ->values();
    }
}

09

UI system

Same look as the old system: white sidebar, blue active state, sticky top bar, dark mode. What changed is underneath. The sidebar is data, inputs read their own errors, enums return tone names and Blade owns the Tailwind classes, because Tailwind only finds classes it can see in the views.

A password field (type="password") also gets a show / hide eye button inside it, from the same component: Alpine switches the input between password and text, starting hidden, with aria-pressed and a changing label for screen readers. Every password field in the app has it without adding anything.

A locked button always says why

Pass :disabled-reason instead of a bare :disabled. The button is disabled, its wire:click is dropped, and the reason appears as a tooltip on hover, keyboard focus or tap. For example: "24 employees who worked this period have no payslip yet. Click Generate all first."

The tooltip sits on a wrapper, not on the button, because a disabled button fires no mouse events. The wrapper is focusable, so keyboard and touch users reach the explanation too. For buttons that Alpine locks and unlocks (the camera's Capture), when="!canCapture" shows the tooltip only while it's locked, with the reason from captureBlockedReason.

Every button shows it's working

While a button is busy, a spinner covers its label (so it keeps its exact size) and a second click is ignored. Livewire 4 already puts data-loading on whatever started a request: the clicked button, or the submit button of a wire:submit form, even one outside it via form="…". So <x-ui.button> styles that once and every page gets it. Plain forms (login, register, password) reload the page instead, so form-loading.js marks their button.

Not disabledA disabled submit button drops its name/value from the request. pointer-events: none blocks the click, and a second submit event is cancelled: one login, one reset email.
Only real submitsThe browser fires submit only after its own validation passes; a confirm() that says Cancel arrives already cancelled. Neither shows a spinner.
Back buttonA page restored from the back/forward cache is cleared on pageshow, so nothing is left spinning.
resources/js/form-loading.js51 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
/**
 * Loading state for PLAIN forms (login, register, password, two-factor, account
 * settings, logout). Livewire marks its own buttons; this does the same for forms
 * that reload the page:
 *
 *  - the button that submitted gets data-loading + aria-busy, so <x-ui.button>
 *    shows its spinner;
 *  - a second submit while the first is on its way is ignored (no double login,
 *    no two reset emails);
 *  - the button is NOT disabled: a disabled submit button drops its name/value
 *    from the request. The component blocks clicks with pointer-events instead.
 *
 * Skipped: forms Livewire handles (it cancels the event first), a submit cancelled
 * by onsubmit="return confirm(…)" (also cancelled), forms opening another tab,
 * and any form marked data-no-loading (e.g. one that downloads a file and so
 * never leaves the page).
 */
export default function registerFormLoading() {
    // Bubble phase: by now the browser's own validation passed (an invalid form never
    // fires "submit") and the form's own handlers, Livewire's included, have run.
    document.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
        const form = event.target;

        if (event.defaultPrevented || !(form instanceof HTMLFormElement)) return;
        if (form.hasAttribute('data-no-loading') || (form.target && form.target !== '_self')) return;

        if (form.dataset.submitting) {
            event.preventDefault();
            return;
        }

        form.dataset.submitting = 'true';

        const button = event.submitter ?? form.querySelector('button[type="submit"], button:not([type]), input[type="submit"]');
        button?.setAttribute('data-loading', 'true');
        button?.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
    });

    // Back button: the browser may restore this page exactly as it was left, mid-submit.
    window.addEventListener('pageshow', (event) => {
        if (!event.persisted) return;

        document.querySelectorAll('form[data-submitting]').forEach((form) => {
            delete form.dataset.submitting;
            form.querySelectorAll('[aria-busy="true"]').forEach((button) => {
                button.removeAttribute('data-loading');
                button.removeAttribute('aria-busy');
            });
        });
    });
}

Dark mode that survives a page change

Picking dark mode and then opening another page went back to light. wire:navigate swaps in the next page's <html>, whose attributes come from the server without the dark class, and it doesn't re-run the head script that adds it. The fix: the head script also listens for livewire:navigating and registers onSwap(applyTheme). That runs right after the swap, before Alpine starts, so the toggle reads the right state and nothing flashes. The Back button uses the same hook.

resources/views/components/layouts/base.blade.php37 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
@props(['title' => null])

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="{{ str_replace('_', '-', app()->getLocale()) }}">
    <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8">
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
        <meta name="csrf-token" content="{{ csrf_token() }}">

        <title>{{ $title ? $title.' · ' : '' }}{{ config('app.name') }}</title>

        <link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="{{ asset('assets/ossi-seal.png') }}">

        {{-- Before CSS loads, so a dark-mode user never sees a white flash. wire:navigate swaps in the
             next page's <html> attributes (no "dark" class) and doesn't re-run this script, so the theme is
             applied again on every swap, before Alpine starts and the toggle reads it. --}}
        <script>
            window.applyTheme = () => {
                let dark = false;
                try { dark = localStorage.theme === 'dark' || (!('theme' in localStorage) && window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches); } catch (e) {}
                document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', dark);
            };
            window.applyTheme();
            document.addEventListener('livewire:navigating', (event) => event.detail.onSwap(window.applyTheme));
        </script>

        @vite(['resources/css/app.css', 'resources/js/app.js'])
        @livewireStyles
    </head>
    <body {{ $attributes->class('bg-gray-50 text-gray-800 antialiased dark:bg-gray-950 dark:text-gray-100') }}>
        {{ $slot }}

        <x-toast />

        @livewireScripts
    </body>
</html>

An error under one field mustn't move the others

A form row lined up on the bottom edge (items-end) jumps when one field shows an error: the error makes that field taller, and its box rises. Line rows up on the top edge (items-start), and give a button without a label an invisible label row (plus the input's mt-1), so it stays level with the boxes. Measured: all four boxes at the same top, the same height.

A bug found by measuring: the dialog flash

Switching Field / Office staff in an open dialog flashed the page darker. Livewire runs a View Transition on every update, and during an update the browser shows the old and the new snapshot of the backdrop at once. A sidebar pixel measured 118 at rest and 63 mid-switch: two 60% layers. Hiding one layer at a time pointed at the old backdrop. The obvious fix, ::view-transition-old(x):not(:only-child), did nothing, because Chrome matches :only-child on these snapshots but never its negation. The fix that works: the old snapshot is always opacity: 0, and the close animation starts explicitly from { opacity: 1 }, so a real close still fades (118 → 188 → 255).

    <p class="mt-1 text-center text-xs text-gray-400">{{ config('payroll.disclaimer') }}</p>
</x-sensitive>
Question you'd askAnswer
Why do some pages use Fortify forms and not Livewire?Posting straight to Fortify's routes keeps its validation, throttling and session handling. Account Settings is plain Blade for that reason; only the avatar uploader is Livewire.
Why a custom select?The browser draws native option lists, so Tailwind can't style them. A hidden real <select> stays the source of truth for wire:model.

composer test runs Pint, PHPStan level 8 and Pest, the same as CI. The access test builds its 66 cases from the Ability enum, so changing who can open a page changes the test with it.

<?php

use App\Data\CarryoverLine;
use App\Data\LateBracket;
use App\Data\LoanLine;
use App\Data\PayslipInput;
use App\Data\RateSchedule;
use App\Services\Payroll\PayslipCalculator;

/**
 * Pure unit tests: no Laravel, no database. The rates are built by hand, so
 * each test states exactly what it depends on.
 */
function rates(): RateSchedule
{
    return new RateSchedule(
        effectiveFrom: '1970-01-01',
        dailyRate: ['field' => 610, 'office' => 900],
        sss: ['field' => 581, 'office' => 900],
        philhealth: ['field' => 225, 'office' => 400],
        pagibig: ['field' => 100, 'office' => 100],
        withholdingRate: ['field' => 0.0, 'office' => 0.02],
        holidayPremiums: ['regular' => 1.00, 'special_non_working' => 0.30],
        nightDifferentialRate: 0.10,
        overtimeMultiplier: 1.25,
        standardHoursPerDay: 8,
    );
}

it('computes the worked example from the spec to net 7,787', function () {
    // Field guard, 13 days, 120 approved OT minutes, 30 minutes late, no brackets, 1 regular holiday worked.
    $payslip = (new PayslipCalculator)->calculate(new PayslipInput(
        isOfficeStaff: false,
        nightMinutes: 0,
        daysWorked: 13,
        lateMinutes: 30,
        overtimeMinutes: 120,
        holidayDaysWorked: ['regular' => 1],
    ), rates());

    expect($payslip->basicPay)->toBe(7930.0)
        ->and($payslip->overtimePay)->toBe(191.0)
        ->and($payslip->holidayPay)->toBe(610.0)
        ->and($payslip->grossPay())->toBe(8731.0)
        ->and($payslip->governmentDeductions())->toBe(906.0)
        ->and($payslip->lateDeduction)->toBe(38.0)
        ->and($payslip->netPay())->toBe(7787.0);
});

it('pays a worked special non-working day 30% on top, and an unworked holiday nothing', function (array $holidays, float $premium) {
    $payslip = (new PayslipCalculator)->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 0, 1, 0, 0, $holidays), rates());

    expect($payslip->holidayPay)->toBe($premium);
})->with([
    'worked regular holiday' => [['regular' => 1], 610.0],
    'worked special day' => [['special_non_working' => 1], 183.0],
    'no holiday worked' => [[], 0.0],
]);

it('exempts field staff from withholding tax and charges office staff 2% of taxable gross', function () {
    $calculator = new PayslipCalculator;

    $field = $calculator->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 0, 10, 0, 0), rates());
    $office = $calculator->calculate(new PayslipInput(true, 0, 10, 0, 0), rates());

    expect($field->withholdingTax)->toBe(0.0)
        ->and($field->isMinimumWageEarner())->toBeTrue()
        ->and($office->withholdingTax)->toBe(180.0) // 2% of 900 × 10
        ->and($office->sss)->toBe(900.0);
});

it('pays 10% night differential only for the minutes actually worked 10 PM–6 AM', function () {
    $calculator = new PayslipCalculator;

    // 10 nights × 8 h = 4,800 min × (₱610 ÷ 480) × 10% = ₱610.
    $nights = $calculator->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 4800, 10, 0, 0), rates());
    expect($nights->nightDifferential)->toBe(610.0)->and($nights->nightMinutes)->toBe(4800)
        // 2 night hours on one day: 120 × 1.2708 × 10% = ₱15.25 → ₱15.
        ->and($calculator->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 120, 1, 0, 0), rates())->nightDifferential)->toBe(15.0)
        ->and($calculator->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 0, 10, 0, 0), rates())->nightDifferential)->toBe(0.0);
});

it('uses the matching late bracket, or nothing when brackets exist but none match', function (int $lateMinutes, float $expected) {
    $brackets = [new LateBracket(1, 15, 50.0), new LateBracket(16, 60, 150.0), new LateBracket(120, null, 500.0)];

    $payslip = (new PayslipCalculator)->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 0, 10, $lateMinutes, 0, [], [], $brackets), rates());

    expect($payslip->lateDeduction)->toBe($expected);
})->with([

    'top of second bracket' => [60, 150.0],
    'gap between brackets' => [90, 0.0],
    'open-ended bracket' => [600, 500.0],
    'not late' => [0, 0.0],
]);

it('subtracts every loan installment from net pay', function () {

    $payslip = (new PayslipCalculator)->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 0, 13, 0, 0, [], $loans), rates());

    expect($payslip->loanDeductions())->toBe(650.0)
        ->and($payslip->netPay())->toBe(7930.0 - 906.0 - 650.0);

it('never lets net pay go below zero: deductions stop and the rest is a shortfall', function () {

    $payslip = (new PayslipCalculator)->calculate(new PayslipInput(false, 0, 1, 0, 0), rates());

        ->and($payslip->sss)->toBe(581.0)              // taken in full: first in line
        ->and($payslip->philhealth)->toBe(29.0)        // what was left

it('takes carried-over amounts after contributions and before late and loans; unpaid loans are not carried', function () {

<?php

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\RequestStatus;
use App\Enums\Role;
use App\Livewire\Admin\LeaveRequests;
use App\Models\EmployeeProfile;
use App\Models\LeaveRequest;
use Livewire\Livewire;

/**
 * Spec acceptance: "Each role can open exactly the screens its
 * gates allow, and gets a 403 everywhere else." Built from the Ability enum,
 * so a change to the access rules changes this test automatically.
 */
dataset('staff pages', function () {
    $pages = [
        'dashboard' => Ability::AccessEmployerArea,
        'attendance-log' => Ability::SuperviseAttendance,
        'leave-requests' => Ability::MonitorRequests,
        'overtime-requests' => Ability::MonitorRequests,
        'employees' => Ability::ViewPeople,
        'payroll' => Ability::ManagePayroll,
        'late-deductions' => Ability::ManagePayroll,
        'tax-settings' => Ability::ManagePayroll,
        'holidays' => Ability::ConfigureHolidays,
        'shifts' => Ability::ConfigureSystem,
        'clients' => Ability::ManageClients,
        'offices' => Ability::ManageOffices,
        'roles' => Ability::ConfigureSystem,
        'audit-log' => Ability::ViewSystemLogs,
        'announcements' => Ability::PublishContent,
        'load-requests' => Ability::ManageLoadRequests,
        'relievers' => Ability::ManageRelievers,
        'roster' => Ability::ManageRoster,
        'patrols' => Ability::ManagePatrols,
        'office-away' => Ability::MonitorOfficeAway,
        'documents' => Ability::ManageDocuments,
        'trainings' => Ability::ManageTraining,
        'radios' => Ability::ManageRadios,
        'referral-cases' => Ability::ManageReferrals,
        // HR, or the Executive for HR staff's own complaints.
        'complaint-cases' => [Ability::HandleComplaints, Ability::HandleHrComplaints],
    ];

    foreach (Role::cases() as $role) {
        foreach ($pages as $route => $abilities) {
            $allowed = collect(is_array($abilities) ? $abilities : [$abilities])->contains(fn (Ability $ability) => in_array($role, $ability->roles(), true));
            yield "{$role->value} → {$route} (".($allowed ? '200' : '403').')' => [$role, $route, $allowed];
        }
    }
});

it('opens exactly the staff pages a role\'s gates allow', function (Role $role, string $route, bool $allowed) {
    $this->actingAs(staff($role))->get(route($route))->assertStatus($allowed ? 200 : 403);
})->with('staff pages');

it('gives every signed-in user the self-service pages, and attendance and pay to those paid through payroll', function (Role $role) {
    $user = staff($role);
    $paidHere = ! in_array($role, Role::paidOutsidePayroll(), true);

    foreach (['profile', 'account-settings', 'help', 'company-policy'] as $route) {
        $this->actingAs($user)->get(route($route))->assertOk();
    }

    // Resignation too: every role but the Executive (paid outside payroll) may file one.
    foreach (['attendance', 'leave', 'overtime', 'payslips', 'load', 'absence-notice', 'complaints', 'resignation'] as $route) {
        $this->actingAs($user)->get(route($route))->assertStatus($paidHere ? 200 : 403);
    }
})->with(Role::cases());

it('sends guests to the login page', function (string $route) {
    $this->get(route($route))->assertRedirect(route('login'));
})->with(['attendance', 'dashboard', 'payroll', 'employees', 'audit-log']);

it('opens an employee record for viewers, with editing only for people managers', function () {
    $profile = EmployeeProfile::factory()->create();

    $this->actingAs(staff(Role::Hr))->get(route('employees.show', $profile))->assertOk()->assertSee('Edit record');
    $this->actingAs(staff(Role::Accounting))->get(route('employees.show', $profile))->assertOk()->assertDontSee('Edit record');
    $this->actingAs(staff(Role::Developer))->get(route('employees.show', $profile))->assertForbidden();
});

it('blocks the next write once a role is removed, even from a page already open', function () {
    $hr = staff(Role::Hr);
    $leave = new LeaveRequest(['type' => 'vacation', 'start_date' => today()->addDay(), 'end_date' => today()->addDay(), 'reason' => 'Rest']);
    $leave->user()->associate(employee());
    $leave->save();

    $page = Livewire::actingAs($hr)->test(LeaveRequests::class)->call('startReview', $leave->id);

    $hr->roles()->delete();
    // Every real request loads the user fresh from the session, so do the same here.
    $this->actingAs($hr->fresh());

    $page->call('approve')->assertForbidden();

    expect($leave->fresh()?->status)->toBe(RequestStatus::Pending);
});

<?php

use Livewire\Component;
use Livewire\Form;

// House rules a pull request can't quietly break.

arch()->preset()->php();
// The demo seeder uses seeded mt_rand() on purpose (same demo data on every machine); it never runs in production.
arch()->preset()->security()->ignoring('Database\Seeders\DemoSeeder');

arch('no debugging helpers')
    ->expect(['dd', 'dump', 'ray', 'var_dump'])
    ->not->toBeUsed();

// Fortify's generated classes follow Fortify's contracts (create(), update()), not ours.
arch('actions are final')
    ->expect('App\Actions')
    ->toBeFinal()
    ->ignoring('App\Actions\Fortify');

arch('actions have a handle method')
    ->expect('App\Actions')
    ->toHaveMethod('handle')
    ->ignoring('App\Actions\Fortify');

arch('queries are final and have handle()')
    ->expect('App\Queries')
    ->toBeFinal()
    ->toHaveMethod('handle');

arch('enums are enums')
    ->expect('App\Enums')
    ->toBeEnums();

arch('data objects are immutable')
    ->expect('App\Data')
    ->toBeReadonly()
    ->toBeFinal();

arch('controllers are invokable')
    ->expect('App\Http\Controllers')
    ->toBeInvokable()
    ->ignoring('App\Http\Controllers\Controller');

arch('livewire pages extend Component')
    ->expect('App\Livewire')
    ->toExtend(Component::class)
    ->ignoring(['App\Livewire\Forms', 'App\Livewire\Concerns']);

arch('form objects extend Form')
    ->expect('App\Livewire\Forms')
    ->toExtend(Form::class);

arch('components stay thin: no DB facade or raw queries')
    ->expect('Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB')
    ->not->toBeUsedIn('App\Livewire');

arch('calculators are pure: no models, no facades')
    ->expect(['App\Services\Payroll\PayslipCalculator', 'App\Services\Payroll\StatutoryContributions', 'App\Services\Attendance\AttendanceCalculator'])
    ->not->toUse(['Illuminate\Support\Facades', 'Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder', 'App\Models\PayslipRecord', 'App\Models\TimeLog']);

arch('mail is always queued')
    ->expect('App\Notifications')
    ->toImplement('Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue');

// Every notice lands in the bell (email is an extra for the urgent ones), so
// nothing important lives only in an inbox. The two auth emails are mail by nature.
it('sends every notification to the bell', function () {
    $mailOnly = ['QueuedVerifyEmail.php', 'QueuedResetPassword.php'];

    $files = glob(dirname(__DIR__, 2).'/app/Notifications/*.php') ?: [];
    expect($files)->not->toBeEmpty();

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        if (in_array(basename($file), $mailOnly, true)) {
            continue;
        }

        $source = (string) file_get_contents($file);
        expect(str_contains($source, "'database'"))->toBeTrue(basename($file).' must include the database (bell) channel')
            // ...written in the request, not left in the queue with the email.
            ->and(str_contains($source, 'WritesBellImmediately'))->toBeTrue(basename($file).' must use WritesBellImmediately');
    }
});

// $wire.upload(), $wire.refresh()… are Livewire's own JavaScript methods. A
// component action with the same name is silently unreachable from Blade:
// wire:submit="upload" calls the JS uploader, not the PHP method. Tests that
// ->call('upload') still pass, so only this check catches it.
it('has no Livewire action named like a built-in $wire method', function () {
    $reserved = ['upload', 'uploadMultiple', 'removeUpload', 'cancelUpload', 'entangle', 'watch', 'refresh', 'js', 'on', 'dispatchSelf', 'intercept'];
    $clashes = [];

    $root = dirname(__DIR__, 2).DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR.'app'.DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR.'Livewire';

    foreach (new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($root)) as $file) {
        if ($file->getExtension() !== 'php') {
            continue;
        }

        // app/Livewire/People/RequirementsChecklist.php → App\Livewire\People\RequirementsChecklist
        $relative = substr($file->getPathname(), strlen($root) + 1, -4);
        $class = 'App\\Livewire\\'.strtr($relative, ['/' => '\\']);

        if (! class_exists($class)) {
            continue;
        }

        foreach ((new ReflectionClass($class))->getMethods(ReflectionMethod::IS_PUBLIC) as $method) {
            if ($method->getDeclaringClass()->getName() === $class && in_array($method->getName(), $reserved, true)) {
                $clashes[] = "{$class}::{$method->getName()}";
            }
        }
    }

    expect($clashes)->toBe([]);
});

// "â€”" on screen instead of "—": a file was re-saved with the wrong encoding.
// It is easy to miss in review and ugly on payslips, so any such sequence fails.
it('has no garbled (double-encoded) characters in the code or views', function () {
    $root = dirname(__DIR__, 2);
    $patterns = ["\u{00E2}\u{20AC}", "\u{00C3}\u{00A9}", "\u{00E2}\u{201A}\u{00B1}"]; // â€ (— – " ' …), Ã© (é), â‚± (₱)
    $offenders = [];

    foreach (['app', 'config', 'database', 'resources', 'routes', 'tests', 'docs/features'] as $dir) {
        foreach (new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator("{$root}/{$dir}", FilesystemIterator::SKIP_DOTS)) as $file) {
            if (! in_array($file->getExtension(), ['php', 'md', 'js', 'css'], true) || $file->getFilename() === 'ArchitectureTest.php') {
                continue;
            }

            $contents = (string) file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

            foreach ($patterns as $pattern) {
                if (str_contains($contents, $pattern)) {
                    $offenders[] = substr($file->getPathname(), strlen($root) + 1);
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

Why does the role-removal test call actingAs($hr->fresh())?Every real request loads the user from the session again. The test does the same, so it proves what production does.

Deploying to Laravel Cloud

Four things the local setup gets away without: a real database for row locks, an object storage bucket because the app disk is wiped on every deploy, a queue worker for email, and a first Super Admin created from the console.

StepWhy
Push the project to GitHub (.env stays out)Cloud deploys from a repository; .env holds the mail password
Attach MySQLlockForUpdate() needs a database server; SQLite only serializes
Attach a bucket, set ATTENDANCE_PHOTO_DISK=s3Selfies and avatars survive deploys; the app streams them privately
Add a queue workerVerification and reset emails are queued
Set secrets in Cloud: APP_KEY, MAIL_PASSWORDNever in code; back up APP_KEY, it decrypts government IDs
Deploy: php artisan migrate --force && php artisan optimizeSchema and cached config
php artisan app:create-super-admin you@company.com "Name" (and --role=president / --role=vice-president)The first account, and the leadership's. These three have no employee record or number, so they can't register like staff; demo seeders never run in production
app/Console/Commands/CreateSuperAdmin.php66 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
<?php

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use App\Enums\Role;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rules\Password;

/**
 * Accounts that aren't employees here: the Super Admin (a system account), and the
 * President and Vice President (paid outside this payroll). They have no HR record and
 * no employee number (Role::withoutEmployeeRecord), so they can't register like staff:
 * they're created here, from the server console. The first Super Admin, on a fresh
 * database, is how anyone gets in at all.
 */
final class CreateSuperAdmin extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'app:create-super-admin {email} {name}
        {--role=super-admin : super-admin, president or vice-president}';

    protected $description = 'Create a Super Admin, President or Vice President account (no employee record; prompts for the password)';

    public function handle(): int
    {
        $email = strtolower((string) $this->argument('email'));
        $name = (string) $this->argument('name');
        $role = Role::tryFrom((string) $this->option('role'));

        if ($role === null || ! in_array($role, Role::withoutEmployeeRecord(), true)) {
            $this->error('The role is super-admin, president or vice-president. Everyone else is added by HR under Employees and registers.');

            return self::FAILURE;
        }

        $password = (string) $this->secret('Password (12+ characters, mixed case, numbers, symbols)');

        $validator = Validator::make(['email' => $email, 'name' => $name, 'password' => $password], [
            'email' => ['required', 'email', 'unique:users,email', 'unique:employee_profiles,email'],
            'name' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255'],
            'password' => ['required', Password::min(12)->mixedCase()->numbers()->symbols()],
        ]);

        if ($validator->fails()) {
            foreach ($validator->errors()->all() as $error) {
                $this->error($error);
            }

            return self::FAILURE;
        }

        DB::transaction(function () use ($email, $name, $password, $role) {
            $user = User::create(['name' => $name, 'email' => $email, 'password' => $password]);
            $user->forceFill(['email_verified_at' => now()])->save();
            $user->roles()->create(['role' => $role]);
        });

        $this->info($role === Role::SuperAdmin
            ? "Super Admin {$email} created. Sign in, then add HR staff from Employees and give them roles under Roles & Access."
            : "{$role->label()} {$email} created. They sign in with this email and password; turn on two-factor in Account Settings.");

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }
}

The Gmail app password was pasted into a chat while this was built. Revoke it in your Google account and create a new one before going live, then store it only as a Cloud secret.

Before Cloud: a one-week pilot on the laptop

For a trial week the app runs from the laptop at a fixed address, https://ossi.tail4ab8aa.ts.net, through Tailscale Funnel. It's free, unlike a fixed Cloudflare tunnel, which needs an owned domain. The pilot must not be the development app, so scripts/pilot/pilot-env.ps1 sets a few environment variables: its own SQLite file, production mode, the public URL. Real environment variables win over .env, so nothing in .env changes and the mail password stays there only. Small scripts keep the web server, queue worker and scheduler running (restarting any that stop), back up the database every night with VACUUM INTO (a consistent copy while it's in use), and start it all at sign-in.

Question you'd askAnswer
Why not just point the tunnel at Herd?Herd picks the site by host name and answered 404 for the ts.net name; the .test name has an underscore, which Tailscale rejects. PHP's built-in server with Laravel's router answers any host.
Can the code be updated during the week?Yes. PHP and Blade take effect on the next page load; CSS/JS need npm run build; migrations need a backup first, then pilot-artisan.ps1 migrate --force. The queue worker restarts itself hourly.
I run npm run dev for my own work. Does the pilot break?No. In production the app ignores Vite's public/hot (AppServiceProvider), so pilot users always get the built assets.
Why Tailscale and not Cloudflare?cloudflared tunnel --url is a Quick Tunnel: anonymous, so a new random trycloudflare.com address every start. A fixed Cloudflare address needs an owned domain; Tailscale Funnel's ts.net name is fixed and free. Two different companies: use one or the other.

How a visitor reaches the laptop:

flowchart LR
  P[Phone or PC, anywhere] -->|HTTPS| T[Tailscale Funnel
ossi.tail4ab8aa.ts.net]
  T -->|only port 8010| W[PHP server + Laravel
production mode]
  W --> D[(pilot.sqlite)]
  Q[Queue worker] --> D
  S[Scheduler] --> D
  B[Backup 2:00 AM] -->|VACUUM INTO| K[(pilot-backups, 14 kept)]
  H[Herd + dev database] -. untouched .- W
Set it up step by step (fresh laptop)
  1. Install Tailscale: winget install --id Tailscale.Tailscale (or tailscale.com/download/windows).
  2. Sign in: the 3×3-dot icon by the clock → Log in… → Google or Microsoft → Connect. Or run tailscale login and open its link. Check with tailscale status.
  3. Enable HTTPS once: login.tailscale.com/admin/dns → HTTPS Certificates → Enable HTTPS.
  4. On a different PC, set $PilotUrl in scripts\pilot\pilot-env.ps1 to its https://<name>.ts.net.
  5. Create the pilot database: scripts\pilot\setup-pilot.ps1 (migrations, shifts and holidays only, assets built; refuses to run twice).
  6. Start it: scripts\pilot\start-pilot.ps1. The first time Tailscale asks to enable Funnel with a link: open it, click Enable, run the script again. Check with tailscale funnel status. Then tailscale set --unattended=true, so it keeps running after a restart before anyone opens its tray app.
  7. Test from outside (a phone on mobile data): the login page is styled, a development account is refused, an unknown page shows a plain 404.
  8. Auto-start and backups: scripts\pilot\install-autostart.ps1; test one backup with backup-pilot.ps1.
  9. First Super Admin (a password only, no employee number): scripts\pilot\pilot-artisan.ps1 app:create-super-admin you@example.com "Name"; the President and VP the same way with --role=president / --role=vice-president. Then: laptop never sleeps, lid does nothing, Windows Update paused for the week.

Run the scripts as powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\pilot\<script>.ps1 from the project folder. Ending it: stop-pilot.ps1, uninstall-autostart.ps1, tailscale funnel --https=443 off.

You seeWhy, and the fix
ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED on the new address, right after renaming the machine in TailscaleThe Funnel is still set up under the old name. tailscale funnel reset, put the new address in $PilotUrl (scripts\pilot\pilot-env.ps1), then stop-pilot.ps1 and start-pilot.ps1. Only the machine name is yours to choose for free; the tailnet name is picked from Tailscale's suggestions, and .ts.net stays.
"This site can't be reached" (DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN)Tailscale isn't connected. After a restart it sat at "starting" because its tray app hadn't opened. Open Tailscale from the Start menu, then start-pilot.ps1 (which now does both). Prevented by tailscale set --unattended=true.
The address doesn't openTailscale signed out or the laptop asleep: tailscale status, then start-pilot.ps1.
502 / bad gatewayThe pilot's web server isn't running: start-pilot.ps1, and read storage\logs\pilot\web.log.
Herd's 404 pageThe tunnel points at Herd, which only answers its .test name: tailscale funnel --https=443 off, then start-pilot.ps1.
invalid hostname "ossi_official_site.test"Tailscale rejects the underscore. Tunnel to the pilot on port 8010, not to Herd.
A page without stylingnpm run build.
Opening it from the same laptop times outNormal for your own public address; test from a phone on mobile data.

Is the laptop safe? Only the app on port 8010 is exposed: not Windows, files or other sites, and no router ports. But the web server runs as your Windows user, so a serious bug in the app or in PHP's built-in server (a development server) would reach your files, .env and APP_KEY. For the week: BitLocker on, Defender and Firewall on, two-step verification on the Tailscale account, two-factor for Super Admin and HR, no everyday browsing on that laptop, backups copied off it, and end the pilot on time. Fine for a short supervised trial; real data long term belongs on Laravel Cloud.

# OSSI laptop pilot: the settings that differ from development.
#
# Dot-sourced by the other pilot scripts (. .\pilot-env.ps1). Real environment
# variables win over .env (Laravel loads .env without overwriting them), so these
# override only what's listed here. Everything else, the mail password included,
# still comes from your .env, which these scripts never change.

$PilotRoot = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..')).Path
$PilotPort = 8010
$PilotUrl = 'https://ossi.tail4ab8aa.ts.net'
$PilotDatabase = Join-Path $PilotRoot 'database\pilot.sqlite'
$PilotBackups = Join-Path $PilotRoot 'database\pilot-backups'
$PilotLogs = Join-Path $PilotRoot 'storage\logs\pilot'
$Tailscale = 'C:\Program Files\Tailscale\tailscale.exe'

# Production mode: debug pages off, destructive DB commands blocked, strict passwords, HTTPS.
$env:APP_ENV = 'production'
$env:APP_DEBUG = 'false'
$env:APP_URL = $PilotUrl
$env:ASSET_URL = $PilotUrl

# Its own database: real people only, no demo data. Sessions, cache and the queue live
# in the database too, so they're separate from development as well.
$env:DB_CONNECTION = 'sqlite'
$env:DB_DATABASE = $PilotDatabase

$env:SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE = 'true'

# Reverb (live bell) isn't reachable through the tunnel; the bell updates on each page load.
$env:BROADCAST_CONNECTION = 'log'

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $PilotBackups, $PilotLogs | Out-Null
scripts/pilot/start-pilot.ps151 lines
Copied from the repository as it is today
# Starts the pilot: the web server, the queue worker and the scheduler (each kept
# running by keep-running.ps1, in hidden windows), and the Tailscale public address.
# Safe to run again: anything already running is left alone.
#
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\pilot\start-pilot.ps1

. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'pilot-env.ps1')

if (-not (Test-Path $PilotDatabase)) {
    Write-Host 'No pilot database yet. Run setup-pilot.ps1 first.' -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}

$keeper = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'keep-running.ps1'

foreach ($name in 'web', 'queue', 'scheduler') {
    $running = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name = 'powershell.exe'" |
        Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*keep-running.ps1*-Name $name*" }

    if ($running) {
        Write-Host "${name}: already running"
        continue
    }

    Start-Process powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -ArgumentList @('-NoProfile', '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass', '-File', "`"$keeper`"", '-Name', $name)
    Write-Host "${name}: started"
}

# Tailscale connected first: after a restart it can sit at "starting" until its tray app
# opens (seen 2026-10-21; unattended mode, `tailscale set --unattended=true`, avoids it).
$state = { try { (& $Tailscale status --json 2>$null | ConvertFrom-Json).BackendState } catch { '' } }
if ((& $state) -ne 'Running') {
    if (-not (Get-Process tailscale-ipn -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        Start-Process 'C:\Program Files\Tailscale\tailscale-ipn.exe'
    }
    foreach ($i in 1..30) {
        if ((& $state) -eq 'Running') { break }
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    }
}
if ((& $state) -ne 'Running') {
    Write-Host 'Tailscale is not connected yet, so the public address is off. Open Tailscale from the tray, sign in if asked, then run this again.' -ForegroundColor Yellow
    exit 1
}

# The fixed public address (it stays set across restarts; this just makes sure).
& $Tailscale funnel --bg --yes "http://127.0.0.1:$PilotPort" | Out-Null

Write-Host ''
Write-Host "Pilot running at $PilotUrl" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "Logs: $PilotLogs"

Version 2 roadmap

The 41 requests from the V2 wishlist, each checked against the code as it is today. Every item can be built; two only partly. Phase 2.0, the 201 file and Buy Load are done (chapters 13 to 15), so fourteen are now finished.

22 builtIdle logout, the privacy acknowledgement, payslips by period; from 2.0: late details, probation alerts, filed dates, FAQs, announcements; from 2.1: the 201 checklist (RAE), uploads, expiry alerts, promised dates; Buy Load with GCash; payroll adjustments; the payroll discrepancy report; merits and demerits; Notices to Explain; promotions; reimbursements; leave requirements; deployment costs; and loan summaries (My Loans).
7 partly builtThe data or the plumbing exists (photo + GPS pipeline, deductions, hire date, supervisor on overtime, the attendance dashboard). V2 extends it.
10 newNew tables, screens and Actions, built with the same pattern as V1: Action + audit entry + policy + tests.
2 limitedA website can't block screenshots, and donations need payroll consent rules.

Foundations to build first

About half the items need the same five building blocks. Building them once, before any feature, keeps V2 consistent and stops every feature from inventing its own version.

Building blockWhat it isUsed by
NotificationsLaravel notifications on the database and mail channels, queued, with a bell and unread count in the top bar. One notification class per event.Probation, expiring documents, 14-day duty, discrepancies, announcements, NTE, approvals
SchedulerDaily commands in routes/console.php (Schedule::command(...)->dailyAt('06:00')). Laravel Cloud runs the scheduler; locally, php artisan schedule:work. Each check is idempotent: it records what it already sent so a rerun never notifies twice.Probation, expiry, 14-day duty
Private attachmentsOne attachments table (polymorphic: leave, complaint, reimbursement, 201 document). Files go on the private disk, the same pattern as PunchPhotoStore. They are streamed through a policy-checked controller, with MIME and size validated on upload.201 file, leave requirements, receipts, complaint proof, reports
Approval stepsAn ordered list of approvers per request type, configured as data. Requests move from step to step, and each decision is audited. This replaces the single reviewed_by column.Chain of command, leave, overtime, reimbursement, training, deduction stop
Operations roleNew Role::Operations and abilities like Ability::IssueNte. These are added to Ability::roles(), so gates, sidebar and the access test update together.NTE, opening/closing reports, duty monitoring, deployment claims

GCash QR: free vs. automatic (superseded on 2026-10-09 by Borrow Load)

OptionCostHow payment is confirmed
Static GCash QR (recommended for V2)Free to build and run. No API, no gateway fee.Manual: the employee submits the reference number and receipt screenshot; IT matches it in the GCash app. The reference number is unique in the database, so the same payment can't be claimed twice.
Payment gateway (e.g. PayMongo, Xendit with QR Ph)A fee per transaction, plus business registration with the provider.Automatic: the gateway calls the app back (a webhook) when payment succeeds.

If many employees will pay this way, use a GCash for Business account rather than a personal one: personal accounts have monthly receiving limits. Check the current fees and limits with GCash before going live.

13

V2 phase 2.0: quick wins

Seven roadmap items plus the notification foundation the later phases build on: filed dates, full late details, the payslip disclaimer, screenshot deterrents, probation alerts, announcements and FAQs. One new gate, PublishContent (Admin, HR, Super Admin), covers the content features.

No polling, on purposeEvery request resets the idle timeout. A bell that polled every minute would keep an unattended payroll screen signed in forever, so it refreshes on page loads instead.
Idempotent schedulersA unique index on sent_alerts plus createOrFirst: a doubled or rerun job never notifies twice.
Honest about screenshotsNo website can block them. Watermark + no print + cover on blur + audit make a leak traceable instead.

Probation alerts

The claim, the notification and the audit entry share one transaction. If queueing fails, the claim rolls back and tomorrow's run tries again.

WhenAlert name (claimed once)Title
30 days beforeprobation.upcomingProbation ending soon: Name
On the day, or within a week of itprobation.dueProbation ends today, or "ended 3 days ago" if the scheduler was late
Every 7 days after, while still Probationaryprobation.overdue.1, .2, …Probation ended 14 days ago: Name (cites Art. 296)
Weekly without a "last sent" dateEach alert name can be claimed once, so the week number goes into the name: 'probation.overdue.'.intdiv($daysPast, 7). Daily runs in between find it already claimed; a new week is a new name.
Why keep remindingLabor Code Art. 296: someone allowed to keep working after probation becomes regular by law, whatever the record says. So until HR decides, the reminder comes back weekly, an amber "Probation ended Apr 8" mark shows on the Employees list (EmployeeProfile::probationOverdueSince()), and HR's dashboard tile says "3 already past 6 months" (scopeProbationOverdue).

<?php

namespace App\Actions\People;

use App\Enums\Ability;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Models\SentAlert;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\ProbationEnding;
use App\Queries\People\ProbationEndingQuery;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Notification;

/**
 * Run daily by the scheduler. Each alert goes out once, however often this runs:
 *
 *   "ending soon"             30 days before          probation.upcoming
 *   "ends today"              on the day (or up to    probation.due
 *                             a week late, worded as
 *                             "ended N days ago")
 *   "ended N days ago"        every 7 days after,     probation.overdue.1, .2, …
 *                             until HR changes the status
 */
final class SendProbationAlerts
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly ProbationEndingQuery $query,
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @return int how many alerts were sent
     */
    public function handle(CarbonImmutable $today): int
    {
        $profiles = $this->query->handle($today);

        if ($profiles->isEmpty()) {
            return 0;
        }

        $recipients = User::query()->notifiable(Ability::ManagePeople->roles())->get();
        $sent = 0;

        foreach ($profiles as $profile) {
            $endsOn = ProbationEndingQuery::endsOn($profile);

            if ($endsOn === null) {
                continue;
            }

            // Days since it ended: negative while still ahead. One alert name per week overdue,
            // so the weekly reminder is sent once a week (each name only once).
            $daysPast = (int) $endsOn->diffInDays($today, false);
            $alert = match (true) {
                $daysPast < 0 => 'probation.upcoming',
                $daysPast < 7 => 'probation.due',
                default => 'probation.overdue.'.intdiv($daysPast, 7),
            };

            // Claim, notify and audit together: if queueing the notification
            // fails, the claim rolls back and tomorrow's run tries again.
            $wasSent = DB::transaction(function () use ($alert, $profile, $recipients, $endsOn, $daysPast) {
                if (! SentAlert::claim($alert, $profile)) {
                    return false;
                }

                Notification::send($recipients, new ProbationEnding($profile, $endsOn, $daysPast));

                $this->audit->record(AuditArea::People, 'probation.alert_sent', "Probation alert for {$profile->name} (ends {$endsOn->format('M j, Y')})", $profile, [
                    'alert' => $alert,
                    'ends_on' => $endsOn->toDateString(),
                    'recipients' => $recipients->count(),
                ]);

                return true;
            });

            $sent += $wasSent ? 1 : 0;
        }

        return $sent;
    }
}
app/Models/SentAlert.php55 lines

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\MorphTo;

/**
 * "This alert was already sent about this record." The unique index on
 * (alert, subject) is what makes a scheduled check safe to run twice.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property string $alert
 * @property string $subject_type
 * @property int $subject_id
 * @property CarbonImmutable $sent_at
 * @property-read Model $subject
 */
#[Fillable(['alert', 'subject_type', 'subject_id', 'sent_at'])]
class SentAlert extends Model
{
    public $timestamps = false;

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['sent_at' => 'datetime'];
    }

    /**
     * @return MorphTo<Model, $this>
     */
    public function subject(): MorphTo
    {
        return $this->morphTo();
    }

    /**
     * Claims the alert for this subject. True only the first time: a second
     * run, even a concurrent one, hits the unique index and gets false.
     */
    public static function claim(string $alert, Model $subject): bool
    {
        $row = static::query()->createOrFirst(
            ['alert' => $alert, 'subject_type' => $subject->getMorphClass(), 'subject_id' => $subject->getKey()],
            ['sent_at' => CarbonImmutable::now()],
        );

        return $row->wasRecentlyCreated;
    }
}
