<?php

namespace App\Models;

use App\Enums\Position;
use App\Enums\ReferralStatus;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;

/**
 * Someone an employee referred for hiring (hiring perks). HR links the record of the
 * person once hired; the bonus and the days they must stay are frozen then, from the
 * terms in force (Referral::terms). The referrer is paid on their payslip once the hire
 * has stayed that long (PayDueReferralBonuses). Nothing is fillable: the Actions set it.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property int $referrer_id
 * @property string $applicant_name
 * @property string $applicant_phone
 * @property Position|null $position
 * @property string|null $note
 * @property ReferralStatus $status
 * @property int|null $employee_profile_id the hire's record, once hired
 * @property string|null $bonus_amount
 * @property CarbonImmutable|null $bonus_due_on
 * @property int|null $decided_by
 * @property CarbonImmutable|null $decided_at
 * @property string|null $decision_note
 * @property int|null $payroll_adjustment_id
 * @property int|null $paid_in_run_id
 * @property CarbonImmutable $created_at
 * @property-read User $referrer
 * @property-read EmployeeProfile|null $hire
 * @property-read User|null $decider
 * @property-read PayrollRun|null $paidInRun
 */
class Referral extends Model
{
    /** The "referrals" Setting HR edits (SaveReferralTerms). */
    public const SETTING = 'referrals';

    /**
     * @var array<string, mixed>
     */
    protected $attributes = [
        'status' => 'submitted',
    ];

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'position' => Position::class,
            'status' => ReferralStatus::class,
            'bonus_amount' => 'decimal:2',
            'bonus_due_on' => 'date',
            'decided_at' => 'datetime',
        ];
    }

    /**
     * The terms in force: what HR set on the Referrals page, else the starting values
     * (config hr.referrals). Company policy, not law.
     *
     * @return array{bonus_amount: int, days_to_stay: int}
     */
    public static function terms(): array
    {
        $saved = Setting::value(self::SETTING);
        $start = (array) config('hr.referrals');
        $pick = fn (string $key) => (int) ($saved[$key] ?? $start[$key] ?? 0);

        return ['bonus_amount' => $pick('bonus_amount'), 'days_to_stay' => $pick('days_to_stay')];
    }

    /** Anyone still working here and paid through this payroll may refer someone. */
    public static function canRefer(User $user): bool
    {
        $user->loadMissing('employeeProfile');

        return $user->employeeProfile !== null && $user->employeeProfile->employment_status->isActive() && ! $user->isPaidOutsidePayroll();
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function referrer(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'referrer_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<EmployeeProfile, $this>
     */
    public function hire(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(EmployeeProfile::class, 'employee_profile_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function decider(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'decided_by');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<PayrollRun, $this>
     */
    public function paidInRun(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(PayrollRun::class, 'paid_in_run_id');
    }

    /**
     * Still open: with HR, or hired and the bonus not settled yet.
     *
     * @param  Builder<Referral>  $query
     */
    public function scopeOpen(Builder $query): void
    {
        $query->whereIn('status', [ReferralStatus::Submitted, ReferralStatus::Hired]);
    }

    /**
     * Whether the hire stayed until the bonus was due: still working here, or their last
     * day (the resignation that closed their account) on or after the due date. Null while
     * it isn't due yet.
     */
    public function hireStayed(CarbonImmutable $asOf): ?bool
    {
        if ($this->bonus_due_on === null || $this->hire === null || $this->bonus_due_on->isAfter($asOf)) {
            return null;
        }

        if ($this->hire->employment_status->isActive()) {
            return true;
        }

        // Their last day, from the resignation that closed the account.
        $lastDay = $this->hire->user_id === null ? null : Resignation::query()->where('user_id', $this->hire->user_id)
            ->whereNotNull('separated_at')->latest('id')->value('last_day');

        return $lastDay !== null && ! CarbonImmutable::parse($lastDay)->isBefore($this->bonus_due_on);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Payroll;

use App\Enums\AdjustmentCategory;
use App\Enums\AdjustmentStatus;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\ReferralStatus;
use App\Models\PayrollAdjustment;
use App\Models\PayrollRun;
use App\Models\Referral;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\ReferralNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;

/**
 * Called by GeneratePayslip, inside its transaction, before the figures are computed:
 * each of this employee's referrals whose bonus fell due by the end of the cut-off
 * becomes a Referral bonus line on this payslip, if the hire stayed that long
 * (Referral::hireStayed); if they didn't, the referral is closed without a bonus and
 * the referrer told. Set by HR's terms, so it's added as approved (no second check).
 */
final class PayDueReferralBonuses
{
    public function __construct(private readonly AuditLogger $audit) {}

    /**
     * @return int how many bonuses were added
     */
    public function handle(PayrollRun $run, User $employee, User $actor): int
    {
        $added = 0;
        $cutOff = CarbonImmutable::parse($run->end_date);

        $due = Referral::query()->with('hire')->where('referrer_id', $employee->id)->where('status', ReferralStatus::Hired)
            ->whereDate('bonus_due_on', '<=', $cutOff->toDateString())->lockForUpdate()->orderBy('id')->get();

        foreach ($due as $referral) {
            if ($referral->hireStayed($cutOff) !== true) {
                $referral->forceFill(['status' => ReferralStatus::Forfeited])->save();
                $this->audit->record(AuditArea::People, 'referral.forfeited', "No referral bonus for {$employee->name}: {$referral->applicant_name} left before {$referral->bonus_due_on?->format('M j, Y')}", $referral, causer: $actor);
                $employee->notify(new ReferralNotice($referral, ReferralNotice::FORFEITED));

                continue;
            }

            if ((float) $referral->bonus_amount <= 0) {
                $referral->forceFill(['status' => ReferralStatus::Paid, 'paid_in_run_id' => $run->id])->save();

                continue;
            }

            $adjustment = new PayrollAdjustment;
            $adjustment->forceFill([
                'payroll_run_id' => $run->id,
                'user_id' => $employee->id,
                'category' => AdjustmentCategory::ReferralBonus,
                'amount' => $referral->bonus_amount,
                'reason' => "Referred {$referral->applicant_name}, hired ".$referral->hire?->hire_date?->format('M j, Y'),
                'status' => AdjustmentStatus::Approved,
                'created_by' => $actor->id,
                'reviewed_by' => $referral->decided_by,
                'reviewed_at' => $referral->decided_at ?? CarbonImmutable::now(),
            ])->save();

            $referral->forceFill(['status' => ReferralStatus::Paid, 'payroll_adjustment_id' => $adjustment->id, 'paid_in_run_id' => $run->id])->save();
            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Payroll, 'referral.paid', "Paid {$employee->name}'s referral bonus of ₱".number_format((float) $referral->bonus_amount, 2)." on {$run->periodLabel()}", $referral, causer: $actor);
            $added++;
        }

        return $added;
    }
}
38

Equipment and accountability

Uniforms, radios and gear: who issues them, what the employee signs, and when the company may charge for them. Operations issues to the guards it deploys (a Satellite: its region's), Admin to office staff (EquipmentIssue::canIssueTo). Admin keeps the item list and prices. Employees ask for items on My Equipment.

Two kinds of item, two kinds of paperA uniform is charged (the owner's rule): its price becomes an EmployeeDeduction waiting for the employee's authority to deduct on My Payslips (Labor Code Art. 113). Until they tap "I authorize this", scopeTakenFromPay skips it. Anything else is company property. The employee confirms they received it and are accountable for it, in a sentence kept word for word in English or Filipino (AcknowledgeEquipment). Nothing is deducted for it.
Charged only after being heardDamage or loss follows DOLE's conditions for deducting a loss, each one enforced in code. The employee is told and gets 5 days to explain (ReportEquipmentIncident, ExplainEquipmentIncident). Their head (Heads) decides only once they explained or the days passed (readyToDecide). The decision states why, the amount is the actual loss with how it was arrived at, and each payslip takes at most 20% of a week's wages (daily rate × 6 × 20%, maxInstallmentFor). The deduction's basis is LossOrDamage, which Accounting can't pick by hand.
One masterlist, one clearanceIssuing a radio marks it In use with that person on the Radios masterlist. Returning it puts it back in stock, and a loss report marks it Lost. On a resignation, the clearance lists radios and unreturned gear. A uniform's unpaid balance shows in final pay like a loan.

/**
 * One item asked for by, or given to, one person: a uniform (charged, with their authority to
 * deduct), a radio from the masterlist, or other company gear (they sign that they're
 * accountable for it). Who issues (the owner's choice, 2026-10-23): Operations for the guards
 * it deploys (a Satellite: its region's), Admin for office staff; the Super Admin as backup.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property int $user_id
 * @property int|null $equipment_item_id
 * @property int|null $radio_id
 * @property string $label
 * @property string|null $size

 * @property string|null $unit_price
 * @property bool $charged a uniform: paid by the employee through an authorized deduction
 * @property int|null $employee_deduction_id

 * @property string|null $reject_reason
 * @property int|null $issued_by
 * @property CarbonImmutable|null $issued_at
 * @property CarbonImmutable|null $acknowledged_at
 * @property string|null $acknowledgement the sentence they confirmed, word for word
 * @property int|null $returned_to

 * @property string|null $return_note
 * @property CarbonImmutable $created_at

 * @property-read User $user

 * @property-read Radio|null $radio
 * @property-read User|null $issuer
 * @property-read EmployeeDeduction|null $deduction
 * @property-read Collection<int, EquipmentIncident> $incidents
 */
class EquipmentIssue extends Model
{
    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'status' => EquipmentStatus::class,
            'unit_price' => 'decimal:2',
            'charged' => 'boolean',
            'requested_at' => 'datetime',
            'issued_at' => 'datetime',
            'acknowledged_at' => 'datetime',
            'returned_at' => 'datetime',
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Whether this person may issue to (or take back from, or report an item of) that one.
     * Never to yourself; only to someone still on the payroll.
     */
    public static function canIssueTo(User $issuer, User $employee): bool
    {
        $employee->loadMissing('employeeProfile');

        if ($issuer->is($employee) || $employee->employeeProfile === null || ! $issuer->can('issue-equipment')) {
            return false;
        }

        return match (true) {
            $issuer->hasRole(Role::SuperAdmin) => true,
            ! $employee->employeeProfile->is_office_staff => $issuer->hasRole(Role::OperationsHq) || ($issuer->hasRole(Role::SatelliteOperations) && $issuer->canSeeEmployee($employee)),
            default => $issuer->hasRole(Role::Admin),
        };
    }

    /**
     * Who to tell when this person asks for something: Operations for a guard (Operation HQ
     * and their region's Satellite), Admin for office staff.
     *
     * @return Collection<int, User>
     */
    public static function issuersFor(User $employee): Collection
    {
        $employee->loadMissing('employeeProfile');

        if ($employee->employeeProfile !== null && ! $employee->employeeProfile->is_office_staff) {
            return Heads::of($employee);
        }

        return User::query()->notifiable([Role::Admin])->whereKeyNot($employee->id)->get();
    }

    /**
     * Narrows a query of users to the people this viewer issues to.
     *
     * @param  Builder<User>  $users
     */
    public static function constrainPeopleHandledBy(Builder $users, User $viewer): void
    {
        match (true) {
            $viewer->hasRole(Role::SuperAdmin) => null,
            $viewer->hasRole(Role::OperationsHq) => $users->fieldStaff(),
            $viewer->hasRole(Role::SatelliteOperations) => $users->fieldStaff()->visibleTo($viewer),
            $viewer->hasRole(Role::Admin) => $users->officeStaff(),
            default => $users->whereRaw('1 = 0'),
        };
    }

    /**
     * The items of the people this viewer issues to.
     *
     * @param  Builder<EquipmentIssue>  $query
     */
    public function scopeHandledBy(Builder $query, User $viewer): void
    {
        $query->whereHas('user', fn (Builder $users) => self::constrainPeopleHandledBy($users, $viewer));
    }

    /**
     * Still with the person and theirs to give back: company property issued and not
     * returned or lost (a charged uniform is theirs).
     *
     * @param  Builder<EquipmentIssue>  $query
     */
    public function scopeOutstanding(Builder $query): void
    {
        $query->where('status', EquipmentStatus::Issued)->where('charged', false);
    }

    public function isCompanyProperty(): bool
    {
        return ! $this->charged;
    }

    public function total(): float
    {
        return round((float) $this->unit_price * $this->quantity, 2);
    }

    /** "Uniform polo (L) × 2" */
    public function describe(): string
    {
        return $this->label.($this->size ? " ({$this->size})" : '').($this->quantity > 1 ? " × {$this->quantity}" : '');
    }

    /** An open damage or loss case: reported, not decided yet. */
    public function openIncident(): ?EquipmentIncident
    {
        return $this->incidents->first(fn (EquipmentIncident $incident) => $incident->decision === null);
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function user(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class);
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<EquipmentItem, $this>
     */
    public function item(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(EquipmentItem::class, 'equipment_item_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<Radio, $this>
     */
    public function radio(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Radio::class);
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function issuer(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'issued_by');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<EmployeeDeduction, $this>
     */
    public function deduction(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(EmployeeDeduction::class, 'employee_deduction_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return HasMany<EquipmentIncident, $this>
     */
    public function incidents(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(EquipmentIncident::class)->orderBy('id');
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Equipment;

use App\Actions\Payroll\SaveEmployeeDeduction;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\DeductionAuthorizationBasis;
use App\Enums\DeductionType;
use App\Enums\EquipmentKind;
use App\Enums\EquipmentStatus;
use App\Enums\RadioStatus;
use App\Models\EquipmentIssue;
use App\Models\EquipmentItem;
use App\Models\Radio;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\UpdateNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Gives an item to someone: from the list, or a radio from the NTC masterlist; new, or
 * answering their request.
 *
 *  - A uniform is charged (the owner's rule): its price becomes a deduction the employee must
 *    authorize on My Payslips (Labor Code Art. 113) before any payslip takes it.
 *  - Anything else stays company property: they confirm on My Equipment that they received it
 *    and are accountable for it. Nothing is deducted unless it's later lost or damaged through
 *    their fault, decided after they were heard (DecideEquipmentIncident).
 *
 * A radio issued here is marked in use, with them (and at their post), on the masterlist.
 */
final class IssueEquipment
{
    public const MAX_QUANTITY = 20;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
        private readonly SaveEmployeeDeduction $saveDeduction,
    ) {}

    public function handle(User $issuer, User $employee, ?EquipmentItem $item, ?Radio $radio, ?string $size, int $quantity, ?float $installment, ?EquipmentIssue $request = null): EquipmentIssue
    {
        if (! EquipmentIssue::canIssueTo($issuer, $employee)) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        if (($item === null) === ($radio === null)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueItem' => 'Choose an item or a radio.']);
        }

        if ($request !== null && ($request->user_id !== $employee->id || $request->status !== EquipmentStatus::Requested)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueItem' => 'That request was already answered.']);
        }

        if ($item !== null) {
            if (! $item->is_active) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueItem' => 'That item is no longer given out.']);
            }

            $size = $item->has_sizes ? $size : null;

            if ($item->has_sizes && ! in_array($size, EquipmentItem::SIZES, true)) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueSize' => 'Choose the size.']);
            }

            if ($quantity < 1 || $quantity > self::MAX_QUANTITY) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueQuantity' => 'From 1 to '.self::MAX_QUANTITY.'.']);
            }
        } else {
            $size = null;
            $quantity = 1;

            if ($radio?->status !== RadioStatus::Spare) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueRadio' => 'Only a radio in stock (Spare) can be issued.']);
            }
        }

        $charged = $item?->kind === EquipmentKind::Uniform;
        $total = $charged ? round((float) $item->unit_price * $quantity, 2) : 0.0;

        if ($charged && $total <= 0) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueItem' => 'Set this uniform\'s price on the item list first.']);
        }

        if ($charged && ($installment === null || $installment <= 0 || $installment > $total)) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['issueInstallment' => 'Per payslip: more than ₱0 and at most the total, ₱'.number_format($total, 2).'.']);
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($issuer, $employee, $item, $radio, $size, $quantity, $installment, $request, $charged, $total) {
            $issue = $request ?? new EquipmentIssue;
            $label = $radio !== null ? "{$radio->brand} {$radio->model} radio (SN {$radio->serial_number})" : $item->name;

            $issue->forceFill([
                'user_id' => $employee->id,
                'equipment_item_id' => $item?->id,
                'radio_id' => $radio?->id,
                'label' => $label,
                'size' => $size,
                'quantity' => $quantity,
                'unit_price' => $item?->unit_price,
                'charged' => $charged,
                'status' => EquipmentStatus::Issued,
                'issued_by' => $issuer->id,
                'issued_at' => now(),
            ])->save();

            if ($charged) {
                // Their authority to deduct, asked on My Payslips; nothing is taken until they give it.
                $deduction = $this->saveDeduction->handle($employee, $issue->describe(), DeductionType::Uniform, (float) $installment, $total, $issuer, DeductionAuthorizationBasis::Employee);
                $deduction->forceFill(['remaining_balance' => number_format($total, 2, '.', '')])->save();
                $issue->forceFill(['employee_deduction_id' => $deduction->id])->save();
            }

            if ($radio !== null) {
                $radio->forceFill([
                    'status' => RadioStatus::InUse,
                    'assigned_user_id' => $employee->id,
                    'client_id' => $employee->employeeProfile?->is_office_staff ? null : $employee->employeeProfile?->client_id,
                ])->save();
            }

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Operations, 'equipment.issued', "Issued {$issue->describe()} to {$employee->name}".($charged ? ' (charged ₱'.number_format($total, 2).', authority to deduct asked)' : ''), $issue, [
                'new' => ['charged' => $charged, 'total' => $charged ? $total : null, 'installment' => $charged ? $installment : null, 'from_request' => $request !== null],
            ], causer: $issuer);

            UpdateNotice::tell($employee, $issuer, $charged ? 'Uniform issued: confirm and authorize' : 'Equipment issued: confirm you received it',
                $issue->describe().($charged
                    ? "\n₱".number_format($total, 2).', ₱'.number_format((float) $installment, 2).' per payslip once you authorize it on My Payslips. Confirm you received it on My Equipment.'
                    : "\nCompany property. Confirm on My Equipment that you received it."),
                route('my-equipment'), 'package', email: true);

            return $issue;
        });
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Equipment;

use App\Actions\Payroll\SaveEmployeeDeduction;
use App\Enums\AuditArea;
use App\Enums\DeductionAuthorizationBasis;
use App\Enums\DeductionType;
use App\Enums\EquipmentIncidentDecision;
use App\Enums\EquipmentIncidentKind;
use App\Enums\EquipmentStatus;
use App\Models\EquipmentIncident;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Notifications\UpdateNotice;
use App\Services\AuditLogger;
use Illuminate\Auth\Access\AuthorizationException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

/**
 * Their head decides a damage or loss report, only once due process is done (they explained,
 * or the days passed). DOLE's conditions for deducting a loss or damage, each enforced:
 *  - the employee is shown responsible: the decision says why;
 *  - they had a fair chance to explain: readyToDecide();
 *  - no more than the actual loss: the amount, and how it was arrived at (a quote, the price);
 *  - at most 20% of a week's wages per payslip: EquipmentIncident::maxInstallmentFor().
 * Charged, it becomes a deduction ("Loss or damage, after due process") with that balance.
 * A lost item leaves their hands either way.
 */
final class DecideEquipmentIncident
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly AuditLogger $audit,
        private readonly SaveEmployeeDeduction $saveDeduction,
    ) {}

    public function handle(User $decider, EquipmentIncident $incident, bool $charge, string $reason, ?float $amount = null, ?string $amountBasis = null, ?float $installment = null): EquipmentIncident
    {
        $incident->loadMissing('issue.user');
        $employee = $incident->issue->user;

        if (! EquipmentIncident::canDecide($decider, $employee)) {
            throw new AuthorizationException;
        }

        if (! $incident->readyToDecide()) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['decision' => $incident->decision !== null
                ? 'This was already decided.'
                : 'They can still explain until '.$incident->explain_by->format('M j, Y').'. Decide after that, or once they have explained.']);
        }

        $reason = trim($reason);

        if (mb_strlen($reason) < 10) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['decisionReason' => $charge ? 'Say why it was their fault.' : 'Say why they are not charged.']);
        }

        if ($charge) {
            $this->checkCharge($employee, $amount, $amountBasis, $installment);
        }

        return DB::transaction(function () use ($decider, $incident, $employee, $charge, $reason, $amount, $amountBasis, $installment) {
            $locked = EquipmentIncident::query()->with('issue')->lockForUpdate()->findOrFail($incident->id);

            if ($locked->decision !== null) {
                throw ValidationException::withMessages(['decision' => 'This was already decided.']);
            }

            $deductionId = null;

            if ($charge) {
                $deduction = $this->saveDeduction->handle($employee, "{$locked->kind->label()}: {$locked->issue->describe()}", DeductionType::Equipment, (float) $installment, (float) $amount, $decider, DeductionAuthorizationBasis::LossOrDamage);
                $deduction->forceFill(['remaining_balance' => number_format((float) $amount, 2, '.', '')])->save();
                $deductionId = $deduction->id;
            }

            $locked->forceFill([
                'decision' => $charge ? EquipmentIncidentDecision::Charged : EquipmentIncidentDecision::NotCharged,
                'decision_reason' => mb_substr($reason, 0, 2000),
                'loss_amount' => $charge ? number_format((float) $amount, 2, '.', '') : null,
                'amount_basis' => $charge ? mb_substr(trim((string) $amountBasis), 0, 300) : null,
                'installment' => $charge ? number_format((float) $installment, 2, '.', '') : null,
                'employee_deduction_id' => $deductionId,
                'decided_by' => $decider->id,
                'decided_at' => now(),
            ])->save();

            if ($locked->kind === EquipmentIncidentKind::Lost) {
                $locked->issue->forceFill(['status' => EquipmentStatus::Lost])->save();
            }

            $this->audit->record(AuditArea::Operations, 'equipment.incident_decided', ($charge ? 'Charged' : 'Did not charge')." {$employee->name} for {$locked->issue->describe()} ({$locked->kind->value})", $locked, [
                'new' => ['decision' => $locked->decision?->value, 'amount' => $charge ? $amount : null, 'installment' => $charge ? $installment : null, 'reason' => $reason],
            ], causer: $decider);

            UpdateNotice::tell($employee, $decider, $charge ? "Charged: {$locked->issue->describe()}" : "Not charged: {$locked->issue->describe()}",
                $charge
                    ? '₱'.number_format((float) $amount, 2).', ₱'.number_format((float) $installment, 2)." per payslip.\nWhy: {$reason}"
                    : "Why: {$reason}",
                route('my-equipment'), 'package', email: true);

            return $locked;
        });
    }

    private function checkCharge(User $employee, ?float $amount, ?string $amountBasis, ?float $installment): void
    {
        if ($amount === null || $amount <= 0 || $amount > 999999) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['lossAmount' => 'Enter the actual loss: the repair cost, or what replacing it costs.']);
        }

        if (mb_strlen(trim((string) $amountBasis)) < 5) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['amountBasis' => 'Say how you got the amount (a repair quote, the purchase price…). It may not be more than the actual loss.']);
        }

        if ($installment === null || $installment <= 0 || $installment > $amount) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['installment' => 'Per payslip: more than ₱0 and at most the amount.']);
        }

        $cap = EquipmentIncident::maxInstallmentFor($employee);

        if ($cap === null) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['installment' => 'Set their daily rate first: the law caps this at 20% of a week\'s wages per payslip.']);
        }

        if ($installment > $cap) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['installment' => 'At most ₱'.number_format($cap, 2).' per payslip: 20% of a week\'s wages (DOLE).']);
        }
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use App\Enums\EquipmentIncidentDecision;
use App\Enums\EquipmentIncidentKind;
use App\Support\Heads;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;

/**
 * A company item reported damaged or lost. Due process before any charge (DOLE's rule on
 * deductions for loss or damage): the employee is told and may explain in writing within
 * EXPLAIN_DAYS; only then does their head decide whether it was their fault, and charge no
 * more than the actual loss, at most 20% of a week's wages per payslip.
 *
 * @property int $id
 * @property int $equipment_issue_id
 * @property EquipmentIncidentKind $kind
 * @property string $details
 * @property int $reported_by
 * @property CarbonImmutable $explain_by
 * @property string|null $explanation
 * @property CarbonImmutable|null $explained_at
 * @property EquipmentIncidentDecision|null $decision
 * @property string|null $decision_reason
 * @property string|null $loss_amount
 * @property string|null $amount_basis
 * @property string|null $installment
 * @property int|null $employee_deduction_id
 * @property int|null $decided_by
 * @property CarbonImmutable|null $decided_at
 * @property CarbonImmutable $created_at
 * @property CarbonImmutable $updated_at
 * @property-read EquipmentIssue $issue
 * @property-read User $reporter
 * @property-read User|null $decider
 */
class EquipmentIncident extends Model
{
    /** Calendar days to explain, as for a Notice to Explain (NoticeToExplain::MIN_DAYS). */
    public const EXPLAIN_DAYS = 5;

    /** DOLE: a deduction for loss or damage may not exceed 20% of the employee's wages in a week. */
    public const WEEKLY_WAGE_SHARE = 0.20;

    /** The week the cap is figured on: six working days (my assumption; confirm with HR). */
    public const DAYS_PER_WEEK = 6;

    /**
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'kind' => EquipmentIncidentKind::class,
            'explain_by' => 'date',
            'explained_at' => 'datetime',
            'decision' => EquipmentIncidentDecision::class,
            'loss_amount' => 'decimal:2',
            'installment' => 'decimal:2',
            'decided_at' => 'datetime',
        ];
    }

    /** Their head decides (Heads; the Super Admin as backup). Never the person themselves. */
    public static function canDecide(User $decider, User $employee): bool
    {
        return Heads::isHeadOf($decider, $employee);
    }

    public function canStillExplain(?CarbonImmutable $today = null): bool
    {
        return $this->decision === null && $this->explained_at === null && ($today ?? CarbonImmutable::today())->lte($this->explain_by);
    }

    /** Due process done: they explained, or the days to explain have passed. */
    public function readyToDecide(?CarbonImmutable $today = null): bool
    {
        return $this->decision === null && ($this->explained_at !== null || ($today ?? CarbonImmutable::today())->gt($this->explain_by));
    }

    /**
     * The most a payslip may take for this (DOLE: 20% of a week's wages), from their current
     * daily rate; null when no rate is set yet.
     */
    public static function maxInstallmentFor(User $employee): ?float
    {
        $profile = $employee->loadMissing('employeeProfile')->employeeProfile;
        $rate = $profile === null ? null : EmployeeRate::query()->where('employee_profile_id', $profile->id)
            ->whereDate('effective_from', '<=', CarbonImmutable::today()->toDateString())
            ->orderByDesc('effective_from')->orderByDesc('id')->value('daily_rate');

        return $rate === null ? null : round((float) $rate * self::DAYS_PER_WEEK * self::WEEKLY_WAGE_SHARE, 2);
    }

    /**
     * The cases this viewer sees: of the people they issue to, and of the people they head.
     *
     * @param  Builder<EquipmentIncident>  $query
     */
    public function scopeVisibleTo(Builder $query, User $viewer): void
    {
        $query->whereHas('issue.user', fn (Builder $users) => $users->where(fn (Builder $who) => $who
            ->where(fn (Builder $handled) => EquipmentIssue::constrainPeopleHandledBy($handled, $viewer))
            ->orWhere(fn (Builder $office) => Heads::constrainOfficeStaffHeadedBy($office, $viewer))));
    }

    /**
     * @param  Builder<EquipmentIncident>  $query
     */
    public function scopeOpen(Builder $query): void
    {
        $query->whereNull('decision');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<EquipmentIssue, $this>
     */
    public function issue(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(EquipmentIssue::class, 'equipment_issue_id');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function reporter(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'reported_by');
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<User, $this>
     */
    public function decider(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'decided_by');
    }
}

  2. As opshq@example.test: Issue equipment → a guard → the polo, size L, ₱150 per payslip. As that guard: My Equipment shows the authority to deduct and "I received it".
  3. Back as Operation HQ: report a flashlight damaged. The Decide button waits until the guard explains or 5 days pass.
39

Patterns & lessons

The decisions that keep coming back, and the mistakes made along the way, so the next feature starts from them instead of relearning them. Each pattern names where it lives in the code.

Patterns to reuse

Suggest, then a person decidesWhen money depends on judgment, the app suggests and Accounting accepts or dismisses with a reason. It never adds pay silently. Examples: corrections from earlier cut-offs (DetectPriorPeriodCorrections), paid leave (DetectPaidLeave), reliefs to claim. The suggestion holds the payslip until decided, is idempotent (one row per source and run), and is never re-suggested once decided.
No deduction without a basisLabor Code Art. 113: the employee's written authorization (ticked in the app, or a signed paper) or the law (SSS/Pag-IBIG loans). The exact sentence is saved with the time. Used by loans (DeductionAuthorizationBasis), Borrow Load and the resignation's final-pay consent. Without a basis, nothing is taken; the debt is shown instead.
Acknowledge briefly, keep the wordsOnly forms that commit someone to something get an acknowledgement: resignation, complaint, reimbursement, Borrow Load and loans. Routine requests waive nothing and get none; more checkboxes teach people to tick unread. It's 3–7 plain sentences and a required tick, saved word for word with the time, in English or Filipino (lang/*/acknowledgements.php, partials.acknowledgement, partials.acknowledged).
Policy numbers belong to the people who own themCaps and day limits are company policy, so the owner sets them in the app, not a developer in .env. They're stored in the settings table, written only through an audited Action, and read through one helper with starting values in config (Reimbursement::limits() by Accounting, LeaveRules by HR). Forms read the same helper, so their text can't drift from the rule. Only infrastructure (disks, keys) stays in env.
Link records, one standing per sourceWhen one record follows from another, keep a link both ways and allow one standing child, enforced under a row lock. Examples: a relief and its fare claim (absence_notice_id), a just-cause resignation and its complaint (resignation_id). The page then shows the child's status where people look.
Confidential by designSensitive papers (medical, VAWC) are private files opened only by the employee and whoever decides, and every other view is audited (LeaveRequest::documentsVisibleTo). VAWC skips the endorsers, is hidden from other lists, and emails say only "Confidential leave". Decide who must not see something before building the screen.
Close things, don't delete themA state that ended badly is still a fact: "Not covered", "Dismissed: reason", "You didn't agree", "Withdrawn". Records stay for the audit and the client. A daily command moves stale states on (app:close-uncovered-absences), so lists stay clean.
Speak to the readerThe same fact reads differently to each person: "Authorized by them in the app" (Accounting) versus "You authorized it in the app" (the employee); "Serious insult on my honor" on the employee's form versus "on their honor" for HR. Give the enum one label per audience (labelForEmployee, labelForOthers).
Don't store what a value already saysThe province of birth is in the employee number's letters, so it's read from there (EmployeeNumber::provinceCode()), not saved again in a column that could disagree. The dropdown is just a way to fill in the letters. Likewise "expired" is computed from expires_on.
Invite proof, don't demand itWhen a requirement would block the people a feature exists for, offer it instead: an optional upload, a "who saw it" field, and a way for the handler to ask later. Complaints work this way; leave documents block approval only because the law ties those leaves to a document.
One list, narrowed by tabsWhen two kinds of people share a page, keep one search and add tabs with counts, not two search boxes. The list and its counts come from one base query, so they always agree, and the gate decides who gets the tabs at all (Employees, Leave and Overtime Requests: view-office-staff).

Lessons from mistakes

What happenedThe lesson
₱20,000 appeared as a reimbursement cap; when asked, it turned out the developer had picked it, not the law or OSSI.Say when a default is your own suggestion, and let the owner set it in the app.
A regex replace once emptied PHP files; a later one was used again to add imports.Never edit PHP source with regex replacement. Use exact string replacement or the editor, count the matches, and syntax-check (php -l) after.
A PowerShell script failed to parse because Blade text contained curly quotes (“ ”), which PowerShell treats as string quotes.Edit text with typographic quotes through the editor, not inline shell strings. A half-run script can leave changes half-applied, so check what landed.
Paying leave to someone with no attendance was blocked twice: by "no attendance, nothing to pay" in generation and in adjustments.A rule like "who's due a payslip" must live in one place (User::scopeDueAPayslip), or each copy has to be found and changed.
Approve stayed enabled for leave without its certificate in an early design.Block it in the Action (the rule), and show it on the button (disabledReason) with the same text.
Two staff could claim the same relief's fare at once."Only one" needs a row lock around the check, not just a check.
Twice a button vanished on hover in dark mode: "Choose file", then Clock In. It had dark:bg-white but only the light hover:bg-gray-800, under dark text.Every hover needs its dark twin: if a class sets dark:bg-…, also set dark:hover:bg-…. Better, use x-ui.button, whose variants already do. Check the hover in dark mode, not just the resting state.
A third time: the "Common hours" chips on the shift picker turned white on hover in dark mode. Their classes sat in an Alpine x-bind:class string, and the rule "every dark:bg needs a dark:hover" was written down but no test checked it.A rule that only lives in a document gets broken. DarkModeColorsTest now fails on any light hover background (hover:bg-white, -50, -100, -200) without a dark:hover:bg-…, in class="…" and in class-only strings. It found 12 more on its first run.
The Equipment menu reads new tables. That code was saved several minutes before the pilot was migrated, so the pilot's pages could fail in between: the Radios slip again.With a new table, migrate the pilot first (backup, then pilot-artisan.ps1 migrate --force), then save code that reads it. Or write the migration and code together, and migrate before the first test run.
Every error page said "Go to the dashboard", but guards have no dashboard and a visitor may be signed out.A button's label must be true for everyone who sees it. Point it at a route that decides (/home: sign-in, My Attendance or the Dashboard) and name it neutrally. An error page can't reliably check who's signed in: a 404 often never starts the session.
The 500 and 503 pages were missing, so a server error or an update showed Laravel's default page; the others were bare text with a blue number.List every status a user can hit (401, 403, 404, 419, 429, 500, 503) and give each the app's look, a way forward and a reason, using no session or database. A 500 page shows the time for IT, never the error.
The dashboard looked fine for HR (3 numbers) but squeezed for the Super Admin (11 in one row, every label "Peop…", "None yet" wrapping onto two lines).Check a layout with the most data a role can have, not the usual. Wrap past a column count instead of shrinking forever, and give text values their own size so a row still lines up.
Twenty actions changed something about a person without telling them: a guard moved to another post, a duty removed, attendance entered for them by hand, a new daily rate, a training moved.Audit by the rule "is someone other than the actor affected?". Every Action that answers yes notifies that person. Plain updates share one class, UpdateNotice::tell(), which skips the actor and anyone no longer working here, so adding the next one is one line. The map by role is docs/features/33-notifications.md.
A 500 from a click (a Livewire request) showed the error page in Livewire's pop-up window over the half-hidden page, not full screen like a 500 from a page load.resources/js/error-pages.js hooks Livewire.interceptRequest → onError: it calls preventDefault() and writes the returned error page over the whole document, so every error looks the same however it happened.
A rename ("Retired" → "Disposed") broke the pilot's Radios page for a few minutes: the code was live before the pilot's migration ran.The pilot serves this folder live; there is no deploy step in between. A change that needs a migration is migrated on dev and the pilot in the same step (after a backup), or the code accepts the old and new values until it is.
The first pilot start served a PHP fatal error ("index.php not found"), and its logs read like "s p a c e d o u t" text.Laravel's router script must start from public\, as artisan serve does; Windows PowerShell 5's >> writes UTF-16, so send native output through cmd. Test the real public address end to end (styles, a login, an error page), not just "it answers 200".
Pointing a public tunnel at the dev server for a quick test exposed the demo accounts and debug mode.Anything reachable from the internet runs in production mode on its own data. Stop a public dev server as soon as the test is done.
An old migration was broken by a stray keystroke (-nullable>()). The running app was fine, but every test and any fresh deploy would have failed.Run static analysis over the whole project, not just the changed files: it caught this. A broken file that isn't yours: say so and ask before fixing it.
A comment in config/privacy.php said a test protected the "acknowledge, never consent" wording; the test file had never been written.A comment that names a test is a promise: check the file exists. When adding a guard test, also break the thing on purpose once and see it fail.
A "random pick, 100 tries" generator would almost never find the last free number, and a test written for it would have been skipped as "slow".When a test is awkward, check the design first: picking at random from the free values always works while any is left. Livewire 4's wire:model.blur also no longer sends a request on its own; use .live.blur when the server must react.
One word, "Executive", was both a role and a position (now President and Vice President), and the Board was drawn from the role, so nobody could tell what a director, the President and an approver each were.Keep access (roles), jobs (positions) and governance (a Board seat) as separate fields. A word used for two things in the data confuses the people reading the screens.
The dashboard hid office staff from Operations, but the Employees list still showed them.A visibility rule belongs on every list of the same people. When you add one, search for the other screens that list them (view-office-staff).
Sick leave couldn't be filed after the fact because the form refused past dates.Ask how people really do it (sick first, file once back) before writing a date rule.
